Planet Explorer's is a good game, much better than other Early Access Titles - I know I'm kinda against those but I took a risk one more time with Planet Explorer's and boy did it ever pay off.
Pros:
+ The Creation System allows for a wide-range of creativity You can ride and create vehicles (air, land, sea, submerisible), swords, guns, armors, bows, and some other objects with the Voxel Creation System. In addition to the creation system there is a "Standard" Selection of items you can make or buy if you have the resources. Unfortunately Vehicles are custom jobs only but you can d/l some from the budding library of multiplayer workshop items.
+ The Game has really great detail of graphics.
+ Those who follow my activity thinking know I concentrate on 2 things when it comes to games, Tools, and Crafting, this game has a stellar crafting system in SP and MP it has that potentional but - more on that in the cons section.
+ The Game has a definite level of challenge that will make it not overly difficult but certainly not too easy to found and run your own colony.
+ 1st and 3rd Person Perspective (Switch with f5)
+ The Technology range is massive - For future explorer's you can make some pretty primitive and very advanced stuff.
+ Multiplayer is working now.
+ Patches are MASSIVE - in terms of additional content per patch.
+ The "Skill Tree" - is completely optional at the maps outset. Don't Like to be limited? Just find/create a map that doesn't have it enabled.
Cons:
- Naturally there's bugs, but hey it's still in Alpha Stage so that's pretty normal. I can see strides being made with the previous patches (which I wasn't around for but got the benefit of) and I wonder where it will lead.
- Patches are rather slow, in timing.
- Skill Tree doesn't progress very fast. (Which is OK since it's optional)
Finally I saved the most "neutral" thing and imo the "best" thing about the game for last.
+/- The Game is unfinished, and from all accounts the devs listen to those who are playing the alpha when they speak.  Unfinished doesn't refer to a lack of quality, but the presence of potential. As you all know potential is very hard to find in games that force you to do it "their way", I see at this stage atleast the ability to make a great game, but it's not quite finished yet. I was going to reserve judgement until after it made Beta Stage but I decided to review it anyway to let you know this might be a great investment, and pretty low risk if you like the idea of creating your own objectives/world/objects/stuff.
1/6/2016 - Updated Review to reflect the resolved Multiplayer Issues.

Easily one of the best team combat games I've ever played.  This game's single player takes the free campaigns from Star Wars Battlefront II to a whole new level, the combat as well.  This game is so unique and so amazingly open and one in which you can set your own limits and really rewards you the higher you go.  The difficulty is so customizable that any level of player would be able to enjoy this game for a long time
Now, the mods.  The mods are where this game truly shines.  Not to say that the vanilla game isn't amazing, but the mods can take this game, a diamond in the rough that really shows the limitations of it not being a big-name developer, and makes it shine.  The mods act like sequels, adding features and new locations and new items, new units and new quests, new characters, and new worlds even.  The mods for this game are as amazing in Mount & Blade as they are in the major Paradox-developed games.
The game is very easy to get into and very easy, as I said before, to build up the difficulty to your personal taste.  The game also allows you to choose different routes.  You could choose to be an honorable and chivalrous lord, helping the peasants and cleansing the crime-ridden realm like an exterminator to rats.  You could choose to be a bandit leader, slaughtering the innocent and burning their homes taking for yourself their valuables.  You could choose to be a trader, leading a caravan from town to town, maneuvering through mine fields of banditry and hostility.  You could be a mercenary captain, a king, the options really are diverse.
The versatility and the lack of structure gives this game an extreme level of replayability.  I've been playing this game regularly on and off since the release of the first Mount and Blade back in 2008.  I fell in love the day I discovered it and that love has done nothing but grow.
I haven't played too much multiplayer due to constraints on my end but from what I've had of it it is fun and very challenging.  There are some very good players out there, taking you from slaughterer in the single player to swine in the multiplayer.  I think that could go for most any game though.
Over all, this game is an 8.5/10 for me, 10/10 with mods.  I'm a pretty strict grader too I like to think.  If you liked Star Wars Battlefront, I would absolutely recommend this game.  Even if you didn't, it is still worth a shot.  Warband polishes up and adds a lot of features to the old Mount & blade and also has a much stronger mod community due to cumulation over time.  If you're going to spend your money on mount & blade, go with Warband.  They recently ported the TLD (Lord of the RIngs) mod to Warband, making the original kind of pointless.
Sufficed to say, I am looking forward to the Banner Lords sequel.

It feels like Warhammer Fantasy. Everything about it feels gratifying, visceral, immediate, brutal. Where so many would have used Warhammer as a skin, resulting in the setting feeling shallow, Fatshark took the rat ogre by the eyes and made the theme an integral part of the game, without requiring a sliver of Warhammer Fantasy knowledge or background. The combat is weighty, varied, and lives and breathes Warhammer. The map design is sprawling and clustered, claustrophobic, and expansive, full of life but utterly desolate. From the artstyle you can see the concept art; they are one in the same, the drawing made tangible. The animation quality is superb, from the groestque Skaven, to the hulking rat ogres, nothing feels stock. Sound assets are high quality, and exist wholely within the world, not a single gutteral death out of place.
The game is not perfect. It is marred by bugs, and some wonky optimisation. But if you can play this, you should play this. It is love for it's craft incarnate, and Warhammer Fantasy brought to grim, miserable, stricken life.
It's like Left4dead and skyrim had a love child, and it grew up to be a 10.

Deadlight represents a little bit of a coup for me, in that I have not played a classical 2D platformer in a VERY long time, and there is a really good reason for that - They generally make me want to go super saiyan 2 and annihilate a small country community. But I thought, "Why not? It's been a good ten years between drinks, let's see how things have progressed." Part of me hopes that Deadfall doesn't represent the best that 2D platformers have to offer, because to be brutally honest, Donkey Kong Country had 97 times the gameplay and there were more colours on the SNES controller than there are in Deadfall. The leaping and rolling gave me flashbacks TO THE ORIGINAL Prince of Persia, and unfortunately didn't work as well. Coming to think of it, if you rendered Prince of Persia and took out all the awesome sword fighting, traps, and hidden secrets, then shaved like.... 37hrs of gameplay and a metric ♥♥♥♥tonne of difficulty off it, you'd be in the ballpark of where Deadfall sits.
Here's where Deadfall had wins for me: I didn't feel like an octopus with cerebral palsy trying to finish it. The art in the cutscenes was screenshot-worthy. And there were some cool (albiet underused) slow motion moments where I became the king of parkour.
Here's where Deadfall faceplanted in the loose gravel of disapointment: It's horrendously short for a platformer, and just as easy to finish (the masichist in me likes the feel of the ocean occasionally). The protagonist is all kinds of ♥♥♥♥ed up, as illustrated by his diary and....um....halucinations? The slingshot is ridiculous and shouldn't have been included in the game - there's not shortage of ammo, and the guy is a ♥♥♥♥ing Mounty/MMA fighter/parkour ragamuffin from the streets. What does he need a ♥♥♥♥ing slingshot for? Shotgun and revolver would have been just fine thanks, and I think I only used my shotgun once because I was afraid there'd be no ammo and might need it in the next 20hrs of gameplay that never came, or to fight the nonexistential bosses that I assumed would eventually appear.
The story wasn't even original. Or good. And I've seen better endings in YouTube videos of people eating sandwiches.

I have gotten way more gameplay out of this game in its alpha phase than I have in many other finished games.  The worlds here can be massive, the creation options are only limited by ones imagination, and the potential for further game development is endless.  The devs are active, updates are steady and useful, and there's already a ton of user content available.  The coming addition of the world editor adds further customization options.  It's all pretty exciting... hitching a ride in the development process is groovy.  This game and Prison Architect have generated a ton of goodwill from me directed towards Early Access.
Highlights for me so far include:
- Exploring certain luminous areas at night.  The flora and night sky can be striking.
- Building a massive base in a cave system
- Learning to use the jetpack... and sometimes going SPLAT
- Building some crazy/interesting/useful community ISO items, like a VW bus, great weapons, and the Millennium Falcon
- Running into the Giant Robot once or twice and getting absolutely (and humorously) destroyed
Now, I would say that this sort of gameplay has to be your thing... not everyone is going to dig it.  Mining and gathering can get a little tedious.  Harvesting plants is sometimes a large pain.  And like any alpha, there are some bugs (though I've not had any real problems), and things are going to need to be fixed as development continues.  But the potential... stacked on to what's already here... is, again, pretty exciting.
If you like rpgs, sandboxing, exploration, creation and all that jazz, this game could be a great fit.   And there's still much, much more to be added to the game, so the potential is limitless.  I can't wait to see where the game goes in the future.  I hope to be playing it for years.

I also love the simple design! Neutral background and character makes it so you can focus easily on the keys and not be distracted by the background, I even tried the other pink background and my eyes couldn't take it. Even the pink character made me immediately change it back to the default.
Now unlike Osu! the songs arn't player made and then checked by admins to see if they're playable or even follow the beat. I do acknowledge the fact that sometimes the orbs/slides don't match the beat but it was done through the program so Im not going to complain, being able to play songs that I love and that arn't available on Osu! cause they arn't made yet is pretty awesome. Sometimes it throws me off but practice makes perfect and you can separate the beat from what you see. Muscle memory kicks in and helps you through it.
A few kinks here and there but ultimately a good game with a good future if it's taken care of by good hands, I hope to see this game develop further in the future.
If I had to rate I would give it an 8.5/10 because it's a really good game but some kinks in it(mentioned above) will throw off the rhythm loving crowd. And because when I end up failing in it in any part I don't rage, instead it makes me laugh and enjoy the game more.

Heroes & Generals is a free game, and therefore I was not expecting a great product. However, I gave it a go, and really enjoyed it.
The graphics are good (reminds me of the quality/style of "Day of Defeat"), the ambience is well done, and the gameplay is fun.
It is set during World War Two; you can choose to be an American, German, or Russian. You can ride in a jeep (either as the driver, one of several passengers, or the gunner), take a bike (or ride pillion), or go on foot. There are rifles, RPGs, handgrenades, and a bunch of other weapons you can get as you go up in rank.
Anyone can buy extra weapons through ranking up, or you can pay actual money to get those weapons more quickly (whilst that makes the game a little bit "pay to win" in style, the fact is that non-payers can rank up to those weapons; also, we should cut the developers some slack in that regard as they do need to get some money to live on).
In the game you win points by eliminating enemy soldiers and by capturing bases. It reminds me a bit of "Battlefield 1942" and the WW2 "Call of Duty" games, albeit with a "Day of Defeat" graphic style.
To sum up, it may not be the most brilliant game in the world, but it can be a lot of fun to play, especially if you are teaming up with friends. And it's free, so that's a good bonus. If you are looking for a bit of simple and fun WW2 gameplay, then I recommend giving "Heroes & Generals" a try.
P.S. I have found the waiting times for this game to be terrible, and the game's estimation of how long you will have to wait to join a game usually have no link to reality.

Deadlight is an entertaining but short game; I completed in under 4.5 hours in one sitting. I recommend getting it but only when it's on sale and you can grab it for a couple of dollars. It's a 2D sidescroller consisting of a mix of platforming, puzzle solving and a bit of combat. It's not mindblowing or life changing, but is fun to finish in an afternoon.
Pros:
- Interesting story, if a little cliche (you will probably see the ending coming a mile away).
- Gameplay is mostly enjoyable, despite a few control issues listed below.
- Voice acting is good. I didn't find the dialogue cringeworthy or over the top, although I note some other reviewers have.
Cons:
- The game is short to very short, depending on how fast you solve the puzzles. This may annoy some (although I felt it was a good length for the type of game it is).
- The controls can be sticky and unresponsive at times, leading to some unfair deaths.
- A few moments may have you stuck for a while, being unsure of where to go or what to do to progress.
- Game was laggy for me at the standard resolution, despite my fairly powerful computer. The recommended specs are useless and cannot be relied upon. I adjusted it based on the advice of others online to 1024x768 and it played perfectly fine, but obviously did not look as good.

I want to like this game. I really do. I enjoy it for the cocaine-like stimulation of fast paced run and gun, knowing maps well enough to use tactical positioning to outwit your opponents and memorize gameplay patterns, etc. I basically want to turn off my brain and use muscle memory and let all the endorphins in my skull release at once. And you'll get a bit of that. But you'll die often if you play that way, and that gets annoying--and for two major flaws with the game that ended up being a dealbreaker for me.
CONS:
The maps. Camping is the best way to succeed at this game, and that's what most people do. Maybe because the levels are too big, maybe because they are too open or are missing some magic rule of thirds--the fact remains that they are poorly designed for run and gun style gameplay and trying to play that way you will die often and it will be frustrating. Whereas camping is also annoying because most of what you're doing is waiting. Your best chance is really to stay in a high traffic area with a lot of corners and watch your map like a hawk, relying on direct combat--but that is even more frustrating than the levels.
Lag. Oh my god, the lag. I've heard a few theories. That the Ghosts multiplayer server is based in Russia, and slow, or that people hack the game and force you to lag out when near, I honestly have no idea. But I would say a conservative of estimate is that a third of my deaths are utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. "I should've killed that guy" is a phrase you'll come to know well, whether from little things like putting a couple extra bullets into someone and them then turning and killing you in a single shot, or to big things like the game stalling and your opponent magically jumping from ten feet away to right in front of you and knifing you. Maybe 1/15 (trying to be realistic) games you play will drop from bad connection. At least 1/5 have major hiccups, shaking your around the map or having to connect to a new host, and almost every game will have some noticeable connection issue...unfortunately usually the ones that leave you saying "wtf i should not be dead right now."
Also dogs. God I hate the dogs in this game. They take three times as much damage to kill and will leap from fifteen feet away and you will die when they are five feet away in midair. Basically if you see one and don't have a shotgun and time to volley out four shots you are dead. But I digress.
Lastly I mean I might as well mention it but the campaign is just utterly stupid. All holds barred I haven't actually finished it or even really made it past maybe the fifth chapter or whatever. But the way it plays I feel like I am at Dave and Busters playing House of the Dead or one of those foot pedal games where you have to save the president's daughter or whatever. They really make an effort to make the cinematic moments epic... buildings falling in front of you, giant explosions in space, etc. but the gameplay is mind numbingly stupid.
Last gripe are all the microtransactions and high premium for DLC they expect you to pay, while offering very little cool features and customization in game. It just feels blatantly skeevy and disappointing, but I guess when no one plays this game except the 25 kids who play it 24/7 and dominate each game, it makes sense to try and suck as much money out of it as possible. Maybe the DLC maps are better, but the hell I'm going to pay the price of most other games for each of them just to find out.
PROS:
The most fun I have playing this game is running around with the Bulldog and on some of the smaller levels like Strikezone, Fog, or Tremor. That gun is fun as hell, maybe a little OP but I guess compensates for the lag sometimes.
With graphics turned all the way up the game is admittedly beautiful. I am sort of hesitant to give CoD 4 (which rumor has it is still the best CoD game) a try just because it's not as pretty.
Besides that yeah I will probably uninstall very soon.

-Review for release version-
First off, I have no idea why this is getting so many negative reviews.  This game is hands down one of my favorite video games *ever*, and not without reason.  I'll split this review into three sections:
Co-op is IMO, one of the weaker aspects of the game, but even then manages to be pretty good, if co-op is your thing.  Extraction is my favorite of the two team modes, where you must find survivors hiding in their homes, defend them from zombies, and get them to the edge of the quarantine zone.  The sheer number of zombies pressing in on whatever stronghold you happen to be in is enough to cause panic at the worst of times.  Add the zombies ability to climb into the mix, and often you'll watch a friend as a hungry mouth stretches through a window to bite him.
The NPC survivors are admittedly not the brightest, but it's nothing game breaking.
I know that Contagion is primarily marketed as a co-op game.  Do yourself a favor, and play the pvp.  It's the best.  Playing with friends makes it better than the best, weather you team up and destroy the opposition, or just save a bullet for them.  The gamemode is last man standing, with players scavenging for weapons and ammo while hunting each other and avoiding the undead.
This mode is a beautiful mix of stealth and combat, chasing and hiding.  Each weapon has it's own niche, and even the weaker ones are often so cool that you can't help but use them.  You are forced to make choices on the fly as you hunt your prey, but do your best not to be trapped by the roving hordes.  Any gunshot alerts the dead to your location, and players can easily deduce it too by watching the movement patterns of the horde.
Headshots are always an instant kill, with the exception of the sig, which is an instant kill 90% of the time.  Choosing between spraying with your assault rifle or taking a careful shot with a crossbow to avoid making noise is the lifeblood of this game.
I struggled not to mention most of this stuff throughout the rest of this review, as it factors into everything else.  Too make it short and to the point:
Melee- Simply amazing.  Swings take chunks out of zombies and snap their bodies in the direction of your blow.  Make sure to aim for the head.  Against players, one hit is usually enough to down them, but it's difficult to get in close.
Gunplay- Each gun has a perfect feel and balance based on it's type.  Admittedly, in the beginning I thought the hit detection was off, but then I realised the the recoil has more of an effect than I realised.  Taking your time for that perfect shot is super-satisfying.  Again, zombies lose chunks of flesh, skull, and brains as you shoot them.  You can even blast their legs off.
Explosives-  Deserves a seperate section, despite having only two tools, the grenade and the IED.  Both are VERY powerful, in a good way.  If you aren't careful, you'll end up killing yourself.  Zombies caught in the blast will often lose their legs but survive, so watch for crawlers.
Gore-  As mentioned multiple times before now, the gore is exactly what a zombie game should have.  Skulls break, arms are chopped off, legs get blown into nothing.  As of the latest update you can even decapitate zombies.
Rating- 8/10, only critisims are that the game needs more maps, and slightly better co-op.  You will not regret buying this game.

This game is a timekiller. Not more not less. The level-grinding in this game is quite enormous and takes a lot of time - which doesn't have to be a bad thing. I have enjoyed it so far though.
+ Immersion. I love the immersion in this game. Maps just have the right sizes, espescially in skirmishes! Troops look quite authentic, and so do the tank models. The weapon variation isn't too wide, which makes you feel more involved in a unit.
+ You can see your feet. Not a lot of games can say that.
+ Balancing. I'd definitely say this game is balanced (in most parts)! Despite what others say on how OP the russian tanks are, I can't agree. If you're running around when a tank is nearby, then it really is your own fault for getting shot.
+ "Classes". You have to unlock them, and they aren't really "classes". You unlock stuff with every level, so you always have rewards to look forward to.
- Make gold earnable without having to spend real cash. Long-term players need to be more rewarded.
- You can't really leave a match. You can quit out, yes, but as long as the game is not over, you can't pick a new one.
- Graphics. Too be honest, they aren't that bad, but definitely improvable.
- The Russian Weaponry. Russian Rifles really are OP. Hate them or love them. I'm not saying the whole russian army is imbalanced, but the Rifles definitely are.
- No real squad-system. You may find yourself in the same "brigade" as other players, but you still can't spawn by them or be in a seperate squad-chat.
- Spawning System. You can only spawn by your spawnpoint (in skirmishes; in assault you can spawn by every captured point). If you're in a squad, you should be able to spawn by them.
All in all I'd say that this game has some stuff to improve, but it is on a good way. I would definitely recommend this game to whoever likes WW2 games.

There are many things right or wrong with this simple open world survival game.
Some good things.
Exploration and otherwise the construction of making the nice home for ether yourself or a village.
Crafting is fine, items are not that hard to come by because there is a shop in a town that restocks them over night.
The diversity and blending of multiple climate landscape make you feel if you have walked more than just kilometers.
Some bad things.
The part about items are easy to find is forshadowed for a fact natrual metal resources are hard to find to make those items. Many item recipes require a rare metal recource to craft, otherwise the crafted item in question can just be sold in the NPC town shop.
Combat is questionable.
Sword and shield is not really a combat option, in fact it is not a perfered option. The gun is where it's at.
Enemy difficulty is rediculous, depending on creature. Some are aggrive, some are passive, some are huge. The worst part are that the alien inhabitants kill on sight,  and they are usially the hardest besides the fact thier little colonies are amost impossible to defeat alone. Kiting seems to be the only option to win.
Building and Governing towns.
Feature that is locked unless you compete a few quests in ether adventure or story mode. But NPC are known to be killable in not revived in time, even though there is no real way to get more NPC fallowers.
Creation and Crafting.
So complex and uniformitive that sometimes I wonder how someone is able to make a car, a car that turns out is not that good and not repairable.
All creations are made as a blueprint and then they are placed in the world only if you have the required resources to place item in world. You make your creation in the creation editor and then save creation as a blueprint for item placement in game.
The creation editor is not user friendly at all. It requires more than a slideshow tier manual.
Open world Placement of object finds yourself unable to rotate such object for placement, or the fact the game does not tell your how though the keybinding in the options menu.
The Ugly
Multiplayer is dead when the populated servers up to 16 people has only four people in it. This is an open world cooperative game if most if the overall metagame features like town creation and alien coloney raiding requires a group to complete. That is if latency of over 250-300 ping is good for you.
Updates are not automated in Steam. Servers also have to update manualy.
There are much better indie games with much logical purchase prices. I got it half off on sale of what is considered $30.

I love the “neon violence” genre so I came into this game already loving it. I'd like for my friends to enjoy this as much as I have, but if twitch based “rage difficulty” turns you off, you're not going to have fun.
It's very different from the first. Instead of one character with many masks and abilities, you play as many different characters who disappointingly similar. Your base skills are going to be instant kill punches, spawn with gun, and roll dodges.
It plays very quickly. You're dead in one hit, but so are your enemies and restarting levels is instant. On map start, some bad guys remain stationary until they see you, while others roam around. The roaming is random so it's not going to play the same after each death. Often I feel a feeling of false difficulty because maps have many wide open spaces so much of the game is spent dying to enemies barely on screen, or who roam around that you couldn't keep track of.
You can't be as aggressive and fast as Hotline Miami 1.
One vital character you play as does not use guns so you must "bait” the projectile enemies into coming to you. Normally you can blast your gun to get bad guys to run over and confront the commotion, but since this character cannot use guns, or in later stages when ammo is out or you don't have a gun currently (hard mode especially) you must get into and out of their line of sight, peeking around a corner, or barely entering and leaving a room, to get them to run over so you can melee them without being shot. I find I have to do this enough that it is annoying.
The story is wonderfully convoluted, but this is a video game and not a movie. Gameplay is very difficult but can be very fun if you're into bullet hell and/or reaction based aiming. For a “pixel block” art style, it's very bloody, violent, and often barbaric.
I love it.

People who don't like this game say 2 things I do not agree with: the gameplay is more gun oriented and the stage design is bad.
I'll give you some good reasons why I think differently:
THE GAME IS MORE GUN ORIENTED IS FALSE BECAUSE:
-From The Fans you can pick: Corey, Tony (melee, no weapons), Mark and Alex and Ash (a playable couple that's basically melee oriented). So, out of 4 characters, you can pick 2 melee oriented characters (Alex and Ash are virtually one character).
-Jake can wear three snake masks, one of them won't let you pick any weapon and it's melee oriented.
-The Journalist is a totally melee oriented character.
-The Son has one "technique" that will act almost the same as Tony and also there's another "technique" that equips him with a nice katana you don't want to get rid off.
-The soldier has two modes, knife or firearm (and you will definitely use the knife quite a lot).
-The detective can do everything.
-Ritcher can do everything, however his levels require a nice combination of melee and firearm strategy.
-Mafia member can do everything.
Besides all that, there's a new type of enemy that will only die when using melee weapons against him.
THE LEVEL DESIGN CAN'T BE BAD BECAUSE: the stages are more challenging than in the previous game since they require more time to get the right strategy to beat the level. They are also usually larger in space or number of floors and they all look gorgeous and different to each other.

Do you enjoy killing people? Do you enjoy a bit of challenge. Do you consider yourself a masochist? Then get ready to press R for reset! Cause here comes Hotline Miami 2!
This game is just plain out amazing. It's satisfying to kill enemies, racking up combos, and frustratingly easy to get killed. When I think about Hotline Miami, I think about how easy it is to get killed. And that is a good thing, cause this isn't a Run and Gun game. This game is all about being strategic, planning ahead, getting a good idea of what is waiting for you. Otherwise you are going to die a lot until you learn from your mistakes and get better.
The story continues off where Hotline Miami 1 left off. The main character (who is refereed to as Jacket according to Payday 2) now lives in infamy for taking on the Russian mafia. Thus introduces the cast of characters: a group of people trying to impersonate Jacket to earn some fame, a crooked detective that takes care of cases his own way, and an author researching about the Chicken Masked man, and a group of soldiers in Hawaii... huh... and a few other characters.
So instead of many different masks you instead get to play as many different characters who have their own way of killing people. My personal favorite is Ash and Alex who are pretty much two characters in one, one kills people with a chainsaw, the other shoots. The levels are also large and expansive which can be bad since there is sometimes not a lot of cover, so you'll get shot pretty easily, especially if your playing as Tony one of the masked bandits that can only melee enemies. Sometimes you'll need to be on your toes in case the next area has a guy not to far from where you came from. Like I said before your not going to get far from just rushing, you need to plan ahead and know where the enemies are at, and what you might attract if you start shooting. And once you get a good plan put together you'll be killing people without a scratch.
Also the music and the graphics are just fantastic!
Also on a extra note: when you start the game it will ask you if you want to skip and sexual content that is shown in the game, course if you were following the news you'll know what to expect. And as far as I know there is only one instance of any sexual content.
In conclusion Hotline Miami 2 has its flaws. Sometimes you'll breeze through a level, other times you'll get shot by a guy you didn't see or didn't expect, but in the end you'll be satisfied as you walk back to your car passing by all the dead bodies of every single person you have single handedly killed.
Final Rating: Bloody Amazing!

As a huge fan of the original, (Who spent 52 hours in game) it pains me to see the sequel come up so short. Whereas I thought Hotline Miami 1 was the video game equivalent of "Natural Born Killers," Hotline Miami 2 is more of the video game equivalent of "Pulp Fiction." Yeah that's right I just compared THIS game to "Pulp Fiction!" Come at me!
Hotline Miami 2 is both a prequel, sequel, and midquel to the first game. It has a story that is told out of order, like I said, similar to "Pulp Fiction," and the dates go in between taking place before, during, and after the first game. This game goes further into the lore that the first game set up, which I won't dare spoil for you if you haven't played it.
The gameplay, for the most part, is just like the first game, with the exception of some characters having special abilities, like one being able to use a dodging move to dodge bullets, and another being able to let you control two characters at once (And it's actually not as chaotic as you'd think). Some people have been complaining about the level design and the placement of enemies compared to the first one, and I'm not gonna lie I can kind of see it annoying some people. But I saw the design of the levels and placement of enemies as a way to really ramp up the difficulty compared to the first game, which was already rage-inducingly hard to begin with. My first time playing I did feel like I was dying more than I should, but I played it again, almost as soon as I finished the game, and I'm really not dying as much, and half the deaths I feel are me making a mistake and the other half I would say are some minor game mistakes that'll probably be fixed with a patch, and doesn't, at least for me, hinder my enjoyment of the game. Also playing with a controller really helps, I strongly recommend a gamepad instead of a keyboard.
In addition to the game playing like the first game they also included variety where they needed to. The hardest thing when making a sequel for anything, especially a video game, is keeping gameplay similar without it feeling like a rehash of the first game, and adding new features and variety without completely alienating the sequel from the original game. And Hotline Miami 2 manages to achieve this. Some of the more interesting types of levels are the ones that delve into the backstory of one of the side characters from the first game in which he fights in a Vietnam-esqe war where you can't pick up new weapons and you actually have reloadable ammo for the weapon you initially equip. Or the sections where you play as a character that can only use melee weapons, so NO GUNS!
And I don't usually talk about a game's soundtrack, even though it's a very important element in a game. But this sound track is even better than the first one, which was already amazing to begin with. It really helps intensify the, already super intense, atmosphere of the game. I highly recommend you take the option of buying the game coupled with its soundtrack, you won't regret it!
Back to the game's story, I actually have really mixed feelings about it. Overall I really liked it, and I'll get into why in a minute. But, as is a case with a lot of stories told out of order, it can be very confusing. It's the type of story where after you finish it, you may kind of pause and try and process, "Wait did I like this or not?" Then you decide to play it again and like a puzzle start to piece together some of the more confusing elements, especially if you end up looking hard enough, or just look them up online, and find secrets within the game, including one that unlocks a tough as nails bonus level which, as of this review I'm still trying to beat. The only other thing I have to complain about is that one specific character, the Pig Butcher, I really wanted to see more of. Dispite the trailers showcasing him as a big part of the plot, it's actually shocking how short his inclusion really is. It really disappointed me because, dispite him not having really any impact on the main plot as a whole, I found his story extremely intresting, kind of reminded me of "Black Swan" (God there I go comparing Hotline Miami to another movie, I really gotta stop that!).
Now for what I liked about the plot. It's actually really compelling. There were times where it actually had me questioning what I was doing. Dispite the game being one of the most violent and gory games I've ever played, it actually doesn't glorify the violence. And if you play the game you'll see what I mean, it has some very insightful lines about the various acts of violence and how it affects the characters in the game. The other thing I love is that it really has you questioning the reality of the game at times. There were times where I really didn't know what supposed to be real in the game and what was a hallucination of a deranged killer.
The game also has a planned level editor, but as of this review it hasn't been released yet, but the trailers have really made it look promising, and I'll probably do an update once they finally release it.
I personally thing Hotline Miami 2 is an amazing sequel, but do I think it's as good as the first game, I actually am not sure. I personally think I'll probably play the first one more than the second one, but I found the second one much more interesting both story and gameplay wise. Personally I feel if you thought the first game was difficult enough and that anymore difficulty just wouldn't be as fun, you might not get as much enjoyment from this game as I did. If you're brave enough to take on the extreme difficulty, and want to check out how they expanded on the lore of the first game while you're at it I'd say pick this up, hell get it at full price if you're so inclined. And I don't say that about any game. Now if you'll excuse me, I'm gonna go try and beat hard mode...Yes I'm clinically insane!

Some people don't like this game for who knows what reasons, so I'm going to do a quick rundown.
Yes, it is a zombie game. Like Left 4 Dead, just without pills being thrown at you. And tanks. Oh Lord, the tanks.
In the beginning, the title screen, for me, even that was ominous. The title music, the background, everything. Twas spooky.
The mechanics are kinda like CoD, with the crouching helps aim, and iron sighting, and the v to melee thing. Yes, we get it. It's like CoD.
The inventory system is very realistic. None of the characters have backpacks (at least I haven't noticed one), which means you can only carry 4 items. Preferrably, keys, melee, pistol, and rifle.
The zombies, seeing there is no special infected, range from slow as a wet week, to track runner zombies.
The players side is cool as well, seeing that you will need health as it goes on, and that once you die, you don't respawn. No resupply closets, nothing. Although you can become a zombie once you die, or if no player zombies are enabled, then you'll become a kawaii little insect. Naww, cute :D
All in all, Contagion is a good game. The corpses don't usually lag you out, and you can get blood and gore in it. What more could you want?

I was anxiously looking forward to Hotline MIami 2: Wrong Number over the months before it's release. Being a massive fan of the original, I thought this game was gonna blow the original out of the water. I even committed the worst PC gamer sin of all and broke my no pre-order rule. I think this has taught me that even your most trusted developers can make mistakes.
Now, onto the review: Hotline Miami 2 is by no means a
game. The soundtrack is excellent and heart-pumping and the neon visuals are hypnotizing to look at. The thing is, I can't recommend Hotline Miami 2 since the original Hotline Miami is much cheaper and better in a lot of ways. If you've already played Hotline Miami and are desperate for more, then sure, give this a try if you like what you see.
Now, the problem that a lot of reviewers have mentioned is what I'll start with first and give my opinions on. The level design.
I'm going to be honest, the level design in Hotline Miami 2 isn't very great. As opposed to quickly and widely bashing mobster's skulls in like the original, HM2 has a much larger focus on gunplay, and because of that very large open maps with little cover. This can very easily get annoying, as missions drag on for too long and you are forced to restart several minutes of gameplay because you got killed by an enemy from afar you couldn't even see. The worse examples of this have got to be the
missions. They're plain awful.
It's trial and error, but not in the challenging way like the original where you knew that every time you died it was always your fault. It can get frustrating.
That being said, not all of the levels are that frustrating, but very few come close to the fast-paced skull-crushing action of the original. The fast paced flow of the original is gone, replaced by accuracy-based, teeth grinding shooting.
The story is... just really
. The original Hotline Miami's story was weird, too, but it was mainly kept to the background. The general jist that you needed to know is that your character is on a drug-fueled psychopathic murder spree. The clues to the story are there, you just have to piece them together.
The story in this game, however, is much more in the foreground, which wouldn't be bad if the story wasn't
The biggest problem is the characters. There are just way too many of them. You practically play as every Miami citizen and their mother in this game. Characters are introduced and dropped after only a couple levels and I kid you not
Talk about bloated. The characters that have been advertised most, the Fans, barely get ANY game time.
To make things even more confusing, the plot jumps between different locations, characters, and years randomly, leaving you with no idea how it even fits into the plot. It's a mess, and to top it all off the ending is downright insulting, taking a hard left turn and leaving you with more questions than answers.
Speaking of characters, while the Fans distinct and unique playstyles should have livened up the game more, it just makes it harder.
Corey, the Zebra, has a dodge roll. Using it in a small room is suicide because you'll get caught on a piece of scenery and die. In larger rooms with melee enemies, though, it's pretty fun.
Tony, the Tiger (get it?), has killing punches, but the problem is that he can't pick up guns, and since so many of these levels are so big you'll end up getting shot before you can punch a dude, forcing you to play the good old corner peak-a-boo game.
Mark, the Bear, has two machine guns, which are useful until they (very quickly) run out of ammo, leaving you slow and vulnerable.
Alex and Ash, a brother and sister murdering duo, are by far the most fun characters to play. As you play Alex, slicing people with a chainsaw (which never stops being fun) you're followed by Ash, who you can use to cover you with guns. It works alright, but there were several times where Ash got stuck in a doorway, usually leading to your death. He's also a terrible shot, so don't rely on him to save your life.
The other characters play pretty much the same as a standard Jacket from the original, with the exception of a character I won't name due to spoilers, so there's not much to go into with them.
In short, the game isn't bad, but it was certainly disappointing, If you've never played Hotline Miami, pick up the first one for cheaper and I promise you'll have more fun as opposed to playing this one. If you're a Hotline Miami fan who's dying for more, then pick this one up, if only for the level creator that's supposed to be coming out soon.
Overall, Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is a brutal, gory, and punishing top down shooter that, while not living up to it's predecessor's charm and flow, stands up well enough on it's own merits.

Whereas the first one was a lot of twitch melee action, 2 is all about the guns. If you can master shooting, covering fire, swapping guns, you may just have a chance at getting that coveted A+. While the story can be confusing, I actually appreciate it. It doesn't spoon feed you, doesn't tell you who is good or bad, what's right or wrong. Thats up to you.

One of my rare Early Access game recommendations that is still impressive following full release.
After having 100%-ed
(which I still take out for a ride from time to time), I needed a new music game that allowed me to stuff one of the thousands of MP3s I had into the game and generate levels out of it. And
fit the bill perfectly.
Back when it was still in Early Access, I do feel that it is amongst one of the more complete Early Access titles on the Steam store nowadays. The basics of the gameplay are already well-versed: you control this rather cute* girl, perhaps the titular Melody, as she walks, runs, jumps over or ducks under obstacles, kicks apart other obstacles, even flies, while you mash the keys on your keyboard in a game not too dissimilar to Dance Dance Revolution or Guitar Hero.
It's a rather refreshing take on the genre as a 2D sidescroller rhythm game. The only downside I've seen is that since you're focusing more on the buttons you need to hit, you'll get eye strain and observe motion blur after a while, so don't play this for too long at a time.
The game also has Steam Workshop support, so you can customise your playing field anyway you like. You can customise Melody's attire, hair, and even the colour background/scheme. It's a cool way to personalise the game to however you want it to be.
's an example of what you are capable of.
Finally, the game engine is one of the best I've seen, and can certainly rival Audiosurf. Beat detection and vocal detection is superb, with well-placed sliding segments where you have to hold down the key during a vocal section.
I'll end off with the following statement from their
: "Icetesy is an indie game company from Belgium, with a passion for music generated gameplay." I hope this means more of this kind of game from them. I'm stoked.

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is the sequel to one of my favorite games of all time, and like any true sequel, it expands upon and improves upon the mechanics and story of the first one, for the most part at least. In the game, you play as a cast of interesting characters, ranging from a group of crazed fans of the first game's protag to a non-violent writer just trying to get the real story out there. While the idea of ditching the traditional mask system for different characters sounds good, it can be confusing, since you never play multiple chapters in a row as the same character, and there's a lot of rewinding, as the game has the aesthetic of a VHS tape. This also makes the story confusing.  The gameplay is mostly the same as the first, with nothing but improvements and pleasant variations on an already successful formula. The game does seem to lean more towards ranged combat using guns than melee combat at times, though. The game is near perfect, until about halfway through. It seems at this point, the developers rand out of ideas for level layouts, and just got lazy, making rooms much more open than they need to be, causing you to get sniped without being able to see what hit you, even when looking using shift. This leads to overly frustrating levels, that take a while to complete. Whereas in the first game I felt that when I died, it was my fault, this game had me saying "this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t" time after time. Due to the level design towards the end of this game, I'm swayed not to reccomend this game, but the stream of positives in this wonderful sequel balance it out.
"One more level" to the extreme.

There's plenty to enjoy in this game if you liked the first. The crazy story is back for more, the music is stylized and memorable, the overall playtime is longer, and the gameplay is familiar and twitchy with a few minor changes.

Overall grade: C-
Pros
+Truly challenging
+Some of the character arcs are amazing
+Great final level
+Still as violent and relentless as ever
+The amazing, no wait. THE BATSHIT INSANE AWESOME OST THAT WILL BLOW YOU THE ♥♥♥♥ AWAY
Cons
-Confusing story that doesn’t effectively tie up loose ends
-Poor weapon variety and restricted gameplay options especially compared to the first game
-Much shorter than expected with an ending that deliveries a “Wait what, that’s it?” response
-2-3 missions per character on average that make some character seem meaningless
-Horrifying bad bugs that really impact gameplay
I was on the fence whether to recommend or not recommend Hotline Miami. Hotline Miami 2 has many strengths but also has a fair number of problems that kill the mood and make the game experience more of a negative experience. However, the game is still fun and a blast to play despite these glaring problems. Most of the hatred and/or veneration this game gets is not deserved.
Make no mistake this a challenging game that will frustrate and enrage you. I find this to be a positive however, as I will get angry take a break come back and beat the level without trouble. This is an awesome experience beating what before was giving you so much trouble.
A few of the character arcs such as the secret character, the son, the journalist, and the detective are really fun as their arcs are the most fleshed out although the detective arc is one of the loose ends the game doesn’t fully address sadly. The final level while I’ll avoid spoiling it for you is ♥♥♥♥ing incredible but it doesn’t feel like a final level (No real climax).
While the core gameplay has changed for the worst caving a thugs head in with a baseball is just as great as it was for the first one and racking up the combo is an adrenaline inducing experience especially now that it’s even harder to really rack up the higher combos.  Lastly it cannot be overstated how badass the ost to the game is but I’ve heard that the ost that you can buy on the store is not complete.
The story is wretched. There is no other way of putting it. While the narrative is interesting the almost constant switching of characters makes it hard to follow the story at first. The second half of the game tends to stick with established characters so the second half is much easier to follow and until the ending is considerably better than the first half that is plagued with characters you only really get to play once or twice making them seem they don’t have a point to the larger narrative. What makes the son, the detective, the journalist so intriguing is that their narrative is that their stories are fundamentally tied together. Every other character doesn’t even come close to this. Especially the actor, who gets the introduction and one, ONE CHAPTER to play as. The movie never gets mentioned again that I’m aware of.
The ending deserves to be talked about as well. This ending literally makes Mass effect’s 3 original ending look good. No joke. The way it’s executed does not leave a trace of finality and feels like the devs couldn’t figure out a proper way of ending the story. At least two of the character “arcs” are left unresolved. Also the ending comes out of nowhere, the last level doesn’t even feel like a proper final level. The game would have really benefited from an additional 3-5 hours of gameplay.
The bugs, oh god the bugs, right now mooks will get stuck in walls, doors, anything and everything. One of the characters is a duo who you directly control except the second one who has the gun lags behind and loves getting stuck which is quite infuriating when you need him to pop some mooks while you’re chainsaw finishing some poor soul. The levels are often way too big so when you die it seems like a punishment where in the original death was cheap. I never got as annoyed in the original as I did in this one.
Finally, the game is very restrictive on how you play. The first one allowed you to choose what kind of direction and gameplay you wanted to go in. This one is very forceful of you playing in the gameplay style they want you to play as.
Overall, it’s not a terrible game but it’s definably of a case of too much hype and too much experimentation by the devs.

Ohboy. I'm really mixed on this game. It has another great soundtrack, great graphics and some really fun and interesting concepts, but the levels are bigger, the AI is lackluster, and bosses are easier.
Yeah, I mean I love virtually everything about this game, as I loved the original, but only a few isolated parts keep the level to a lower size. And because this game is way more gun-focused, you'll have guys running at you from the corners of the map, making you have to constantly look around you and keep on your toes, even when you need to focus on a fight. This isnt all that bad in some of the earlier parts of the game, but towards the end you'll absolutely despise the decision.
The AI is lackluster, I really hope an update comes out to fix some enemies being invincible while they fidget around on a doorway they're stuck in.
Bosses are really easy to kill, even the final bosses, which are neat, but still very easy compared to the original's tricky sequence.
But there are still really cool things about this game, mostly the characters and what they do. You dont have as much freedom of choice, basically being forced to a sub-group of masks or a certain character's special abilities every level, but the amount of fun you'll have with each one is really worth it in my opinion.
The scenarios the levels put you in are really interesting and give a unique twist to HM1's samey experience.
The story revolves around Jacket's "fans", people influenced by his actions or involved with him in some way. Which makes the story that much more interesting.
So I'd honestly reccomend waiting for a sale to pick up this one, but it's still a fairly decent game.

1. In-game sound is GONE. There's a random click here and there but ZERO environmental effects or music or anything like that.
2. Dialog is AWFUL. Seriously, talking to NPC's in the game is now worse than trying to read a cheap china-made fortune cookie... In chinese.

4. Framerates have gone straight into the crapper. Somehow, despite adding 12 GB of RAM and upgrading to a much beefier video card since my original review, my framerates are about HALF what they were before.
This seems like a classic case of a game being fixed until they broke it. I couldn't even play for an hour before I felt compelled to quit. Any longer and I would probably have gouged my own eyes out. I honestly hope they can fix this game, because it was SO GOOD before. I'll revisit this review at some point in the future and I'd REALLY like to be able to give it a thumbs-up again... But in the current state of the game, I simply can't recommend it. Not anymore. Cons

I was on the fence whether to recommend or not recommend Hotline Miami. Hotline Miami 2 has many strengths but also has a fair number of problems that kill the mood and make the game experience more of a negative experience. However, the game is still fun and a blast to play despite these glaring problems. Most of the hatred and/or veneration this game gets is not deserved.
Make no mistake this a challenging game that will frustrate and enrage you. I find this to be a positive however, as I will get angry take a break come back and beat the level without trouble. This is an awesome experience beating what before was giving you so much trouble.
A few of the character arcs such as the secret character, the son, the journalist, and the detective are really fun as their arcs are the most fleshed out although the detective arc is one of the loose ends the game doesn’t fully address sadly. The final level while I’ll avoid spoiling it for you is ♥♥♥♥ing incredible but it doesn’t feel like a final level (No real climax).
While the core gameplay has changed for the worst caving a thugs head in with a baseball is just as great as it was for the first one and racking up the combo is an adrenaline inducing experience especially now that it’s even harder to really rack up the higher combos.  Lastly it cannot be overstated how badass the ost to the game is but I’ve heard that the ost that you can buy on the store is not complete.
The story is wretched. There is no other way of putting it. While the narrative is interesting the almost constant switching of characters makes it hard to follow the story at first. The second half of the game tends to stick with established characters so the second half is much easier to follow and until the ending is considerably better than the first half that is plagued with characters you only really get to play once or twice making them seem they don’t have a point to the larger narrative. What makes the son, the detective, the journalist so intriguing is that their narrative is that their stories are fundamentally tied together. Every other character doesn’t even come close to this. Especially the actor, who gets the introduction and one, ONE CHAPTER to play as. The movie never gets mentioned again that I’m aware of.
The ending deserves to be talked about as well. This ending literally makes Mass effect’s 3 original ending look good. No joke. The way it’s executed does not leave a trace of finality and feels like the devs couldn’t figure out a proper way of ending the story. At least two of the character “arcs” are left unresolved. Also the ending comes out of nowhere, the last level doesn’t even feel like a proper final level. The game would have really benefited from an additional 3-5 hours of gameplay.
The bugs, oh god the bugs, right now mooks will get stuck in walls, doors, anything and everything. One of the characters is a duo who you directly control except the second one who has the gun lags behind and loves getting stuck which is quite infuriating when you need him to pop some mooks while you’re chainsaw finishing some poor soul. The levels are often way too big so when you die it seems like a punishment where in the original death was cheap. I never got as annoyed in the original as I did in this one.
Finally, the game is very restrictive on how you play. The first one allowed you to choose what kind of direction and gameplay you wanted to go in. This one is very forceful of you playing in the gameplay style they want you to play as.
Overall, it’s not a terrible game but it’s definably of a case of too much hype and too much experimentation by the devs.

Ohboy. I'm really mixed on this game. It has another great soundtrack, great graphics and some really fun and interesting concepts, but the levels are bigger, the AI is lackluster, and bosses are easier.
Yeah, I mean I love virtually everything about this game, as I loved the original, but only a few isolated parts keep the level to a lower size. And because this game is way more gun-focused, you'll have guys running at you from the corners of the map, making you have to constantly look around you and keep on your toes, even when you need to focus on a fight. This isnt all that bad in some of the earlier parts of the game, but towards the end you'll absolutely despise the decision.
The AI is lackluster, I really hope an update comes out to fix some enemies being invincible while they fidget around on a doorway they're stuck in.
Bosses are really easy to kill, even the final bosses, which are neat, but still very easy compared to the original's tricky sequence.
But there are still really cool things about this game, mostly the characters and what they do. You dont have as much freedom of choice, basically being forced to a sub-group of masks or a certain character's special abilities every level, but the amount of fun you'll have with each one is really worth it in my opinion.
The scenarios the levels put you in are really interesting and give a unique twist to HM1's samey experience.
The story revolves around Jacket's "fans", people influenced by his actions or involved with him in some way. Which makes the story that much more interesting.
So I'd honestly reccomend waiting for a sale to pick up this one, but it's still a fairly decent game.

The characters are all very interesting if you pay attention to details to get some of the unspoken backstories, as well as just their inner monologues. The soundtrack, as expected, is ♥♥♥♥ing PHENOMENAL. I cannot stress enough how much thought and work went into the music for this game. If I had to listen to one album for the rest of my life, it would be the Wrong Number soundtrack.

It has improved on the previous game. One downside that I need to talk about is that you do not get to choose your masks, as you play as characters. This improves the story, but means there is very little customization. This is completely fine and don't let it influence your decision.
All the characters play very differently and all in fun ways. Some of the levels are challenging, but in the same spirit as the first game, you can get right back up and try again immediately.
If you're on the fence about the game, go play the first one and see if you like it.

After putting in a full solid day worth of playing I can say this game did not impress me at first.  I found it incomplete having some quests/ dialog voice acted (poorly I might add) and others not at all as well as sketchy UI and graphics issues.
My original intentions were to buy this game for my kids however I'm changing my mind on that due to the games inherent lack of any type of tutorial system.  Some very basic things are outlined for you but most of it is glossed over with little to no detail.  For example you'll have a quest to obtain certain plant types (or kill certain animals).  The most help you'll receive is an extremely tiny picture (literally maybe 50x50 pixels) of what you need to find.  I found myself having to search the online wiki a few times just to get an idea what the heck I was looking for.  Also from what I can gather there is no way to know what you're looking at - mousing over animals or plants doesn't give you the slightest idea what it is you're looking at.  So all you have to go off of is this tiny picture in the mission UI.
After a few hours of play though the game did start to grow on me.  It felt like a mix of Minecraft and a RPG.  The graphics are adequate, the game runs fair at best on my i7 Crossfire rig under max settings.  I think this is in part the game does not run in true full screen mode.   I have a triple monitor setup (non eyefinity) and many times (during battle mostly) found myself clicking off the screen thus pushing the game to the background.  In other words in this alleged full screen mode you can still move the mouse beyond the frame of the game.  Also since this is not true full screen it probably plays a role in why crossfire / SLI can't be fully utilized.  Also let me add the game crashed after several hours of play due to a memory leak.
If you are running high resolution (1920x1080 for myself) the UI does not scale proportionally making it difficult to see / read.  To my knowledge you can move the UI around which helps you customize and tailor to you needs but you cannot resize any of it.  This is especially true for the mini map.  Devs if you're listening please make the UI scalable / let us resize as we see fit.

I honestly feel the game has huge potential but in its current state needs work.  It definetely feels like an early access game.  If the developers keep an ear to the ground and resolve some of these basic issues this game will have serious legs.
As it stands as of today I'd give this title a 76 out of 100.  If the full screen issue was resolved, the game was fully voice acted, and there were better UI and tutorials it would score in the mid to high 80s for me.
I'll continue to play it as I feel I've only scratched the surface of what the game has to offer.  I will update this review in the future if need be.

I have been eyeing this game for quite some time. I finally pulled the trigger on it and it is now in a pretty enjoyable and playable state.

If you like games where you craft and build stuff (like minecraft) but with a beautiful 3d engine and a story. . .  jump on in!

I have played mostly the story mode, using the building functionality to weave in a little creativity, but I have yet to play this a la Minecraft. But I really, really like the game! The story is interesting, the world is immersive, and it's just plain cool. It's a very well done game. However, it's by all means still in Beta.
My complaints:
-Some of the missions require walking back and forth across the (very large) map, with fast traveling not an option when you have a follower. I dislike that, it's a waste of time. Enabling followers to fast travel with you would fix this, and I'm confident they'll do that before the final version.
-The storyline gets implayable at a certain point. I hit a wall where a bug disallowed the game from recognizing one action as complete, and it couldn't progress the story. Obviously, these will be handled before a full release, so it's not fair to say the game is bad when it's simply (and admittedly) incomplete, but I thought it was nonetheless worth mentioning in my review.
-Gathering resources to go through stuff you use in regular gameplay gets a little tedious. You can buy resources from certain NPCs, but the quantities available are small and the prices high. Building your own stuff is a nice part of the game, but gathering resources for an hour just to restock on bullets is annoying. Again, I expect they may improve this before the final release.
My praises:
-I really like the way combat is done, the way you can focus on it or not. There's a fair amount of combat to be done, but I just made automatic turrets, carry them in my inventory, and let them take care of whatever it is while I just keep clear. That way, combat for me is just making sure I've got enough turrets and ammo in my inventory for whatever I expect to fight.
-The RPG and the sandbox elements work together really nicely.
-The opening quests do a good job explaining how the game works. It did take me a minute to figure out what buttons to press, but once I got that down the explanations were helpful without being annoying.
All in all, I think this game will be one of my favorites once it's done. The RPG gameplay seems to only be 60% done, whereas the builder gameplay seems to be 95% up and running. So depending on your gameplay preferences, you may prefer to wait it out until it's a little more complete. I personally chose to put it aside and plan to revisit it when it's complete, since I was more focused on the RPG gameplay, but I definitely recommend it either way.

I found myself enjoy this quite a bit. It manages to be a lot more like games like Guitar Hero than an actual runner, as it uses button timings, that, for the most part, are on rhythm with the song and it works quite well.
The game uses your own library of music, and it manages to find it easily, so you don't have to work to find it. I do miss an option to search for the songs though, but you can drag and drop them into the window instead, so I suppose that searching for them outside of it works as well, but in full-screen mode, that of course doesn't work, so you're stuck looking for the songs instead. I also wish that you could search for song length and file-type as well.
There are some issues with the way the songs work sometimes, and that is that it randomly, it takes a pretty energetic part of a song and instead of making it a running section, it becomes a walking section instead. This can be quite off-putting, and kind of take the joy away from you when you are ready for a blasting section of intense gameplay, though it is quite rare that it happens, so it might just be the song's fault that it interacts weirdly with the system.
A personal problem I have is that when I play more intense sections, my eyes get fuzzy and I cannot concentrate that well. This is of course not something everybody experiences, but even with all settings turned off or tweaking them, I still get it. It doesn't affect my gameplay much, as I can still concentrate one one point, it's more my peripheral vision that gets a little bit wonky.
I tried to put it at a lower resolution, but that didn't work either. That was also the point where I noticed another problem. The fact that it doesn't seem to fill out the whole window, rather, it puts black bars on the top and bottom of it, which is quite ugly looking, making me not want to play the windowed version.
I like how you can customize your character and have the Steam Workshop integrated right in so you can use other characters, should you wish to do that, and I like how you can make your own rules to the gameplay, and it has quite a lot you can actually change.
Some changes I think could be cool would be to have multiple songs play after each other, a playlist feature of sorts, and possibly a leaderboard, though that might be a little bit hard to implement since everybody is using different files and names, so not sure how that would work, but it could be possible.
I think it could use a bit of tutorial that teaches you as you play, instead of the vague slideshow tutorial that you even need to look in another menu to find. While it's a simple concept that you can grasp quickly, I still felt as though I was doing something wrong the whole time. I wasn't sure how long I was suppose to hold it, or if holding it had any impact for the one button presses, and I also felt as though the way that the buttons were arrows were pressed didn't give me much feedback, so I felt as though I did it wrong.
Though, while it has problems like that and things I would like that aren't there, the game is still fun, and this is coming from a guy who doesn't play a whole lot of runner games.
9/10 Graphics - The graphics have a very simple style to them, the main character, Melody, looks like something out of an Apple commercial, which I think might be the point, though the works very well regardless of the simplicity. You are never confused as to which button you're suppose to press, and while I was confused if I was doing it right when I started, I got the hang of it later.
7/10 Gameplay/Controls - It's a simple runner with some button press elements, it's not anything you haven't seen before, I can even name a game that does the same, Bit.Trip Runner, and it doesn't really add anything new to that either, and I wish it had something more original to it, but that said, doesn't mean that it's bad. It's smooth, it works, it's fun, it doesn't feel as though it's ever cheating you in the button presses, you always feel as though it was you that made a mistake (not that I make any of course :P), so there's nothing wrong there. I do miss a bit of feedback when you hit it, a sound effect to let you know you hit it right, but of course not something so distracting that it distracts from the songs themselves. The control side is pretty much perfect though, as all you do is click the button, there isn't much room for error, but if there was, it would make the game unplayable. Luckily, there isn't.
8/10 Music/Sound - Well, of course this is a little bit hard to actually say, since you use your own music, though hear me out here: The songs are high quality, you can use plenty of file types from the look of it, and the way the songs make the levels works well 9/10. I do wish for the ability to search your songs more easily though. Sound-wise, well, there are not any sound effects during gameplay, and that might be okay for some, but I wish for feedback when I click a button, as mentioned already. There are sounds in the menu though, it's nothing special either, but it isn't annoying and it blends in well with the style of the game as well.
7/10 Value - There is not a whole lot to this game. It's a simple game with a simple concept, but what it does is very good, even for it being early access. It's worth your money as it is right now, around 10€, as the game can never really be done, at least until you run out of music ;)
8/10 Overall - The game is high above average, while it doesn't do a whole lot new, it does it well, and doesn't make any false promises. Pick it up if you like music, you like runners/rhythm games and you like games that make levels off of your music.

I blew through normal mode today, so time to write a review I guess.
If you've come here after playing Hotline 1, you want to know how it holds up on two fronts.
Combat is still visceral and fun, although I found myself missing the level design from the first game. It feels more restricted, although that's likely due in part to the character system present here. While the personalities do add to the story, I feel like the mask system from 1 worked better. I can see why they didn't use it though-so moving on.
The story in Wrong Number left me cold. The characters all work, and as a writer I can't argue against them. There will be some spoilers from here in-minor ones that you'll probably see coming anyhow. If you don't want any spoilers at all, please skip down to "CONCLUSIONS."
Ready?
I didn't feel that I had enough time to really grow to like (too strong a word for most of the sociopaths) the characters before their untimely deaths. While the structure works-flipping between characters to get the big picture-the ending didn't really leave it open to interpretation like 1 did, which I felt was a defining moment for the first game, as we were given reasons to "like" each character making it hard to internally decide who survived the events of 50 blessings.
HOWEVER
Having done some minor research and putting a lot of thought into it, the entire game is an interpretation.
Super spoilers ahead guys. You may want to skip ahead to the conclusion down there.
In Hotline Miami, Jacket ends up following a false lead from the 50 Blessings group, which lead him to his attack on the Mafia tower. This takes him to the wrong address and is why Richard said Jacket would never find the answers he wanted. Only Biker's path-where Jacket dies-takes a good turn, where he finds and unmasks 50 Blessings for what is really is with the puzzle pieces. This takes him to the other side of town, and a different address. The "Right" number.
Still, the ending of this game sort of whacked me-it definitively shows Jacket's death. As a generally pro-Jacket guy, this means that no matter which ending of Hotline 1 you preferred, Jacket is still dead. More's the pity for me, although I think we can all agree it was bound to happen eventually. Just not like this.
CONCLUSIONS
I blasted through normal in six hours or so, and despite not enjoying it overall as much as I did with the original, I still had a blast and a half. Hotline fans, rejoice, for the sequel is indeed good. Just prepare to be crushed a few times over the course of the story.
Oh, and there's an unlockable hard mode which does add to the story-and it lives up to the name. You can't go wrong with this game if you liked the first.

Excellent game! Even better if you have friends to play with. If you don't, like me, you can still play with bots or random players, and so far I've not had a bad experience with random players. A lot of them don't use their mic or even text chat, but they still play well and help you when you're down.
It feels like Left 4 Dead mixed with a bit of Chivalry. There's a large focus on melee, though there are pistols, rifles, crossbows, etc. for when you need to kill someone from a distance.
The game is very fleshed out, with a loot system (roll dice after finishing a mission, you get more dice to roll by completing higher difficulties, collecting hidden tomes and grimoire in the missions, etc.) and a forging system. You can combine 5 items of the same rarity level to create a new item. It's very addicting!
There's an Inn that you can hang out at between missions if you want to. You can look at your inventory here, mess with the forging system, vote on the next mission, and test out your weapons.
There's five classes to play as. Witch Hunter, Bright Wizard, Dwarf Ranger, Empire Soldier, and the Waywatcher. They all feel very different from one another and a cool touch is that they all have voices and will respond to one another during missions.
I'd highly recommend this game, it's a fantastic co-op game with a lot of depth. There may only be 11 missions, but each one has a bit of randomization to it and feels fresh each time you play through it.

The only downside is that it is not yet optimized. This is a shame because the longer you play, the more fun toys there are to play with, but the slower the game runs, making it harder to enjoy said toys. And it only gets worse underground.
I'd be Batmanning it up in the Giant Spider Caves right now if it didn't run at about 13 FPS in my current save file.
Still, this is far and away better than your average indie alpha sandbox game. It puts Sir You are Being Hunted, Windforge, StarForge, and Edge of Space to shame. In my opinion, it's worth every penny full price as is, let alone when it's finished.
