Well , where do I begin ...
While the gameplay may seem very different from the first one , it's still pretty good. In the first game you were more the meele guy , Thugs (aka the big guys) being rare , thus not needing guns. Rooms were smaller , corridors werent so long , there weren't so many windows , and the list goes on. In HM2 level design took a different direction , meaning that now there are a lot of open spaces and big rooms filled with ranged enemies. HM2 is more based on gun fight , rather than meele (and thats why so many people got their jimmies rustled). Many people say that the best tactic is luring enemies , but that's only if you are a big sissy. You can go guns blazing , doing combos and still having fun. I admit that some levels are poorly made , resulting in a lot of frustration , but overall the level design isn't horrible , just different from the first game. One thing that bothered me is that there are some objects that seem to be just part of the background , but when i try to shoot through them , i can't. These "cover" objects can really be annoying.
In the first Hotline Miami , there was some story , but pretty vague. Only after getting the secret ending , you could understand some things. In Hotline Miami 2 , most of your questions are answered. You will see some new faces , some old faces and you will get a handful of answers. In some cases , you just need to look carefully and think about what you just saw to fully understand the story. The ending ? Well , what can I say ... It was really unexpected. The ending (the normal one , i havent found any secret endings yet) was pretty mind-blowing and shocking. Clearly not what I expected , but clearly not bad.
In Hotline Miami 2 you will have a large selection of characters to play as. My personal favorite are the Fans. Most of the characters are unique , and have their unique mechanics (Roll dodge , killer punches , akimbo , etc). Each character has it's own storyline that you will discover as you play the game.

Pure genius. Hell , even if you hate the game with passion , you can still love the soundtrack.
Overall, Hotline Miami 2 feels very different from the first game , but it's still a very good game , even with it's flaws.
It's story may be hard to understand , it's levels may be hard to finish , but when you get to the end of it , oh boy , it feels so good.
Should you buy this game ? Right now , without the level editor , i say its kinda overpriced , wait until is like 10 bucks or so.

Hotline Miami is one of my all time favorite games and I couldn't have been more excited to finally play this, but does it live up to the original? Yes and no.
Let's get the negatives out of the way: You would think that the games story would be the highlight of the game and believe me, it was until about three quarters of the way through. What gives? Well, there certainly is more story to it, and in all honesty theres probably more dialogue in one act of this game (of 6) than there was in the entirety of the original. And it's not bad, it just feels very incomplete. Story lines pop up like weeds and just like that, they fizzle out or amount to little more than a bit of backstory. This all makes me think the characters are all but useless in this sequel with just as pointless story lines. The other negative is the fact that the game opted out of the tightly packed apartments and neon drenched clubs for wide open exteriors and bigger neon drenched clubs. In a game that means instant death , a stray bullet from the corner of the map happens way too often. The other drawback is the overuse of guns in the game; As some levels almost force you to use them for the duration of the level, and killing as stylishly room to room goes out the window in favor of taking pot shots from behind cover and constantly baiting enemies to come to you. The amount of variation just isn't as extensive as the original due to a lack of different masks. Sure there are a lot of characters to play as but The Fans play exactly the same as The Son (with the exception of Ash and Alex) And The Detective plays just like Richter.
Time for the positives: Even though I seemed to have hammered the game above, it's still exhillerating to play and just as addictive as the first game. Environments are still stylish and vibrant, and it's still a blast murdering thugs one by one until an abandoned warehouse turns into your own personal painting of mayhem and death. The other huge plus is the soundtrack. Chances are if you played the first game, you loved the soundtrack just as much as I did and this time around the music is even better. The hypnotic synth and pounding beats propel you forward through each level even more so than the story itself. Another positive is that this sequel seemed to have taken risks. Sure, I gave them negative marks for some of them above but at least it wasn't just a copy and paste job of the original (Even though I don't think that would be bad for this game). Some of the additions to this game are wonderful like the aforementioned Ash and Alex (The Swans), a brother/sister duo that you control, one on the chainsaw and the other trailing behind with a gun in hand. Some of my favorite moments were due to this team as I barged through a door and made messy work of 2 or 3 goons and perform a lengthy chainsaw finisher on the fourth guy as 2 or 3 more guys tried to crash my party only for them to meet the business end of the pistol in hand of the other sibling. It was an absolute blast playing this game sometimes.
Truly exciting stuff happened while playing this sequel, and while a lot of things happened that I didn't care much for, I do not regret my purchase. You can defend the story by saying it had a truly deep meaning to it and that's fine, to each their own, it just wasn't my cup of tea and I wish it had turned out more like the original than this ill fitting jigsaw puzzle that seemed like it was hammer fisted into place. Although, I'm very excited to get my hands on the level editor due out this Spring and spend hours building levels reminiscent of the original and playing other players' creations, crafting my own story.
- Too many meaningless characters and story lines, too big of environments and gun happy levels, Too much baiting and pot shotting instead of barging in and taking risks and not enough variation in masks.
+ Amazing soundtrack, The Swans, Still addictive and fun, Beautiful, The level editor will no doubt add endless replayability and allow us to create better fitting levels.
EDIT: Okay, so after mulling over the story and letting it sit, it's starting to grow on me and I'm starting to like it. Is it better than the first game? No, not at all. It does weave a decently interesting narative that feels more like a spin off inhabiting the same world rather than a sequel. I can come to terms with most of the characters and their specific stories but there are two characters that I feel contribute almost nothing to the story and that's the tale of The Son and The Pig. I felt like The Son should have had a compelling story to tell as he has somewhat of a history with the original games protagonist but it just winds up being filler. As for The Pig, he has almost nothing to do with the story that I can decipher. He just happens to be an actor of a film that is inspired by Jacket and his wave of destruction in the first game; He also happens to be going a tad bit insane, but instead of capitalizing on that thread, they simply do almost nothing with it. So in the end, while I happened to enjoy the overall story, I feel like it was a huge missed opportunity. They could have told a half dozen truly engaging stories that built up and beautifully crescendoed in a bloody and trippy finale that all merged like a horrifying train wreck, but instead it erratically jumped between storylines that loosely tied together. I expected grand fireworks and I got those pop rocks and sparklers. To those that know the ending, I'm okay with the "big ending", I just wish the journey to that point was told a little smoother and had more of a lasting impact than being half baked stories.

So if it wasn't due to the F2P weekend, myself and my mates probably would have never heard of this, and put it down to a 'risky purchase' title, due to its price when it's not on sale. Thankfully, after getting into this game with a couple of mates, I have to say this has been the best co-op experience I've had for quite sometime.
Now, this is based on my experience with two other mates, on TS. Not random people, which is something I don't do. So my opinion/review may not apply to those who are looking to play this with randomers, and I can say this is a game you don't play on your own as it's heavily geared towards a co-operative experience, and that's a good thing.
Gameplay: Overall, the experience was very enjoyable. There is a lot of 'immersion' going on coupled with the excellent quality of sounds that make things intense. We found it most enjoyable with the Escape mode which, in my opinion, is the games main selling point and I think the developer should strongly consider developing this mode further as it does need to be fleshed out with more maps. Right now there is only a limited few actual Escape maps available and I'm not entirely sure how much the game randomises the rounds/maps but I'd imagine not by a lot.
The game is very well paced and you find yourself never wanting to go back to the horde mechanics of L4D with it's fast zombies. The zombies here are much slower, but in a strange sense, much more deadlier. Your ammo is limited and getting attacked by zombies can result in an infection. It also adds greater tension to gameplay when your backed up in a corner, limited ammo and trying to fend off an encroaching horde. I do feel the game needs some balancing in terms of the infection mechanic during co-op. Because infected players can keep on coming at you, and at you, and your ammo supply is very limited in this game. It does change the pace a lot when that happens, forcing the players to hurry, but some sort of balancing might be needed there. Perhaps a longer respawn time for infected players?
Map Design: The maps, despite the small amount of Escape ones, are very well done. The ones we did, Biotech and the Police Department one, are very large. Our game session in the PD one was 66 minutes long. The only thing holding this game back is the lack of similar maps. I would love (even pay) for a good quality large map-pack.
Sound: If there's one thing I can say I like best about Cotagion, it's the sound. The sound is very impressive and very underated in any reviews I've seen. Coupled with the excellent music and the backdrop of high quality zombie moans, you've got yourself a terrifying experience. The weapon sounds are also impressive which is surprising considering so many top studios fail at producing good quality sounds. I can't stress enough that the sound quality in this game is by far the best I've seen in most other games I've played.
Graphics: I've seen one review that called the graphics in this game 'dated'... I laughed. They're not AAA graphics by any sense of the imagination, but they are not decades old either. The graphics do their job. I would say they are a cut above the average but I've not heard any complaints from my mates who've tried it out and I can't say I've got any complaints either.
Overall I'd recommend this game. I've gotten this game on sale at 75% off. I think if the game had more maps, and considering its geared towards co-operative play, I'd say it would then be worth the original price. Then again the counter-arguement to that is your apparently getting all future DLC and content for free? If that's the case then the original price may not be so bad, but the developer doesn't make it clear, or at least, I can't find it, on where or what future dlc might be in the works other than what's listed on the front page.

The thinking man's L4D.  My favorite game mode 'Escape' has you and up to seven other players cooperating to escape from the map, which is dynamically arranged with new paths and objectives every time you play.
Ammo conservation and trigger discipline is absolutely critical, you can't just mindlessly run into a room full of zombies and hope to survive without backup, you never know where the next box of bullets will be.  The frenetic horde-style action of L4D is replaced with a somewhat more thoughtful pace, you have time to realize that you have three bullets left, and you know you'll have to open another door to maybe find more ammo, or a room full of zombies, and ideally they aren't going to break through it while you're considering your options.
Teammate cooperation becomes not only beneficial, but it is required for success, as each player has a very limited supply of ammunition, and whatever weapons they've picked up along the way.  Your guns, one of which you'll spawn with, the rest need to be found as they spawn randomly, have to be manually reloaded, and you'll need headshots if you hope to kill enough zombies to get through the next room.  Melee weapons are an option, if you've found any, but the speed of lifting your axe to swing it, chopping an enemies arm off, to have them continue attacking you, leaves you open to attack from more zombies behind you.
The randomly appearing obstacles through each map include things like: locked doors; you found a key right? Fires; This hallway is on fire, did anyone find a fire extinguisher?  Chained up doors; damn!  There's got to be some bolt cutters somewhere...
So, you ran out of ammo, fell into a fire, and got trapped against a locked door while a horde of zombies came rushing in?  No problem!
Dying in coop has a consolation prize, you die and become a zombie!  Now you can punish your erstwhile companions for having gotten to that ammo before you did, not helping you find a fire extinguisher, and not shooting those zombies that were attacking you!  After all, that was probably what caused your death, right?  Every player that has died is now on a team of zombies, to coordinate their attack and prevent the players from accomplishing their objectives to escape.
All in all, killed a zombie with a wrench and died in a fire 10/10 would buy again

Terrible game.  I read one of the positive reviews and wonder what game they played.  This game is confusing and glitchy.  The cell phone, which gives you your missions, had text that was too large for its screen, so I ended up with only a quarter or less of the goal description, which was useless.
I spawned (twice) in a building that had no way out.  I gave it the benefit of the doubt and searched for a key or something to open the outside doors, and after about an hour of searching, gave up and disconnected.  It wasn't even that big a building.  Even if there WAS a way out, a good game doesn't have you sitting around with nothing to do for an hour.
Buttons would sometimes not do what they were supposed to.  Once I ran out of ammo, and it wouldn't let me melee.  What is worse, when you do melee, it feels like your just slapping the zombie.  If I was gonna hit a zombie, I'd hit the zombie hard enough to knock it over or break something.  In the game, I hit a zombie over and over and over, and it never got knocked back, and it never died.  Finally a teammate found me and shot it.
Someone mentioned how much fun it was to not have much ammo.  Well, I got stuck without ammo on a ladder with zombies at the top, and I couldn't get them out of the way.  These zombies finally discovered the perfect strategy.  Just swallow the ammo and stand on the ladders, and there's no way they'll ever escape.
If this game has any hope of being a fun experience, they've got a lot of work to do.  It isn't exciting.  It isn't scary.  It isn't fun.  What were they hoping the game would be?  And why have a free weekend when the game is in such a terrible state?
I'll follow this up by saying that the game may have some redeeming qualities that I didn't see.  I didn't play much, and won't be coming back, so I may have missed the best it has to offer.  But with so many excellent games out there... I don't see how they can balance out the hours of unexplained, empty, lonely exploration that concluded in exiting to desktop.

Zombie Hunger Games Simulator 2014
10/10

Ill start with what I liked about the game:
The single player is fairly fun, it has quests and the like. Crafting system is very basic and the UI is easy to understand. Graphics are nothing to write home about but are okay and playable in my opinion. The custom content creator is VERY cool which you can make custom 3D vehicles and weapons after getting used to it for about 10 minutes. The content you made can be seen in-game right after you make it (after you purchase it and materials). Its also a voxel game which means the mining and everything is in 3D as opposed to minecraft where its all blocks. Combat can also be fun against certain mobs and large boss monsters. The vehicles and equipment can be fun to use like the jetpack + glider.
Why I don't recommend it:
First of all the game has been in development for about 3 years now and I still feel like its VERY unfinnished. Most of my complaint is the multiplayer. The lobby is REALLY buggy and attempting to connect to friends can be a pain. Me and my friends played it for about 25 or so hours (steam says only 10 because it disables after you close the launcher) and we pretty much did all that you can do in the game and quickly got bored.
Building structures is very lame and unrewarding as there is practically no actual use for them other than aesthetics (they also look terrible). It also feels very awkward to build and you don't get much choice in materials and objects to use.
The survival element is mostly just fighting off monsters. Which until you can afford to buy weapons, is almost impossible. You also have NO reason to craft items as you can BUY everything via in-game shop which after you just mine random ores and sell it you can buy anything you want fairly quickly, you get end-game content in under an hour if you wanted.
I feel like the game is VERY lackluster in content and will only keep you entertained for 30 hours at most before you get bored of it. They say they will release the game sometime in 2014 and if they do at this state then that means this game is a ripoff. There was also plenty of bugs but because it is early access I won't have that as a reason for my unrecommendation.
Almost none of the features work, constantly crashes. I do realize it's an alpha, but this game should not be on the market right now.  I wan't a refund.

You could describe it as zombies meet the classic Prince of Persia platformer, but I'd call it a frustration simulator.  The problem is that most parts of the game will kill you the first time.  You then replay the section knowing what the trap is and hopefully avoid it.   Some sections have short gaps between checkpoints, some large.  So you might end up doing a long bit again and again as you discover each trap.  Worse, sometimes there are dialogue bits that you heav to hear over and over again.
All this constant reloading is made worse by the delay in first asking you to press a button to reload, then taking a while to reload.  I'm dead (again), there is nothing I can do except reload, why bother asking and delaying me?  The strangely long load time along with a couple of times the menu seems to get stuck hint at a poor PC port.  BTW I particularly wouldn't recommend this without an XBOX controller.
The game also suffers from giving you a limited supply of ammo for guns - you're clearly only supposed to use it in a worst case scenario.  I found that meant I just horded it and never used it, though towards the end this did improve.
For the postives, the story is OK, though a bit hammy - the whole Rat man bit is quite poor. Where the game really shines is graphically, the art direction is great.
I picked it up for a few quid and got more hours out of it than I wanted to.

The recommendation for this game is kind of an opinionated situation.
This game has tons of potential, to say first. There are many small things that could make this game much more fun to play. Here are a few examples:
Spotting- There is a very limited spotting system in this game. To spot something, you have to look at it for a few seconds, then a red blip, an inverted triangle for infantry, or a rhombus for vehicle, pops up on where you spotted it at for a few seconds. This could be improved by having a button initiated spotting system, and the spot, maybe, could show you what kind they are, for example, a recon could be marked with a different colored triangle, or a plane could be a different shape than, say, a tank.
Hitmarkers- There are no hitmarkers in this game, all you get is a message on the bottom area of your screen informing you that you hit someone. This can get annoying when you are on a killstreak and messages are taking up your viewspace. Also, when you get a hit, a short 'ugh' plays, like you could hear them from however far away you hit them. In my opinion, that sound should be removed, along with the message of you hitting someone, not killing anyone or destroying anything, and replaced with a simple hitmarker.
Weapon Reloads- This isn't that big of a deal, it's just something that I would change if I was the developer. Every time you reload, you don't just put the magazine in- you have to reload it as if there was no bullet in the chamber. Also, it would be cool if a single bullet that represents the one in the chamber would be added in addition to the current magazine size.
Graphics and Character Models- Graphics should be improved. 2d grass is kind of annoying. Character models should be improved, also, because the current ones are a little bit unrealistic.
Weapon Descriptions- When I'm looking at a weapon, I want to know every single stat possible. Bullet velocity, bullet drop, damage, accuracy, rate of fire, ammo in magazine, and with tanks, planes, and other vehicles, I want to know the armor stat for them, for example, 25mm of armor on the Tiger I's back. I don't know if this counts as descriptions, but the battle briefing is not very detailed. I want to know what assault team resources I have at my disposal, the country I'm fighting, and how many other players there are, and, (For my team) their branch of the army. Also, in some weapon descriptions there are spelling errors.
Melee Weapons- These things are vastly underpowered. The biggest thing that I don't like about them is that they take up a slot in your loadout instead of being something that you have by default. The second thing is that it takes a hit up very close to the head to kill someone. Maybe, a knife or shovel animation could be introduced, or make the thing one hit anywhere, at least for a knife, and a little bit longer range.
Things that I love about this game:
-You can see your feet!
-Weapons are less accurate when moving
-The maps are big, and there is a lot of tactical play in battles.
-There are authentic WW2 weapons and vehicles!
-Strategic war part of the game
I understand that this game is in beta, and that it was released on July 11th of last year. Since I have last played, I have noticed some great changes to the game.
What I think is that Reto-Moto should spend less time on adding new content, like the Soviets, and focus more on gameplay mechanics and small things like I described. Of course, the Soviet update was pretty cool- now I can go around talking about vodka, Stalin, and the motherland.
If you like the tactical gameplay and enjoy authentic WW2 weapons and vehicles and can tolerate some annoyances like these, play this game. I do. I enjoy it a lot.

Hotline Miami is one of my all time favorite games and I couldn't have been more excited to finally play this, but does it live up to the original? Yes and no.
Let's get the negatives out of the way: You would think that the games story would be the highlight of the game and believe me, it was until about three quarters of the way through. What gives? Well, there certainly is more story to it, and in all honesty theres probably more dialogue in one act of this game (of 6) than there was in the entirety of the original. And it's not bad, it just feels very incomplete. Story lines pop up like weeds and just like that, they fizzle out or amount to little more than a bit of backstory. This all makes me think the characters are all but useless in this sequel with just as pointless story lines. The other negative is the fact that the game opted out of the tightly packed apartments and neon drenched clubs for wide open exteriors and bigger neon drenched clubs. In a game that means instant death , a stray bullet from the corner of the map happens way too often. The other drawback is the overuse of guns in the game; As some levels almost force you to use them for the duration of the level, and killing as stylishly room to room goes out the window in favor of taking pot shots from behind cover and constantly baiting enemies to come to you. The amount of variation just isn't as extensive as the original due to a lack of different masks. Sure there are a lot of characters to play as but The Fans play exactly the same as The Son (with the exception of Ash and Alex) And The Detective plays just like Richter.
Time for the positives: Even though I seemed to have hammered the game above, it's still exhillerating to play and just as addictive as the first game. Environments are still stylish and vibrant, and it's still a blast murdering thugs one by one until an abandoned warehouse turns into your own personal painting of mayhem and death. The other huge plus is the soundtrack. Chances are if you played the first game, you loved the soundtrack just as much as I did and this time around the music is even better. The hypnotic synth and pounding beats propel you forward through each level even more so than the story itself. Another positive is that this sequel seemed to have taken risks. Sure, I gave them negative marks for some of them above but at least it wasn't just a copy and paste job of the original (Even though I don't think that would be bad for this game). Some of the additions to this game are wonderful like the aforementioned Ash and Alex (The Swans), a brother/sister duo that you control, one on the chainsaw and the other trailing behind with a gun in hand. Some of my favorite moments were due to this team as I barged through a door and made messy work of 2 or 3 goons and perform a lengthy chainsaw finisher on the fourth guy as 2 or 3 more guys tried to crash my party only for them to meet the business end of the pistol in hand of the other sibling. It was an absolute blast playing this game sometimes.
Truly exciting stuff happened while playing this sequel, and while a lot of things happened that I didn't care much for, I do not regret my purchase. You can defend the story by saying it had a truly deep meaning to it and that's fine, to each their own, it just wasn't my cup of tea and I wish it had turned out more like the original than this ill fitting jigsaw puzzle that seemed like it was hammer fisted into place. Although, I'm very excited to get my hands on the level editor due out this Spring and spend hours building levels reminiscent of the original and playing other players' creations, crafting my own story.
- Too many meaningless characters and story lines, too big of environments and gun happy levels, Too much baiting and pot shotting instead of barging in and taking risks and not enough variation in masks.
+ Amazing soundtrack, The Swans, Still addictive and fun, Beautiful, The level editor will no doubt add endless replayability and allow us to create better fitting levels.
EDIT: Okay, so after mulling over the story and letting it sit, it's starting to grow on me and I'm starting to like it. Is it better than the first game? No, not at all. It does weave a decently interesting narative that feels more like a spin off inhabiting the same world rather than a sequel. I can come to terms with most of the characters and their specific stories but there are two characters that I feel contribute almost nothing to the story and that's the tale of The Son and The Pig. I felt like The Son should have had a compelling story to tell as he has somewhat of a history with the original games protagonist but it just winds up being filler. As for The Pig, he has almost nothing to do with the story that I can decipher. He just happens to be an actor of a film that is inspired by Jacket and his wave of destruction in the first game; He also happens to be going a tad bit insane, but instead of capitalizing on that thread, they simply do almost nothing with it. So in the end, while I happened to enjoy the overall story, I feel like it was a huge missed opportunity. They could have told a half dozen truly engaging stories that built up and beautifully crescendoed in a bloody and trippy finale that all merged like a horrifying train wreck, but instead it erratically jumped between storylines that loosely tied together. I expected grand fireworks and I got those pop rocks and sparklers. To those that know the ending, I'm okay with the "big ending", I just wish the journey to that point was told a little smoother and had more of a lasting impact than being half baked stories.

This problem is very quickly fixed however as you can simply press a button in the gameplay menu that will fill the camps with enemies again and then teleports you back to the first base, which you unlock during a tutorial.
All in all, I would definitely recommend this game. It has a large amount of variety and a good amount of customization as well as an interesting story and one of gaming's best villains, which all come together to make one excellent game.

Deadlight is an old-school 2D platformer in the vein of Prince of Persia and Flashback, set in post-apocalyptic Seattle, in which you'll also have to either fight, or find your way around the zombies.
While the game isn't groundbreaking in
way, it entertained me while it lasted, despite having some clear mechanical flaws.
I've played it with a controller, since it's a console port, and most people seem to find the keyboard controls unintuitive and unresponsive.
Let's start with the presentation.
The
are certainly the highlight of Deadlight. Despite being a 2D game, every scene was completely done in 3D, creating really deep and detailed backgrounds that are great to look at, and provide a good atmosphere!
One issue some people may have is the color scheme, as everything is gray-ish brown, giving it the typical post-apocalyptic look. But there are a few points where the game is colorful during the main character's memories.
There are also some well put filters during the character's mental breakdowns.
Overall, the game looks really great! The cutscenes have a more comic book style, but they're still pretty good.
The
was very, very minimal from what I could tell. It added to the atmosphere, but it was too quiet for me to notice it too much. Which fits the kind of game that it is, I'd say, so nothing wrong sound-wise either.
A good addition is a bunch of
, and even a diary (that you complete by playing the game)! These certainly add value to the game, and give you a reason to explore the levels.
If you're generally interested in the developing process, have this in mind.
Well then, let's talk about the
.
This is where the game falls a bit short of expectations.
While it's not a bad game, it doesn't innovate all that much, and does feel all that great to control.
Mainly, you go from area to area by platforming around the place, running and jumping through roofs and cars, with the occasional indoor sections.
You'll have an Axe, a Revolver, and a Shotgun. Outside of that, you'll have to use the environment to kill or stall the zombies. And it works pretty well, in my opinion. I ended up playing too conservatively regarding ammunition, and made some situations harder on myself. While the game expects you to scavenge for ammo, you never really hold these weapons for long periods of time to make it matter too much.
One problem I've had overall, was that the controls were a bit clunky and unresponsive. They were slow, and while giving a feel of weight to the character's movements, it could get frustrating when you were stuck to an action that you knew was going to kill you.
And the platforming felt very similar. Everything was a bit too slow and heavy, and it's aggravated by far from perfect grasp on ledges and imprecise wall jumping.
Despite these shortcommings though, the game knew its limitations, and was very forgiving with its checkpoints (with an added Nightmare mode for beating each Act without using any checkpoints, after beating the game), so it didn't get to be very frustrating for me.
There was a significant delay between death and respawning that I could see getting annoying to many people. It's no Super Meat Boy in that regard. But it's not supposed to be, I'd say.
The game also breaks up the platforming and running away from zombies with some very simple puzzles. Nothing too complicated or dragged out, these consisted mainly of moving a box, unlocking a gear, etc.
One issue I've had with it, is when it comes to traps. Sometimes, the foreground and background blended a bit too much, which often led to death. And there was quite a bit of that. Some sections required trial and error instead of quick reflexes (since inertia is a very real thing in Deadlight), and it's generally not very good design.
But, outside of that, I think this is an entertaining game to play for a low price. It's short, it's not very innovative, but it's still a pleasant experience. I've found the plot to be very generic, but all the added collectibles, diary pages and other souvenirs manage to deliver it in a refreshing way.
There are much better games out there, but this is certainly not bad. If it looks like your cup of tea, give it a go!

Okay, first off, let me say that this isn't Hotline Miami 1's original formula, it has been modified. Most people who review and give it negative scores probably forget that.
Story: Great story, honestly, the character changing makes you hate certain characters and love others, and the role Richard plays is pretty awesome. Not much more to say except it's realllllllllllly out there at points, and some events will hurt you a bit.
Soundtrack: C'mon, it's a Hotline Miami game...
Performance: My computer isn't close to top of the line, but my R key always works and the game runs smooth, even better than the first Hotline Miami.
Gameplay: The part that actually matters. Many reviews are based on what Hotline Miami 1 is like to play now, where you know how to do it and you run around getting one giant combo score on a level's worth of enemies. When you start playing the first one though, it's still really ♥♥♥♥ing new to you, and you do scope out and take it a bit slow. Hotline Miami 2 makes you take it slow on your first playthroughs as well. I went back after playing a bit and did an early mission that I had struggled with and it played like Hotline Miami 1 does now. I've sunk well over 50 hours into HM1 (Finally just shortening it), but as there was that glitch removing steam overlay for a large portion of time after HM1's release, my profile doesn't reflect that. It's all new, and it takes getting used to. Isn't that what fans wanted? Something new? I will mention some gameplay negatives that can be frustrating at first until you accept them. The cursor is kinda locked to 67% of your screen around your character, so to actually aim at the area you want if it's far you must use shift, even if it was in your original vision. The shift look is also different, it's finicky at first, but gets better the more you use it. ♥♥♥♥ing windows (which allow enemies to see you, despite the portion being attached to a wall, a bit tricky to get used to) all over this place. There are also areas that can be shot over but still obstruct your movement, preventing traversal. Easy to spot places like this are tables, but sometimes set pieces like a ditch look like an elevated shed, and it really just depends on how you perceive it yourself until being told what it is by a bullet. The whole enemies shooting from offscreen thing can be a ♥♥♥♥♥, but it really just depends what frame of mind you are in when you play. You can't play this game while sad or angry, You'll just get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off by the constant death, and that will cloud judgement leading to more death. I was stuck on a level for a bit while mad, came back to it the next day and was able to be it in my 10 minute play window. Honestly, but the game if it looks interesting, do a bit of research, watch some gameplay, and keep what I've said in mind. You will ♥♥♥♥ing die a lot, your finger will get sore hitting R a lot, but you'll still have fun if you keep a level head. Oh, and forgot, the characters play differently too, so that changes your playstyle dependent on the character, keep that in mind too before you buy, if you don't like frequent change, you may hate this.
tl;dr It's good, has quirks, but it is good. Hell, nah, it's great, I love it, many will too. It will just take some getting used to even for experienced Hotline Miami players, so don't expect it to be like a bicycle where you just get on and go, this game is a motorbike and requires more learning.

To start: I used to add a much longer header to the reviews, but since it often made the review too long to submit, I've opted to leave it on my Backloggery.
Gameplay. This is a review I really haven't been looking forward to writing. Rather, this is a review in which I didn't have as many bad things to say about this game as I do. This is coming from someone who was quite a fan of the original Hotline Miami; in fact, I played it again about a week ago in preparation for this game and it's still as fantastic as ever. It had a near-perfect formula: go hard, hurt people, win game. I'd like to say that this game is just more of the same, but I just can't.   Hotline Miami 2 is practically a cover-based shooter now. As much as it pains me to say such a thing, it is the case now.
One of the main reasons why this is a problem is because of the absolutely gargantuan level design in this game. When I read the (somewhat notorious) PC Gamer review of this game, I looked at one of the grievances we share pertaining to the super huge levels and I thought, "Man... those guys are chumps. Big levels sounds awesome for this game!" It really isn't. One of the things in Hotline Miami 1's level design that I really liked was that the levels are designed in a very compact way; the levels are quick bursts of adrenaline, usually completable in about 20-30 seconds. Stages in this game can take upwards of three or more minutes. Add in the fact that you still die in one hit from *mostly* everything (pistols take two shots to kill which I'm alright with), and it can become really frustrating really quickly. Having to replay a pretty meaty section of a level just because of one little mistake you may or may not have been able to dodge, such as hitboxes for dogs kinda not working at times, someone shooting you off camera even with camera panning, etc.  for the thirtieth time just isn't fun.
When the game keeps its fairly compact  level design, it's almost always for the best. The most fun levels in the game are the ones that, as mentioned above, can be completed in a sub-minute rush. That doesn't mean that the levels have to be super easy to be fun; they just have to be non-tedious. Speaking of tedium, this game has multiple characters - or in some cases groups of characters - and most of them have gimmicks. Many of these characters are pretty alright, playing in much the same way that the main character from Hotline Miami 1 played, but there are a couple of characters which are straight up garbage tier; these two being the detective and the soldier. The detective can't pick up guns except for the part where he can... it's confusing, I know. Either way, his levels end up having some of the most egregious examples of this game turning into a cover based shooter in the game. The soldier is just a mess. He can use guns, but not the ones that the enemies use 'cuz I guess holding Russian weaponry would taint his American spirit or something i dunno. Instead, he gets ammo from ammo crates, of which there can be many crates but only one will arbitrarily open, and in fact in one level there is no ammo crates, which is pretty
terrible whenever there is an enemy in the upper right corner of the level which can only be killed with bullets. Another *fun* thing about the Soldier is that he only picks up a few bullets at a time, rather than stocking up on bullets all at once. Hey, tedious backtracking is fun right guys?
Again, when the game sticks to its roots it's a hell of a lot of fun. However, once it goes and becomes a cover-based shooter, it isn't fun. Even though my playthrough ended up at about six hours, I'd say that about three of those hours were me having fun and three not having fun and repeating tedious levels ad nauseum. Also keep in mind that just because the characters are alright, that may not mean that the levels are good. Ultimately the game becomes about half good and half bad, and the only reason why this game won't be getting below 5/10 from me is because the final level is easily the best thing Cactus has ever done ever. Still though, there's just too much garbage in this game to keep me from giving this game a higher score than what I will. 5/10.
Story: This game doesn't really have much of a story, per se; more like a collection of character studies joined by a common theme. Some of these stories aren't bad, but there are a few which are either incredibly cliched (the soldier is the biggest example) or just plain uninteresting (the Russians and the detective). Again, much like the gameplay section there are a few characters which do have some fairly interesting storylines, but all of the storylines are just so short that it ends up feeling fairly unsatisfying. Ultimately, the sheer amount of playable characters in this game ends up being to the story's detriment, mainly due to a lack of focus on the narrative's part. As for the overarching storyline... well, it ends. Satisfyingly? Not even close. It all felt like a cop out, which is something that I also really don't like having to say about this game. Hotline Miami 1 may not have had the Hollywood ending, but that was for the game's benefit; it was all about the futility of your actions, a character's willingness to commit atrocious acts of violence just from a phone call. This game continues that motif but doesn't really do anything with it, instead concluding with something along the lines of "oops i ended the story welp." Another major disappointment about this game. 5/10.
Graphics: Well, at least the pixel art is all well and good. There's a lot of very nice, subtle touches that the levels in Hotline Miami 1 just didn't have. These range from carousels actually turning to basketballs bouncing around to blood diffusing with water. It's all quite good. Stage design is pretty nice as well; not many stages look even close to another. There is something of a problem with enemies being hidden under scenery as well as lighting sometimes making the game much harder than it needs to be, causing a nightclub stage to be infintiely more frustrating than it needs to be. As for the technical details, it ran at a perfect 60FPS throughout, fullscreening my default to my native resolution but strangely rendering at a lower resolution for some reason. Either way, it was very easy to sort out under the options menu, and I was good from there. Very easy on the technical side as one would expect from a game like this. Overall, this game has much higher quality of pixel art than the predecessor, but some effects do have a tendency to make the game harder than it needs to be. 4/5.
Sound: It's Hotline Miami; of course the soundtrack is excellent. It's Hotline Miami; of course the sound design is excellent. 5/5.
Overall scores are: 5/5/4/5; cumulative score of 6.3/10. Ultimately this game's biggest problem is that it's so damned unfocused. Hotline Miami 1 was such a tight, cohesive game that it was hard to find any flaws in it. If it ain't broke, don't fix it after all. They tried to fix it, and they broke it in the process. Wait for a sale, I'd say. Unlike Hotline Miami 1, I don't see myself playing this game ever again. There's too much unfun material in here. I'm only marking this as recommended by virtue of the score; if you're a fan of Hotline Miami 1, I can't really recommend this on a subjective basis.

Far Cry 3 is a definite recommend. It is full of action, has an alright story, and some rather excellent gamepley. The skill tree has interesting perks, and it has a small modding community to help make gameplay more interesting, however this is definitely not need for a first playthrough.
The large variety of weapons yet limited carry capacity (Up to 4) can also lead to multiple playthroughs. I myslef started a second playthrough where I attempted to use pistols only.
My main problem with this game is that once you capture all the enemy bases, they stop spawning randomly around the world, and this ruins those few amazing moments at the start of the game where you have no weapons and have to hide from enemies as they drive past. This problem is very quickly fixed however as you can simply press a button in the gameplay menu that will fill the camps with enemies again and then teleports you back to the first base, which you unlock during a tutorial.
All in all, I would definitely recommend this game. It has a large amount of variety and a good amount of customization as well as an interesting story and one of gaming's best villains, which all come together to make one excellent game.

After a couple of hours into this game i decided to give my opinion on it in review form to help others decide over the course of the free/sale weekend [may not be on sale during time of reading]. Upon my journey to the review page i found many negative reviews and it left me shocked. For starters i did not play this game during beta so i am unaware to its supposed negative changes from beta to release that most negative reviewers criticize.
My first game in Contagion was a very positive experience, the other players helped each other and team work was apparent, but really I do not care for an online experience in a zombie game but rather its relation to gameplay, sound, and realism. So that is what i am going to cover.
GAMEPLAY [8/10]: As a zombie enthusiast I would say Contagion plays like a proper zombie survival game and it is up there in terms of ideas and gameplay. Shots to a walkers head is exciting and fun, guns feel real and its a joy to use them all, melee weapons feel powerful and are great to use in order to concerve ammo though can feel loose at first, and above all the atmosphere is great. Bunkering down in a house to find supplies, rushing yourself as a horde bashes its way in downstairs is a stand-alone amazing experience. Most times I found myself breaking a window and jumping out from a height to save my life rather than be eaten by the horde. The objective based gameplay in Contagion is also refreshing. The game has a minimul HUD, adding to the immersion, with the use of a phone as your source for guidance [whether it be a map or other players 'texting' each other their accomplishments]. Players do not also have the fear of a lowering health bar, but also the risk of infection that can turn an online game upside down for the better, maybe even leaving your team in a panic. Overall the gameplay is great and i honestly would not change it for anything nor compare it to another game or mod.
SOUND [7/10]: Sound design in Contagion is immersive and feels well put. Each gun has its own distinctive punch and sounds great put with the pop of a zeds head. However, sound related to melee can feel bland and does not seem to match the powerful feel of swinging a bat or axe, but nevertheless it works. Explosions are highly similar to most games using the source engine but are actually well put together [L4D being an example of 'loose' or 'laggy' explosions]. Atmospheric sounds and the groans of zeds are well placed and adds to the games immersion if wearing a headset. Breaking glass, banging on doors, and footsteps are other great sounds that adds to this games overall feel and atmosphere, causing an improved experience.

REALISM [9/10]: Gameplay and sound in Contagion add to its realism intensively; however, it is the games atmosphere that makes it feel real. The level design in Contagion reveals the time and effort the dev team put into making the game. Zombies wonder the streets aimlessly and it is easy to make your way around the map in silence rather than running and gunning like most of todays zombie 'survival' games that they claim to be. The games lighting is dark and positively empty, causing the player to use the flash light which, at times, can be a pain that blinds the player but 8 times out of 10 it is an effective tool. Pickups in the game are randomly placed and can lead the player in finding items that are alien to them or endlessly searching for ammo. Overall the atmosphere of Contagion is bleak, dark, and quite scary if played correctly [no running and gunning]. It feels like an apoclypse has took place.

If you're a zombie fanatic looking for an authentic experience, pick this game up. If you're a zombie fanatic looking for a co-op experience like L4D do not buy this, you will be dissappointed. If you're not a zombie fanatic, Contagion is a good starting point for you. The one thing I would like to see from this game is a supported community of modders that actively create maps and content to upload onto the workshop on a regular basis, creating endless hours of enjoyment. Overall Contagion feels real and authentic and it is the kind of objective based zombie survival game I enjoy with friends. I give this game an 8/10. Got this game recently and am rather enjoying it.  It is presently in alpha version a0.8 at the time or writing this, so some of its bugs are bound to work themselves out.
It's part RPG, part voxel builder, part engineering CAD developer, part 4X, part tower defense, all exploration and adventure.  I have been utterly absorbed in playing it for the last few days.  I have one beef with it, though.  Companions.
Throughout normal gameplay, you get tag-alongs, whether you want them or not.  You cannot control them, and they are basically along for the ride.  They are mostly benign, and will even SOMETIMES help with combat (which is nice because they cannot die like the 'hired' companions can).  There are some issues, though.
The first is the pathfinding A.I.  If you are not EXTREMELY careful with where you are going, any following monster bait will get stuck... in a hole, on a tree, in the water, on a herd of turtles.  You can either clear their obstructions so they can get unstuck, or you can build an advanced piece of machinery like a car with spare seats, and HOPE they teleport to the seat.
The next issue with these hoodlums is the fast travel system.  Let's say you have a waypoint that happens to be in the direction of your next quest spot(which itself is a 35 minutes walk), or just somewhere else you want to go for supplies.  If you are babysitting, you are not allowed to use this mechanism in the game without automatically aborting the quest which demands their presence.  Often, they don't go back to where you got the quest, either.  Nope.  They park themselves right there and wait.  And then you have to go find them again if you manage to get the quest once more.
I'm not saying this makes the game bad or unplayable.  But, if a game developer insists on an underwater escort quest, they had better take some special measure to ensure that you don't have to spend an hour fighting water mechanics to dig out a quest giver stuck in a wall.
That's it.  Just the NPCs.  Everything else about the game has drool running out of the corner of my mouth.

Disclaimer: I cannot abide the competitive Call of Duty multiplayer scene, and avoid it. This review does not touch on the competitive multiplayer component.
Single Player: In the fashion of the later Call of Duty games, there are incredibly long portions of each mission during which you have no control of your character, and are forced to listen to dialogue or look at scenery.
The portions that you actually DO get to control your character are so narrow, linear, and short, that they are hardly worth mentioning. While there are some neat moments, they only appear once, briefly during the campaign, making it feel like a string of set pieces.
As for the story, it is laughable and unbelievable. I'd say it breaks the immersion, but the game never even lets you get immersed in the first place. I found myself not being able to relate to any of the characters, or finding any of them sympathetic. I'm also not sure if anyone vetted the absurd dialogue before recording it.
Extinction: Aliens made it into Call of Duty! This mode can be fun, if you have a competent team. There is no tutorial on the mechanics of this mode, so seeing new people running around, making things harder, can be difficult to watch sometimes. It can be brutally hard for new players, or teams with new players. It is nice in that it does not have the completely random feel of the competitive multiplayer, but is not just a string of set pieces and cutscenes like the campaign.
Overall: Ghosts plays like a bad action movie, and there is even less gameplay here than previous installments.

Okay, I'm writing this review because the game is currently on the cheap right now, but if you want it and miss it this time, my review will be out there for the next sale. Don't get this game unless you get it really cheap: $3-5 U.S. tops. I'm running this review off of my memories of playing the game several months ago. It definitely left an impression, so let's get on with it.
I'm not writing a really long review this time. Just the basics. It's pretty simple really. Deadlight is an atmospheric side-scroller. You have obstacles in the form of environmental hazards, zombies, unfriendlies, and, of course, obstacles which you must hurdle, climb, dodge, slide past, leap, and time to avoid/survive. There is a very loose storyline that is way too predictable, so if that matters to you, you may just want to skip it. The graphics/atmosphere are actually okay for what it is. Overall the game is a pretty typical side-scrolling platformer, but there are a few pleasant surprises and only a few irritatingly, mind-numbingly, platformer-typical moments of inane aim-twitch-jerk-with-just-the-right-timing @55hat-ery/@55clown-ery. Some odd bits are thrown in for flavor, but mostly I found these elements annoying and distracting from what the game does well. It's almost a runner, somewhat parkour, somewhat zombie survival, with moments dedicated to each of these elements. Think post-apocalyptic urban Indiana Jones/ninja and you might be getting close to the feel of this game. Some elements are too trite and stereotypical to the genre, and there is very little replay value, BUT for a few hours of pleasant distraction it's decent. I recommend it; just don't spend more than what you'd pay for an okay cup of coffee and you'll be alright. And that's about what it's worth to me, a decent cup of coffee: not great, not awesome, but pleasant enough for the short time you spend with it, and it will pump you up a bit, but not too too much. And, although it should pleasantly distract you for considerably longer than that cup, at least you won't have to worry about it getting cold before you've finished with it.

*This review is based off an older version, around .72 alpha build
First off. Let me start with performance.
I do not lag on this game on any settings and with my computer underclocked. And it still looks wonderful.
Let me restate that,.... Space Engineers(on any world older than a day), Minecraft(for most people), 7 days to die, + any other game you can think of that is voxel based..... Planet Explorers not only looks better, but handles better.
Nuff said.
Music/sound: needs more variety if they are still on the same tracks as the last version I played. But for what they do have, the music is refreshing and fits right in. It is not intrusive at all. Sound had wierd glitches here and there, but stuff that was actively getting fixed and nothing that really stood out.
animation/combat: I am clumping these two together for a reason,... they are closely tied for the trouble parts. Overall its pretty good, both the animation and the combat. But something about combat makes me feel more like I am aiming for hit boxes and not an actual entity. I do not like this in the slightest, so even tho I would like to be a melee combatant, I feel forced into ranged combat because of this.
*I believe theres been some changes to combat that may effect my opinion on this, I will change my review to reflect more recent versions as I play them*
Scenery: Yes, this one warrants its own section. The landscape of Planet Explorers is beautiful. And the variety of foliage(trees, grass, bushes, flowers) is beyond what any other game I have played has attempted
Creatures: Again, something that I might not have commented on in any other game... Planet Explorers creature deserve a mention. The variety and detail put into the creatures is astonishing. And they keep adding more! I did 3 'Main' playthroughs of the storymode for this game before the last version- and EVERY time there was more creatures that I hadnt seen before! Someone in their department is pumping them out, and I am loving it!
Story: The story is actually pretty good if you pay attension to what is going on(i.e. dont skip thru text)
The presentation certainly is not winning any awards, but as far as I am concerned, it doesn't have to. What is nice here is that in storymode(singleplayer), the story is not shoved down your throat. You are free to pursue the story, or do your own thing.
Survival Aspect: This is a survival game after all, and thats what most of us(or at least me) come to do. And I must say that on the version I played, I wasnt as impressed as I hoped. It felt like survival was optional, and that should never be the case in a survival game. I don't know if that makes any sense, but... not hardcore enough for me? maybe.
Good news is I heard there is an editor thing planned that from what details I heard, will definately be able to accomidate anything I feel is missing here.
Developers: This one is of special note. I have never before PE seen a head of development for a game interact with the community, on a near daily basis. Furthermore, in the time I spent observing and partaking in the forums I have not seen so much straightforwardness and honestly from developers. This is both commendable and heartwarming. I will not provide examples, as they stand on the forums for all to see.
Also, it is easy to tell these developers actually care about their game.
Summary: It's a great game and only getting better,... I couldn't recommend it more. If still in doubt, try out the demo. I insist! Do the storymode first... the other modes are farther behind and don't accurately represent what the dev's are trying to accomplish.
**Note: I will update this review as I play newer versions.... anything here will likely change for the better.

I will make this review the most fair I can for people considering to buy this game:
This game is very similiar in mechanics of other games such as Starbound and Minecraft but with it's own style. The game is still in early Alpha but with the new update I can see that this developer is providing good updates. What makes the game fun is the ability to create, fight and explore in a procedurally created enviroment. I really like the ability of allowing players to create their own custom weapons, allowing lots of creativity. Some of the ISO's (files that save the design of the custom gun or vehicle) people have created are absurdly cool (recreated vehicles of famous movies). I haven't tried multiplayer but I can see how much fun that will be by allowing games such as free for all or capture the fort, or survival (agaist other players or a creature siege). A lot is still a work in progress however. I can tell the developers are working more on the game engine mechanics. Other things such as more character custimization, more eyecandy,  is for later updates. I will try to list some notable qualities currently in the recent build:

- Has some buffers regarding Health and Stamina
- Full open creation of guns and vehicles (cars, helicopters, and now includes making boats and a monorail)
- Many recipes to create objects in game (materials to create items such as weapons, food, certain resources, etc)
- You have to search your resources (esp ores). Don't expect to dig randomly to find ores. Use your scanner to locate ore deposits.
- You can farm your own crops.
- Fast travel is allowed (starting colony only at the moment though)
- Very large maps (huge in my opinion) and you can also mark and label locations on map.
- Animal AI is getting better (pack hunting and herding). It's like you are on Pandora (from Avatar) but you are poaching every living animal and you use their meat as currency (At the moment...it might change, I am speculating) to buy items and resources if you don't wish to create everything yourself.
- You can have NPC followers and create your own base and assign them jobs. This is still a work in progress however, IDK how much progress  they made in version A.08
Remember that this is an EARLY ACCESS GAME! Saves can be compromised when updating the game, glitches still exist, the are many areas left to finish. The game itself at its current build is very enjoyable though. So far it hasn't crashed on me yet or have encountered any glitches or game breaking bugs.

Planets Explorers is a vast world of discovery, creation, and survival. This game is simply too complex to describe in just a few words. This review will be a challenge to write, as the game just has so much to offer.
Planet Explorers is a survival sandbox adventure game developed by Pathea Games.  While the survival sandbox genre might seem oversaturated, Planet Explorers has several features that make it stand apart from similar titles.
First, there is the Story Mode – a single player campaign experience, complete with numerous quests that send you out into the awe-inspiring world to create your own adventure. Collect resources, fight fantastic monsters and aliens, battle giant bosses, explore the huge map…This is the game mode I spent the most time on, and during my time in Story Mode, I learned how the game worked via the starter quests. It showed me how to use and equip items, how to use the crafting system via the Replicator and Scripts, and how to use the very powerful Creation System to make and edit weapons, tools, objects, and even vehicles.
The Replicator is very simple to use. First, you need a “script” for the item or tool you want to create. Think of it as a blueprint, which tells you what resources you need to craft a given item. Scripts can be bought from shops or obtained from quests. Once you have the script for an item, you can use it to learn the recipe for the item indicated on the script. There are Scripts for nearly everything, from weapons and tools, to medicines and clothing.
Next, we have Adventure Mode. In Adventure Mode, you are placed in a randomly generated world with random quests, missions, bosses, landscapes, and enemies. It still has the survival elements of every other mode. What this means is each time you play Adventure Mode it gives you a brand new experience. No two playthroughs will be the same!
Finally, we have Build Mode. This is the mode for the creatively inclined. All the resources you could want, in infinite supply, at your fingertips! There are no monsters or aliens in this mode, and full terrain destruction is allowed. This mode is ideal for trying out new builds, vehicles, and objects with the Creation System.
Wow, that’s a lot, isn’t it? But wait! The fun doesn’t stop there!
Planet Explorers also has Multiplayer! You can host and/or join servers with friends to enjoy the world of Planet Explorers together! Multiplayer has 2 different modes: Co-Op and Versus. In Co-Op mode you join up with friends to explore the world and create fantastic structures and objects together. In Versus Mode, you are put on a team of up to 16 players against another team, each earning points for kills, resourced mined, and objects built.
The game is currently in Early Access on Steam, and is actually an early alpha build. But it is stuffed full of content for you to enjoy! You’d never guess it was in alpha if it didn’t tell you on the title screen.

After having played through the base game and just barely scratching the surface of Hard Mode, I can truly say that this was a great game. It's rare when I find difficulty picking exactly which elements I liked more, the gameplay or the story.
The gameplay is as chaotic and deadly as ever, and if you're a veteran of Hotline Miami you'll find yourself immersed right away as this game pulls no punches from the start. Levels are generally more open, so the game is less about going on a reckless rampage and more about planning the right execution for your rampage. You can't "improvise" as much as in Hotline Miami 1, but the combat still flows quickly and brutally. The game certainly rewards those who are skilled enough to do everything on the fly, and altogether finishing a level is a satisfying experience. My only problems with the gameplay are that it's difficult to keep up a combo since executions are now much slower, and certain characters' skills make keeping up a combo incredibly difficult due to having to wait for the animation to finish to execute an enemy (Detective Pardo and your fancy shotgun flip, I'm looking at you!). A feature to zoom out and get a glance at the whole floor would also be nice, with an associated aiming restriction of course. Other than that, the gameplay is great and there's plenty of new elements for returning players. New players may want to start with the first game though.
The story was also surprisingly good, beyond my expectations, when everything started to come together towards the end I found myself piecing together the characters and their relations to one another and the significance of the events of the first game. Some plots are less-developed than others (the Midnight Animal one stands out in that regard) but overall the story is quite the ride and well worth it, even without the excellent gameplay. Simply brilliant.
I have to also give my honourable mentions to the soundtrack, which is even better than the first game and the rhythm behind the game's cycle of death (mostly yours). The few frustrating levels are made more bearable due to the soundtrack, driving you onwards with its crazy synth beats and setting the dreamlike and bizarre atmosphere.
Altogether an amazing game and well worth the price at release. I strongly endorse this for any Hotline Miami fan who was either intrigued by the story or looking for an extra challenge, because a challenge you will certainly get with this game. Replayability is also immense, with an unlockable hard mode and plenty of opportunities to replay a level to try and get that perfect score.
Overall, 9/10. I heartily endorse this game.

After playing ~2hrs, the initial opinion about the game is great. The game feels directly influenced by "Left 4 Dead" series. Characters are varied and each character has a unique feel and their own specific inventory. Melee combat feels really fluid, something similar to what  I've seen in games like Shadow Warrior or Chivalry. Ranged combat also feels responsive and satisfying, when you blow away a horde of rats with a blunderbuss, it's definitely a sight worth admiring. Gore is not on the level of let's say Killing Floor 2, but it's sufficient. Gorehounds will still be happy.
There are various "special" enemies like in L4D, but some of them are more interesting and do more interesting stuff, rather that just attack you blindly. The Gutter Rat is almost a carbon copy of "The Hunter" but the rat is a lot more elusive, it jumps from various angles and also evades ranged weapon fire, uses smoke to disorient and so on. Don't want to describe other types of enemies, because it's more fun to find out on your own. However, if you have played Left 4 Dead at some point, most types of "special" Skaven won't be completely new to you. Can't comment too much myself, since I've still yet to experience most of what the game has to offer.
Artstyle of the game has a unique feel to it, but it's no wonder because it's based on the Warhammer franchise. Perfomance on an AMD card is somewhat choppy, game sometimes dips below ~40fps on High settings with R9 280X. But I've yet to install latest AMD beta drivers and the game is still technically in Beta, so there's definitely room for improvement.
TL;DR - If you like co-op games that take you through a level with random enemy spawns and random consumable spots. Get this game. Also there's RNG loot and a crafting system. If you like grindy games, this will definitely become one of your favorites.

I sit here questioning if I want to recommend this game. I do love it, but I really hate it too. Hotline Miami was a favorite of mine.  This is a solid dual stick shooter, but it hardly feels like the original. I see a lot of people saying "if you like the first one, you'll LOVE this one" I disagree.
The levels are a lot more open, meaning you'll be shot off screen a lot. New "jumper" enemies and dog AI seem to be able to jump through walls and can auto kill out of the reach of melee weapons and duck under guns. The game added a lot of more guns but melee weapons are lacking. The sense of progression is removed because now you can't pick masks before each job and while I enjoyed the new characters many felt pointless. The "Bear" for instance is awful and forces you to run through the ammo in the dual guns he starts with before being able to use other weapons. Which means stealth is thrown out the window. The game also seems to have "more weapons" but that hardly seems the case. There are more guns, and more items limited to specific "scenes" and characters, but there are definately less items spread across each map level to level. There is a severe a lack of thrown weapons and a lack of interesting melee weapons, the katana is gone (only as a character specific item) I felt like there was really only the bat, pipes, machete, baton, knife, and fire ax (which if I recall is only on 1 level)
The "Soldier" character and the Writer character embody the problem I have with the game. The soldier is forced to use a starting gun and knife ONLY no pickups, no throwing weapons, all his levels are massive open areas where you're shot by off screen enemies and forced to use your gun which ruins your planned out rhythmic melee killing spree. The writer takes away guns and knives, because he doesn't kill people (unless you execute 2 downed enemies by beating them to death over a long period of time). These characters feel out of place because they force a type of gameplay. Many other levels in the game do this as well, where you feel you don't have options because certain tactics are forcibly removed or heavily pushed on you. Hotline Miami didn't do this to the extent its sequal does. Many of the characters lack diversity where as in HL all the masks gave you an ability but all tactics where still valid. For instance the new Tony mask still give you auto-kill fists but takes away the ability to use weapons.  For those who have played the original game, imagine having to play as Biker for most of the game and never playing Jacket. Stuck with your knives the whole time.
The story is really the focus here though. And it is nice to have some twists on what goes on in the first game.  I enjoyed seeing what would happen next and it is probably the best part of the game. Its simutaneously more cryptic and more clear this time around. Pay attention to the time stamps before each level, it gets confusing because you keep going back and forward in time, sometimes playing in the 90's, late 80's, or early 80's. I won't spoil anything but the ending is fantastic! Dennaton really wanted you to know this is the LAST Hotline Miami game they are making.
The game is buggier than HL1 as well. Enemies often get stuck running in circles, jumping through walls (as previously mentioned) getting stuck in door ways and becoming invincible. The Swan characters pathing is awful, the character with the gun often getting stuck behind and becoming useless.
I suppose I can't help but still like it. But don't expect your skills from the first to roll over too well. I found myself relying on guns a lot more because of all the open maps. The well planned murder routes are far and few between, this game instead forces you to play each level the way THEY want you to play, not the way you want to, this is evident in the characters you play as often being so restrictive. A lot of deaths feel unfair, where I always understood what I did wrong in HL1, in 2 I found myself feeling jipped. I suppose its worth buying with the promise of a level editor. But save you're money until then.

Take this for what its worth because I barely played the game before posting this review. I read several reviews and most were negative, but it was free to play for the weekend so I figured what do I have to lose?. I tried the game out since it was free to play until 9/1/2014. It's only $4.99 until then as well, but after my brief game play (solo mind you) I wouldn't even spend the $4.99. If this was early access, I would buy it in a heart beat for $4.99 (not for $19.99). This game feels really unpolished and not complete.
A few complaints to point out why this seems early access and is not polished and why I wouldn't recommend buying it since they market it as a finished game:
1. A lot of zombies seem to just randomly be walking against a wall and don't notice you until you attack them (they seem glitched out).
2. I found a lot of ammo lying around, and although they are all slightly different there is no HUD message or text display when hovering over the ammo telling you what type it is. So you might pick it up (assuming you want to scavenge whatever you find) and then realize its not even ammo for the gun you're carrying (i.e. Sig, 1911, etc..)  I didn't play mutli player, but I could see this as problematic if you pick up ammo for a weapon your coop friend(s) was / is using. Maybe this isn't a problem in multi player coop mode, but I just found it to feel "not finished".
3. You have 4 inventory slots. As you pick up items it fills the next spot. I think I tried out the Escape game mode so I started with two weapons in slots 1 and 2 (melee and then pistol respectively). I then picked up a first aid kit filling slot 3. Then a shotgun filling slot 4. Cool. Well yes cool until you use the first aid kit up making slot 3 empty and then it moves the shotgun from slot 4 to 3. Not a big deal, but definitely could be problematic if you're in the middle of combating a horde of zombies and realize the shotgun you thought was in slot 4 is no longer there.
4. On the map I played (which was an office building, and which I thought was actually a pretty cool map) there are auto sliding doors. I got caught on a few and slid to the side with the door. Not a big deal if it was a custom map, or in development but "no bueno" in a game that is supposedly finished and normally sells for $19.99.
5. Animations to me felt very rough. The kind of rough you see in Mods for other games, and live with because you know the person either added the mod in their spare time as a hobby / project, and most likey will improve if they are capable. Not the kind of thing you would expect these days from a finished game.

Solid idea, terrible execution. While I love the Prince of Persia-esque 2D platforming, the game is plagued by a myriad of problems, such as:
- A boring story with a plot twist so predictable that you can see it a mile away.
- Awful voice-acting (although this one can be forgiven due to the indie developers).
- Wonky controls that'll cause you to die and restart every now and then because you missed a jump or didn't roll in time or something else.
- Huge number of bugs, some of them game-breaking (no audio in cutscenes, getting stuck in elevators, being unable to interact with items, just to name a few).
- Problems with certain game mechanics (such as being unable to tell which zombies are in your "plane" and which are in the background, which is bound to result in several frustrating deaths and restarts).
- Short running time - it took me only three hours to finish it and I was taking my time to find secrets. Without thoroughly exploring it, I'd probably finish the game in two hours.
All in all, unless you're getting it in a bundle or at a severe discount, I wouldn't recommend buying it.

Fantastic game. Stunning graphics with a breathtaking island, long list of varied and extremely impressive animals, interesting story, strong characters, lots of varied activities, easy to use controls, enormous landscape to explore. Extremely immersive and entertaining. The animals are as lethal as the people, and are beautifully rendered and believable.
On top, is the prophecy-type rise to 'power' which has Jason becoming not only a disturbingly talented killer, but also a symbol of hope to his friends, and fear to his enemies. Perhaps I should mention not a game for the squemish - if you don't like playing hunting and killing, this isn't the game for you.
What sets this game apart is the slight quirkiness, it's got a character and charm all it's own, and Far Cry 3 immediately won me over. Vaas is a particularly charismatic villain and though you obviously want him dead, he is an extremely memorable bad guy. He's crazy and is a little over the top, it all works. If this had been your normal FPS, I would probably have gotten bored, but the off-beat story and characters make sure that doesn't happen.
Though there are two endings, this isn't a game affected by your choices so from a main story POV, there isn't really replay value... however, due to the very large amount of things to do, and the sheer amount of loot and list items to complete, you could easily play it for a very long time, with or without the main questline.
Worth every penny, one of the most enjoyable games I've every played. Honestly, if Far Cry 4 tops this, I will be stunned (and delighted).

Vermintide - Hordemode done right!
Well, I personally enjoy the game a great deal even in it's unoptimized, content lacking and repetitive state.
I guess the repetitiveness is kinda-sorta tied to this genre. However, I totally feel like the crafting and therefore character customization act as a hard counter to that "problem".
