Deadlight, another game set in a post-apocalyptic world full of zombies? Yes, but how much fun was to play it!!
This is a platformer where you play as Randall, a survivor who's trying to reach Seattle in order to find his wife and daughter, lost after the disaster. On his road through run-down and abandoned suburbs, he will find hate, hope and madness, all seasoned with a good amount of undead.
Gameplay is based on survivor skills and environmental puzzle solving, but ferocious combat is not missing and Randall will be able to use an axe, a pistol and a shotgun (do I need to list also the slingshot?). Not that much you will say, and I would agree, except that the game is not very long to finish (4-5 hours), so I think the amount of differentiation between weapons, amount of levels and types of enemies is just right.
It is clear that originally Deadlight was intended as a low budget indie title, and it is a shame that the developer had no more resources in order to extend and deepen Randall's personal story, maybe with more flashbacks from his past, or even only with more levels, enemies and weapons. 2.5 graphics are just perfect to represent this diseased world full of oppressive atmospheres, and the main musial theme is really awesome, so moody!!
Do not let the abused zombie theme fool you, Deadlight is a nice game if you like the genre, it offers the right amount of contents and fun for its price. Now I just need to understand if I want to deal with the just unlocked Nightmare mode :)

First off I would like to say this is a very unique twist on sand box, voxel based games. And for those saying it's just a copy of a game, I say this to you... If we did not have game copies people would be forced to play a version of the game they don't like. So called "copies" add some variation that is important in order to find the game that has just the mechanics that make it the best. Do you really want to be stuck playing Doom?
Second: I will not go on about graphics or anything for that matter because it is still in alpha, but, I think it would be nice to add more surcical type things to the game, such as campfires. Now I haven't been playing to long so Im not sure how much of this stuff is actually in there but I felt like if that stuff would be anywhere, it would be at the beginning.
Finally, I have one complaint abou the revival shot, I have found myself not using it because I respawn, and die again, if you could add a mechanic such as in Star Wars The Old Republic where you are invisible to enemys for a time long enough for you to retreat, If this disrupts balance simply make them a little bit pricier.
I recommend this game and I am excited for features coming soon!

Finally!  A totally open world game which allows infinite possibilities.  This game is delivering upon the potential of the ambitious concept. I cant recommened it highly enough.
You want an open world game?.  This game allows you to do almost anything.  You gather resources,   many types of resources.  You can make everything and anything. You can use pre made designs. Download others designed by players or design your own from scratch.   The only limit I found is that I couldnt build the nuclear missiles I wanted.  Battleship? Fine.  Stealth fighter, fine.  Motorbike, Star wars style land speeder, Monster trucks and madcap mash ups all fine.  Works really well.
You want base building?  You can do anything.  Thought the style is a little tiny bit limiting it is vast.  It is somewhere between the complexity of Landmark (which most people cant use well) and other games with more simiplified base building such as Ark.  A nice middleground allowing the free use of imagination to create some awesome settlements towns and fortified structures.  Great fun and probably the thing I get most distracted by.  I am crazy about base building in games like this and Ark.
You want to explore?  Ok, 2 sides to this.  It is a massive area to explore. You will soon realise you need to develop and get vehicles though nothing stops you wandering on foot.   Hostile alien races and local wildlife abound and the whole thing feels very nicely balanced.  It doesnt feel like a world setup to support your game but a world you literally found yourself in and now you have to survive and thrive.  This works well too.
Sound?  I love the title theme loop (now with some beautiful vocals to make it one of the best game themes I can remember) and the in game sounds are all well done.  I think overall the sound effects could havemore attention to atmospherics but it is a small criticism and it was done well enough not to be any sort of problem.   One absolutely stand out moment is the (in my opinion) very beautiful opening title music.  It really sets a nice an atmosphere and is a beautiful piece of music in its own right.   I wish it was a longer track as I like it a lot.
Probably the only real criticism I have is the NPCs in the game.  They just seem like props.  This was a lost opportunity.  If they actually went and did more with astmospheric sounds supporting it, settlements would have felt much more alive.   This is not a major issue because of the nature of the game,. later they will be doing stuff at your direction but for a long time they feel less alive.
Graphical?  Erm. Interesting one this, It uses nothing in terms of the capability I have, yet somehow, strangely, it is enough. Its not great, it's not bad. Its passable.  This is odd for me as I am a bit of a state of the art graphics guy.  I am a bit split on my opinion on this point. I would have loved it to be way better looking but, I find I like the game so much it bothers me far less than it normally would and I am glad of a game that doesnt use the Unreal engine.  (An engine which was popular but gets on my nerves for many reasons).
I should say, that the only relatively limited aspect is character creation but this is not a big deal, though I try to stay in first person.
I have been having a smooth experience for a while for the most part but there does seem to be a few serious bugs still in the game but not so many that it stops me playing and miles ahead of many other games.
This is a game you will have installed for years and will keep coming back to.  Bang for buck, fun and for the open world nature of the game, I cant recommend this enough to people who like;
Open World
Resource Gathering
Settlement Building and Development
Designing Vehicles and Equipment
Exploration
Longevity and good value.

This is a magnum opus and you should all be very justifiably proud of yourselves.   I dont think I have ever been so effusive in my praise for any game and nor would I be if it did not deserve it.

Very dark and atmospheric. A lot of thought went into the little things, like the backgrounds, use of lighting and pacing. Randall's animations are very well done, as well. I've read some complaints about the voice acting - while I admit it's pretty broad and more like a characature at times, it fits with the style of the game.
Reading lots of griping about the controls, but again, I disagree. I found the controls, for the most part, fine, when playing with a controller. Didn't even try mouse and keyboard because I knew the game wouldn't lend itself to that control scheme.
I'll defend the story while I'm at it too. I didn't come into this expecting a deep, moving story, so I wasn't disappointed. The story
especially linear and there's absolutely no reason to replay the game, but for a 5-6 hour run-through you won't need more story.
The majority of the experience is pain-free as far as puzzle-solving and platforming go. The last third is a
. I mean, it can get downright infuriating. It's almost as if the developers were trying to lengthen the time it would take to beat the game, so they incorporated unfair "gotcha" moments you'd have to replay a dozen times to get through certain sections. I found myself progressing at a snail's pace thanks to the myriad die-reload loops. Thankfully, the time between checkpoints is somewhat short.
The time it takes to beat Deadlight is relatively short, but again, I paid 3 bucks for it, so I still feel like I got my money's worth out of it. The ending felt somewhat lame, but after the frustration of the last third I was happy to be done.
Again, I recommend it, but only if you can grab it at a steep discount.

The skill cap in this game is MUCH higher than similar games which I believe will allow this game to outlive some others that fell short here.

If you can find 3 other people, whether you meet in game or know already to form a group, ANYTHING is possible. Contagion, in it's current beta version, already has a solid core gameplay. It takes on a slightly more realistic approach to a team zombie survival game as opposed to Left 4 Dead (2). The gameplay is limited to what your average human being would be capable of in a zombie apocalypse, meaning that players have to deal with stamina, scarce ammunition (I'm not kidding, it's hard to find ammo in this game), and hordes of relentless zombies that are difficult to destroy unless you shoot them in the head. Headshots are typical in a zombie meta but it's an idea that works, especially with how Contagion is designed: You either shoot them in the head once or you waste ammo shooting them anywhere else until they go down. There is, of course, an exception when dealing with the zombified SWAT officer otherwise known as the "Riot Zombies," who wear kevlar helmets making them priority targets.
Unfortunately, like all beta's the game can be quite buggy. Dropping your weapon by accident could prove to be more dangerous than a zombie horde since they can glitch through the ground. They also have a chance of flying across the screen if you don't aim down to drop them. The biggest complaint I have so far is the lag. Contagion's servers aren't the most reliable despite having many dedicated servers but on the off chance that the network is stable for all players, it is really fun to play.
All in all, it's an enjoyable game with multiple game modes that have good replay value. It maybe a bit challenging for newbies in the begining but once you get the hang of aiming, it all boils down to how you keep up with your supplies while accomplishing objectives at the same time. Also being able to play with up to 8 people also adds to the game's fun factor.

This game's reputation confused me quite a bit. All of the reviews I saw were either harshly negative or highly positive. I bought this for a dollar while it was on sale and it proved that it was more than worth it.
I'll go through the good first. This game has an amazing atmosphere and unique style that's pleasing to the eye and very inspiring. The soundtrack is pleasing as well, adding to the horror feeling of the game.
While many people bash the level desgin, I feel that the design was put together well and kept me on my toes the whole time. The controls aren't nearly as bad as people say either - and I play on a relatively low-end PC (so if anything, it should be worse for me)!
The story is decent, not amazing but certainly better than many of the generic titles out there. The protagonist's narration is not infrequent, but not intrusive, either, and his voice appeals to the ears, making him a likable character from the start. During the game, the cinematics are in a unique artstyle and the animation of the in-game models is superb, making for some notably awe-inspiring moments.
Now for the bad. This game is very buggy,  often allowing you to get into places you aren't supposed to be and triggering events before they're supposed to happen (Crashes and freezes aren't a problem, however). The combat system, while unique, can be frustrating at times, and once or twice I got stuck at a certain segment of the game because I could not figure out how to proceed. Some speed-run segments tend to be paced poorly and require you to try multiple times because the event expects you to finish at an almost unrealistic speed. As with many platformers, there are some places that are difficult to jump-between and will have you trying again and again until you jump at the right time.
Note that this game is mostly a storytelling experience, and can be rather short if you speed through it.
Overall, I believe this game is worth what I paid for it, and perhaps up to $10, maybe even $14.99 if you have the money lying around. It was certainly a welcome change from the typical style-dry titles that are common today.

This is pretty much what happens nine months after you put Left4Dead and Warhammer Fantasy into a room, turn the light down, pour them some wine, turn some soft music on and close the door. It's gory, it's grimm and it's hard as it is fun.
If you  like Warhammer or L4D or melee combat...or killing stuff, or killing stuff with other stuff, you're going to enjoy this one.
However you won't like it if you're not able resist the urge to smash your screen in when you lose a level. And you will lose. Often. But as with anything Warhammer, losing is fun!

Yes, yes and yes, I haven't been this smitten by a game in a long time.
Vermintide wears it's obvious Left 4 Dead inspiration on it's sleeve, however it's set in the oft underused Warhammer Fantasy setting; features a horde of angry, plagued and militant rat men instead of zombies and has a heavy focus on melee combat instead of ranged.
While it may not have the same depth as some other first person melee games, it makes up for it with extremely satisfying animations and sound effects while still retaining a subtle degree of complexity. You will need to learn to use charge attacks, pushblock and
, without those nuanced skills you will find yourself taking alot of needless damage. Ranged weapons are primarily utility, as ammunition can be scarce. However, swapping between melee and ranged weapons is very quick with your only limitation being the associated weapon's reload speed, allowing them to be used reflexively based on the situation (such as taking out that pesky Ratling Gunner on the roof).
The game advertises "mountains of shiny loot", which will flip a switch in some people (myself included). Don't come into this game expecting an action RPG, don't expect to have a "main character" that you level up exclusively, don't come into this thinking the main point of the game is to grind for loot. This is Left 4 Dead, you play the game because you find it
. Unlike L4D you will have a chance at earning loot upon successfully completing a level which can be used only by a specific character, but you won't always get an item for the one you are playing. This is likely to encourage you to try out different characters.
I point this out because many people are understandably miffed by how heavily RNG focused the loot system is, comparing it to Destiny. Unfortunately it seems alot of these (valid) criticisms are made by people who are putting the loot first and the game second, perhaps because they had the wrong idea about what this game's design philosophy seems to be.
if you want an extremely competent and challenging co-op FPS game with an atypical melee focus and are willing to put the loot as a secondary motivator for playing instead of the primary one, I
recommend you pick this one up.

As a steady consumer of the hack-and-slash multiplayer arena that has become so popular in the past couple of years starting in my memory with the original Chivalry Mod for Half-Life. The evolution of the genre has been labored at times, with back-steps and side-steps, but Fatshark was able to learn from the lessons of the previous installments (War of the Roses, War of Vikings) and expand upon previous ideas to settle into a combat system that is both visceral and engaging. Shying away from standard directional attacks it is instead broken down into Light Strikes, Heavy Strikes and the character movements therein for spins and greater fineness, along with a dodge component that really starts to show its utility at the higher tiers of difficulty.
As far as the storyline goes, most of what you learn is via the natural progression of quips and comments from the characters involved in this foray into the world of Warhammer, which is a grim-dark sojourn through a crumbling city infested with jabbering Skaven. It’s nice to see that a developer can make the formula work without jumping on the zombie train, and Skaven haven’t really had any prevalence in any other Warhammer medium thus far (to my knowledge) so this is probably the best possible first appearance that could have been attributed to them.
It’s plain to see that Fatshark has ironed out some of the previous clumsiness in combat that was present in War of The Roses and War of the Vikings and for their first foray into a first person format – they’ve done a hell of a job.
With only three missions so far as a beta sampling they are promising a total of fifteen to come and I’m looking forward to delving into these adventures. So far I’ve completed each of the campaigns on the hard difficulty and each has proved its own set of unique challenges. There was one bug that would allow an easy completion of the Prologue level but it was nice to see that Fatshark was able to rapidly correct this after only a couple of days.
If they can maintain a steady stream of content (Orks or other agents of Chaos?) I can see this game going the distance. As it stands, it’s already more engaging to me than similar games such as Payday 2 have attempted and with a unique loot and crafting system it has a lot more depth than is readily first apparent.
Story : 7.0 (Unfolds naturally through Dialogue, but there is no official overall story thus far, suffice what is done on individual missions.
Combat: 8.5
Sound: 9 (Jesper Kyd’s soundtrack is fantastic.)
Depth: 8
Fun: 10
Overall: 8.5

There is a lot of potential in this game.
However at this point in development, it's just that, potential.
The only reason why this game is getting a "Not recommended" is because the timing on everything is off. From the amount of time it takes to gather resources to the animations of the creatures and NPCs.
I could see myself making some really cool creations in this game, but I can't bring myself to spend the hours to gather all the resources needed to do so. So I then tried the build mode that gives you infinite resources from the very begining and found myself getting bored of building because it took too long to do a simple flat diagonal bridge over a small crevasse (something like 20+ minutes).
The way how the building works is really cool with the options to expand on the XYZ planes before placing the blocks you want. However, due to the constraints of the camera, I found I could only build outwards/upwards so far before I would have to reposition myself for a better view of what I was working on. The process than became: build a little then move a little and repeat until done.
I'd like to see different sized blocks that I could place as the current size can be VERY small when working on anything larger than a small shack (and even then I found myself doubling up on the wall thickness because I felt a single block wide wall looked like a couple sheets of plywood stuck together).
As far as the story section goes, my only comment would be to do away with the voice acting as sometimes it seems out of place, like the voice actors were distracted while reading their lines. Otherwise I found the missions/quests to be very entertaining and fun.
Overall, I'd say pass on this for now and wait for the game to become more fleshed out. It's interesting and visually impressive AND the terra forming is superb. But, the amount of time you spend on creating anything will try your patience as it can feel like you're building because you HAVE to and not because you want to as well as you'll feel like you're fighting the camera to get anything done.

After a couple of less-than-stellar experiences with alpha/early-access/kickstarter games, I was pretty much set in the "never again" camp. A friend told me that I _really_ should check out Planet Explorer, given he knew how much I love sandbox games.
This game - even at the alpha stage is, to put it mildly, absolutely amazing. Many, many years ago, an essay was written in the MMO community called "Let me bake bread" - in short, it said a _great_ video game lets the player play as _they_ want: Be that fighting, building, exploring, crafting or socializing. This game has it all (well, maybe not quite the socializing, but I haven't played multiplayer).
The visuals are beautiful; The build system is limited only by your imagination and the content in the game - again, even at this early stage - reinforces both the suspension of disbelief and wonder.

This is a difficult review to write as I'm going to be going against the grain.  Note that I haven't finished the game yet but I think I have played enough to have a pretty good preliminary opinion, I could change my mind and write my review over but for now this is it.
First of all I loved Hotline Miami and played through the original a few times so as you'd imagine I was pretty excited when I saw Wrong Number had been released.   After a few hours I was left with a thoroughly "bleh" feeling.
First of all the levels feel less like a think on your feet slaughtering ground and more like a puzzle.   In the original through some genius of game design you are able to fly through the levels with minimal planning and succeed with randomized equipment making each attempt a little different and every failure a chance to hone reflexes rather than feeling like you made a bad decision.  Equipment and enemies are generally static and often you are often given a specific character to use who must follow their own rules or have their own "ability" which may or may not equate into fun gameplay.  I appreciate them wanting to expand the cast of characters and make them each unique but...to be perfectly honest it becomes just a giant mess.  Masks are now associated with individual people and while they offer a few new interesting traits the expanded cast of mentally deranged individuals just muddles what little plot the game had making it much more difficult to follow what's going on
Anyway, failing to make to through a level felt more like I was being punished for not knowing a guy with a gun was standing at impossibly long range rather than not dealing with him appropriately.  Perhaps this is due to worse level design or a meaningful attempt to make this game different then it's predecessor but either way it equates into a far less entertaining game and the difficulty arises from what feels like bad design rather then genuine difficulty.
TL;DR:  So the bottom line is "would I recommend this to a friend?"  No.   The game is nowhere near as good as the original and frankly not worth the price of admission thus far.  Maybe I'll change my mind as I play through it but I just find it hard to recommend a purchase to someone when I'm struggling to have fun playing it.

Mount & Blade is a popular game on Steam. It is a game that has been out since 2008 and today it has 20,000 people playing on Steam. I bought this in a sale, as I had heard about it before and people had recommended it to me, when I saw it in the sale, along with the DLCs, I thought I would treat myself.
Graphics
This game was made in 2008, but even so, the graphics are quite good for that time. They are not too bad even now. I will show you a picture of the game to show you what it looks like.
They are definitely not the best graphics, but the gameplay makes up for that.
Gameplay
The campaign is very open in this game. You start out with a few screens that ask you what your history was and this will set your character up. You could start out with an uneducated, unskilled character that has to train up before they are really good at anything, or you could start as a trained, educated character that already has proficiency in combat. All this is up to you and you choose what you start as.
In the campaign, you start out unknown by anyone and you work your way to becoming what you want your character to be. You could be the next king, reining over everyone. You could be the next army commander who everyone fears, or you could be a renowned criminal with people working for you through fear. This is up to you, you can be whoever you want to be.
The combat system is complex, as the way that you attack can be altered by the way you move your mouse when you attack. If you move your mouse left while attacking, it will make your character attack from the left. The same goes for any angle that you move your mouse, thus hitting different parts of the body and taking more or less HP off the target. This is the same for blocking, you have to block in the same direction that the opponent is attacking from, otherwise they hit you.
Multiplayer
This is what drew me to the game. The massive battles that can have up to 200 people on are awesome and the battles that take place in this game are amazing. There are several game modes, some where you attack or defend a castle and some where you battle it out with one life and the team which kills the other team wins.
You get to choose what your character does, you could be a knight or an archer or a gunnery person and fire cannons! They all have different weapons and different ways to be played.
Don't be put off by the graphics, they are not that bad at all really. The gameplay is amazing and the massive epic battles that you can command in single player or be one of the 200 people rushing round in multiplayer are immense!

Battlefield 1942 Nostalgia Simulator.
Really, the game is a reminder of to what point the industry has come. While BF1942 was a well optimized, balanced and supported game, then Heroes and Generals' "potential" that is so often mentioned in these reviews comes from actually cannibalizing the old school WW2 shooter. The controls are similarly floaty (yet still way more awkward), the battle maps are equally large yet fairly linear (but with fewer people on teams to create a real ghost town effect) and the concept centered around combined arms warfare (without the class system that actually enabled infantry to compete with mechanized branches of war).
And to make matters worse than the "borrowing" from BF1942 being done ineptly, it is all coated with a great helping of P2W glazing. Where you could just jump in a plane or pick a sniper class in BF1942 and have the experience guide you to be better and better and eventually a competitive player of your own, here you either need to slog through a horrifying grind where you are essentially left at the hands of those people who fate has somehow decreed to own better weapons than you (and be grateful if it's only a high tier SMG instead of a freaking tank), or simply those who (for some reason or another) have decided to support the game with their hard-earned cash.
Now, I can see why the game piques one's interest. The concept of being a foot soldier commanded by humans high up the food chain is something video games don't really do that often, but as things stand, for an FPS player, the "Generals" aspect seems foreign and indecipherable as they seem to do little more than imbalance specific scenarios, which, from a strictly FPS point of view, is incredibly infuriating. Maybe I'm just not clever enough to pick up why things happen the way they do, but as a simpleton of a simple soldier, the fact that I'm given a low tier weapon and am expected to die against opposition far better armed than me is immensely unfair. Maybe this is what "Heroes" references - the men of WW2 who were indeed put in hopeless and unfair situations - but I cannot see how such exposure to real tragedies is fun to anyone but the most sadomasochistic roleplayer.
And as such, I'm left with slogging through the game, hoping to unlock that amazing sniper rifle I picked up off the ground once and went on a fifteen to nothing killing spree with. But it's way too long of a stride and offers little on the way - and considering how the battles are empty and chaotic (20 players per team seems to be a good haul - on maps that force you to ride bikes to control points only to be scythed down by better-equipped players it means that you will almost never be allowed to "pick your own battles", if you catch my drift) it doesn't really strike me as being worth it. Unfortunately these core issues do not look like they'll be fixed any time soon. I can handle floaty and imprecise controls when the concept gives me enjoyment, but there is so much infuriating me about every aspect of the game that long playing sessions are out of the question. As such I'm left with quick spurts of 30-40 minutes of gameplay, which obviously means that unlocking any of the high tier weaponry is a pipe dream at best.
So is this game worth contributing towards? Honest to god, if you have any money to spare, organize some kind of revival of BF1942 instead. If you play this for free, consider that you won't get any long term enjoyment of it. Value the initial few hours skirmishes and move on. But all in all, this one is just a major let down.

I decided to change my review for this game after the Timoshenko update.
I have been playing this game for quite a long time now, and it seemed to have just reached the point where it was getting fun and my skills and practice were paying off.
That was, until the Timoshenko update this week.
I thought "Oh wow, Soviet teams! That will be awesome!" I started playing a map and suddenly these brand new Soviet characters were charging down the field like an unstoppable beast, capturing all of the points and one-shotting all of my teammates. Map after map, it was the brand new Soviet characters winning.
If they were just added to the game, how are they outperforming players that have been playing for a year?!?!
The answer is that the newest update has really leveraged the pay to win, and most of the soviet teams' characters were bought with real money as an "Academy - Trained Character." Academy trained is basically a cheat code to bypass INSANE amounts of play time. I didn't mind the veteran accounts and the booster ribbons for boosting XP. Sure, that's p2w too, but this new advantage for payers is just ridiculous. It's not even fun to play anymore.
I'm not one of those anti-profit people, but there is a balance. The devs essentially are pushing away a huge portion of their fan base that has been playing for a long time because now they're getting their butts kicked by noobs with a credit card.
I gave this game my enthusastic recommendation and time, but now I'm going back to change it. Pay to win was always there to some degree, but now it's at the level where the game is ruined. It's too bad because they made a great game at first. What a shame.

Planet Explorers is a very unique game. While it does come with several short-comings which I will discuss later, the game itself is very well rounded and based on a sound survival tactical idealism that is reminiscient of minecraft, but has dutifully ascended to what Minecraft could never quite achieve; and it's still not complete!
Before I dive into what I truly love about Planet Explorers, it would only be fair if I start with a few of it's shortcomings. The first thing is the fact that early game survivability is ridiculously odd, with a botchy combat system and not quite complete progression, this game lacks any motivation to keep on playing past the bad in hopes of reaching something good. Not to mention how ridiculously easy it is to aquire the best gear in the game through the incomplete store function. Sure, while the ability to design your own vehicles and weapons is cool, it's not really something to be all that impressed about, it's very linear about voxel placement and the damage to size ratio is far off to say the least.
But putting all of that on the back burner, I would like to now dive in to what I thought was amazing about the game, and the reasons that I kept playing through the faults. The in-game world is beautifully designed, and provides motivation to explore and just admire the scenery. The colony function allows you to find people out in the wildnerness who you can ask to join you and before you know it, you can get a whole group of people following you around. The combat system is great, but part of the problem with it is just how poorly animated it is, but that's very easy to put aside. The animals and aliens in this game are not only well designed, but also are varied in appearance and combat strategy, it will make it difficult to say raid an alien colony without preparation, and it makes your troubles worth it in the end. With a good story mode and great functionality for a game that's still unfinished, it's hard to point out that many faults in it. And even then, to find anything really wrong with the game I had to nitpick.
If I was going to rate this game, I'd have to give it at least a 7/10.

My least favourite Call of Duty game was always Black Ops, mainly because of it's technical performance (a game-crashing glitch that was patched only after 6 months for example). But even that giant flop did not irritate the crap out of me as much as Ghosts. This game manages to be the dullest, most horrible experience in the franchise. Characters are not even cut out of cardboard, they are faceless to the extreme and you would find yourself bored out of your mind at games attempts of drama. Shooting mechanic is been there done that but previous games managed to entice you with colourful vilains and balls to the wall action. In Ghosts there isn't even background music most of the time to keep you engaged in moving from point A to point B. It's a checklist for a publisher, sure, yet Modern Warfare, while being that also, did it's best to be entertaining. This game is a waste of time, money and effort, and a giant botch when it comes to next generation of gaming.
If Advanced Warfare will not be able to deliver series best qualities, the franchise will be worth dumping all together.

The good:  Ghosts new formula of how you prestige, the squads, weapons/attachment slots etc... is a great combination.
The weapons are fairly well balanced, (better than both MW2 and MW3) save for the Bulldog shotty and M27-IAR LMG being far and above the best of their respective classes.
Most of the maps are fun to play and flow well, with the exception of a couple that are just a mess IMHO.
The customization options for the characters, including female characters, is a welcome change, and the operations to get the different camos, patches, headgear, etc... work well since the patch that no longer required that operation to be active to receive the bonus (before that patch, it wasn't worth the effort).
The bad:  Rampant cheating that has not been addressed has yet again spoiled a fun and addicting game.  When this game was launched, they promised a new game engine which ended up being a revised Quake engine, and there were already working hacks available the day of launch.  Why you don't get a few people to review game footage of those with TDM KDR's above 3.0 and start banning them when they are found to be cheating is beyond me.  It would take minimal investment and effort, and you would reap the benefits by making a fair playing field for all.  The fact that less than a year after launch, you only have between 1,000 and 2,500 people playing is testament to the fact that everyone is sick of this garbage.
Matchmaking is not the greatest.  Lag is an ongoing issue due to the large geographic dispersion of the lobbies, where a more localzed matchmaking formula would be much better than what is in effect now.
Conclusion:  Dispite it's flaws, I play this game A LOT, so I guess I would recommend it.  That being said, I will NOT be buying Advanced Warfare at launch due to the lack of the game developers dealing with cheaters.  Deal with the cheaters, and I would not hesitate to buy it.  Without support from the devs on the rampant cheating in every Modern Warfare game since MW2, I will be showing my displeasure with my wallet.

I'm a fan of action co-op like L4D2 and Killing Floor 2 and glad to have a new game added to the mix.  This game has offers of satisfying melee into the mix (blocking machanics and power attacks) and can be quite a challenge.  The fact that it has loot rewards for completing missions is bonus.  This game is in beta and has bugs so wait if that is something that will annoy you; otherwise the game is already extremely fun.  I'm definatley playing this game.

--THE CORE GAMEPLAY--
So if you like L4D2 you'll like this game. It's almost the same exact game reskinned - however - with a loot system.  Each character has a melee attack/weapon and a ranged attack/weapon all of which have a normal and a charged attack.  What sets this game apart from L4D2 is the ammunition, you can run out rather quickly if you are wasting it and you might not find another ammunition pack for a little bit.  You can pick up potions (speed and strength) and bombs throughout the playthrough to help with bigger groups and to escape.  Each map usually has some form of event attached to it - much like L4D2 - where you'll get more than your share of kills.  At the end of the map if you complete it successfully you'll get to roll for loot in a dice system that is all RNG based.
Thoughts - It's fun to play and kill time in.  It's a bit harder than L4D2 as I believe it punishes you more for leaving the group, as most of the special Skaven are very hard to kill when you are solo unlike L4D2.
--SPECIAL SKAVEN--
Right now in the game there is only a few
Pole Skaven - which is basically a jockey from L4D2 - he grabs you and pulls you away from the group and impales you on a pole until rescued.
Assassin Skaven - Basically the hunter from L4D2 - pounces on you and goes to town.
Gas Skaven - Much like the spitter from L4D2  - shoots an area full of gas - you take damage in it.
Armored Skaven - I don't believe these are specials but they are a lot like the riot police guys in L4D2, and you encounter them in packs and they hit like a truck.
Minigun Skaven - Targets one player and unleashes a volley of bullets at them.
Tank Skaven (forget the name) - Basically the tank from L4D2
Thoughts - Other than the Gas Skaven (which I believe needs a bit of a damage buff) there is no real threat for grouping up and just funneling the skaven in through a door or other small area.  Which allows for a lot of events/areas to be kind of cheesed through in my opinion (L4D2 also had this issue). I feel like there should be a couple more specials that can make that kind of strategy a gamble (like adding one that is very fast and blows up dealing aoe damage).  This game is not fully released yet so I hope they had a few more specials in that can throw groups curve balls and make decision making a little harder.
--LOOT & INVENTORY--
The weapon system is pretty simple, you have a few core type of weapons which have different core stats, and then you have unique modifiers (chance on hit) type of things - greens have 1 modifier - blues have 2 modifier - and so forth.  In order to unlock those modifiers you have to upgrade the weapon which you use materials for.  You can get material by breaking down weapons that you get from playing and completing missions.  So basically you farm items.  You can also create items by putting I believe 5 (might be 6) items of the same type to upgrade it to the next tier....so you can put 5 whites in to make a blue, 5 blues to make a purple and so forth.
Thoughts - The system is very RNG , and really supports grinding for weapons.  What I don't like is the fact you can't find weapons in the game (they should be rare drops or something like that but still).  So the only way to get weapons is to lvl up (which you get 1 per level) and by completing maps, which you also get 1.  So what this type of loot system will encourage is everyone running the same map (whatever is easiest to do/cheese on the highest diffculty) over and over to farm items to use for resources and upgrading.
-- ENDING COMMENTS--
They nailed the price point at $30, this game wouldn't be worth $60.  It's fun to play, even better with friends, and should be done on a difficulty that is challenging to all.  The loot system needs some work and the hitboxes for some the Skaven need adjusted.  I feel like ammo crates are a bit common right now and would like them spread out more.  A couple more special infected to make it more interesting, and maybe a way for someone with a sword and shield to actually draw some aggro somehow (it's already in the L4D2 gameplay as boomer bile, just make a skill for the 2 tanks to have a way for the Skaven to only attack them!)

Wow, what an incredible game.
Played it for a couple hours and then bought it on sale. About 15 hours in I think. Since a pint costs about £4 and I bought this for slightly less, and it takes me about 10 minutes to drink a pint, I'd say that pretty much works out to be a very worthwhile purchase even at full price. The same can't be said for games like Last of Us which is inferior in every way to this.
The combat is hard to get used to in the first 20 mins, but it is incredibly fun and satisfying as soon as you get the hang of it. Whether you've defeated your final opponent in the arena, or chopped that last head in an important battle, when it works it is extremely satisfying. If you're anything like me you will actively train yourself and blocking and countering etc. It's doesn't quite look as real as some games, but damn does it FEEL real.
And if you don't like the combat, well, you don't have to. The game is so rich that you could a full experience without ever even drawing your sword. You can Tyrion Lannister your way through the game if you want. No, seriously, you can, and it works, and it's great fun. You can be a general or a king. Not a Total War general who floats above the realm on a jetpack and controls everyone through mind power. You ARE the general, on a horse, with your men, commanding only as far as your voice can carry. The unit command is tricky to learn but very fluid. It's realistic. It requires more than one general to co-ordinate a large force of 1000s with flanking manoevres and real time combat. You will need some practice before you can perform anything as complicated as a flanking manoevre, but not everyone is cut out to be a leader. But a true leader must be at the helm, and you can be that leader. (I haven't tried multiplayer, but I bet it becomes very interesting on voice chat with commanders and leuitenants etc.)

This is review for Far Cry 3 and not uPlay, so I will leave the lousy DRM out of the picture, since it hasn't affected my experience negatively.
I played this game on console and just began on PC, but its the same thing. This game is by far my favorite open-world FPS, and definitely the most immersive. Even 4 years later the island game world seems nearly endless (and when you think you've explored most of it you make it to ANOTHER smaller island.) The game gives you the option to fast travel but I enjoy driving through the jungle, perhaps hunting some animals or pirates every now and then.
One of my favorite parts about this game is that you can play it in different ways, in every aspect of the game. You could rush through the campaign then spend your time doing side stuff, or explore the island to its fullest then complete the story. On a smaller level, you have a choice of being stealthy or loud in most situations and both has their advantages. You could run into an outpost and mow down enemies like Rambo, you could sneak around placing C4 then start an ambush, you could drive in with your allies and take over the place as an army, or you snipe everyone in the place from afar. You also have a vast choice of weapons at your disposal, which adds to the freedom of gameplay.
I'm not a huge fan of crafting/xp in non-"survival" games, but this is an exception. Leveling up gives you even more options for taking on a situation, and crafting allows you to prepare for those situations. The arm tattoo that grows as you upgrade gives even more incentive to keep on playing.
The story is the only part of the game I didn't particularly enjoy. Vaas is a fantastic villain of course, but everything besides his scenes didn't really intrigue me. It's another typical "I'm going to go save my people" cliche and I don't care for it.
Overall, I recommend getting this game. It still holds up 2 games and 4 years later, and you're going to put countless hours into it even if all you're doing is taking outposts from pirates.

This is an overall interesting game, I enjoyed the voice acting and the game successfully commincates a feeling of loss and urgency.  The gmaeplay, when you are navigating the world against zombies, is reasonably entertaining.  That being said, this game has a number of pretty fundamental flaws that keep it from being actually good.
It doesn't always effectively communicate the environment visually, and the actual nature of the puzzles can be confusing.  The rules of the game are occasionally inconsistent.  Sometimes falling into water kills you, sometimes it doesn't.  I get why you took that approach, animating swimming can be time consuming and there aren't enough areas that use it for it to be useful, but neither is water being death an acceptable outcome anymore.
Overall the game feels like no one playtested it that wasn't intimitely involved in the game's creation, which leads to some deeply frustrating and unsatisfying areas.  The game could be good, but some things (like the whole rat man area) would need to be cut, and the gameplay would need additional polish.

Deadlight is one of the very few side-scrollers that I have enjoyed in modern gaming.  The graphics, even though they are just from the side, looks really impressive throughout the game.  The story line is interesting, although not very original.  However, the ending is good, even a little profound.  This counts for a lot.  It's game is just downright fun.
The negative side of things are somewhat inherent with a PC side-scroller.  First of all, this is an xBox port, and its not the worst port out there but I hate seeing those xBox buttons pop up on the screen.  The other issue is that PC controls for the type of game are always a bit odd.  Most of the time they work quite well.  However, in the last parts of the game the challenges get really tricky just because its difficult to mash your keyboard in the exact right way.
All said, this is a fun game, good for maybe 3-5 hours, which is just right for this type of game.  You won't regret buying it.

This review is specifically related to the game's optimization (or, should I say, lack thereof). I have a Lenovo Y510p laptop, with two NVidia GT 755M in SLI configuration (not an impressive hardware configuration, but quite respectable). I've managed to play "Wolfenstein: The New Order" on it's highest settings (on 1920x1080) which is an amazing game by today's standards, but "Call of Duty: Ghosts" pretty much dies/crashes if I try to do the same. This is, of course, because the game is poorly optimized. I contacted support (btw, amazing support team, Activision) and they asked me to downgrade the resolution until the game would stop crashing, which I found (after a couple of tries) was around 1366x768 (which I later confirmed with NVidia's GeForce Experience tool): This is almost 720p, which makes the game horrible to play due to heavy pixelation. On the other hand, the latest Wolfenstein incarnation was incredibly well optimized, so well that it takes a trained eye to realize where optimization happens (e.g., loading and adapting textures on-the-fly as the player scans the scene).
For a game on this price range, I would have expected a bit more attention to detail: Since not everybody updates their rig every year, optimization should be a non-brainer for developers such as Activision to reach more end users, who would happily pay for a game that works on a decent piece of hardware. It doesn't take a product manager or marketing person, nor an epiphany, to realize this is important.
: I hope Steam had offered a demo of the game, so that I would have realized about this before buying it (and don't tell me to read the “Game hardware requirements”... they are worthless when there are a gazillion combinations of hardware components in a PC that can alter the performance of a rig)

This is a re-review. Your comments are welcome and please remember, this is my review based on what I experienced. Also I have played 4hrs of singleplayer and 10 hours of Multiplayer.

Multiplayer is a different story... No matter what time of day I decide to play, I cannot find ANY games on any gamemode except Domination. Yes my NAT is open but the game just doesn't locate a match. I can easily connect to AUS/NZ servers on any other game. And I thought new games were active, I am clearly mistaken. Secondly, after a match is over, instead of returning to lobby, I get a black screen. Minimising the game and Maximising seems to fix this, so i'd say its a nVidia bug that only affects COD:Ghosts.
Multiplayer too, refuses to startup in most cases without hanging, I have to force close and relaunch.
In conclusion, for a game that is the latest in the franchise, with all the issues of Mulitplayer, which is a key component to the game, I am left regretting my descision to buy, and I see why it's cheaper than the older Black Ops: 2. That is enough to give this review a thumbs down, even if the singleplayer was AMAZING.

The first Hotline Miami was released back in 2012, and it became a large success, critics and fans alike praised it for its fast paced, adrenaline fueled ultraviolence to the catchy soundtrack made by several rather unkown but very talented artists, unlike most games which featured a single score made by one person.
The story in the first Hotline Miami was simplistic, and relied on more subtle means to tell its story. The main character never speaks, although there is dialogue in the game.
The gameplay consisted of fast dispatching of russian mobsters with various blunt weaponry such as a pool cue or a baseball bat, kitchen appliances, throwables such as bricks, darts, and glass bottles, as well as firearms.
The levels were rather small, enemies were in a reasonable distance from each other and it was all a very compact format, which lent itself rather well to its very melee-centric combat. You kill fast and die fast, one hit and everyone's out, unless you throw your weapon or punch them when not wearing a tiger mask.
The second game is the same in core principle, albeit with some changes. It feels a bit slower, heavier in a way.
But the most jarring part of it is the level design. Initially rather well done, soon you can't help but feel that they are too big for their own good. Hotline Miami is a concept that doesn't lend itself to large levels. Here's a list of problems that arrives with the large level format.
Here comes some story stuff.
Hotline Miami has several characters that it focuses on.
One of the key components of the Hotline Miami series is the music, and it is delivered in spades on that front. The music far outmatches the first game which was also fantastic, and the soundtrack is in my opinion worth picking up.
Hotline Miami 2 is a hard game.
An unforgiving game, yet very forgiving at the same time.
The levels are long and large, but you can instantly respawn if you die, and you will die. A ton.
You will probably die a lot more in the second game than in the first one, the reaction time on enemies seems to have been reduced slightly and they can therefore react to you quicker. The most successful tactic so far is baiting out and taking your time with the enemies, as in some of the larger levels it is very, very hard to get a complete combo going.
But it is overall a compelling and certainly an unique experience, and if you liked the first game I'd recommend picking this one up too.

If you've enjoyed raw tactical shooters in the past you should definitely give this a shot.  In an era where the ultra-polished FPS games like CoD and Battlefield rule the market, it's nice to see that a simple and yet surprisingly fun MMO shooter like HaG can offer so much for FREE!
Currently, the map selection is a bit lacking but the game is still in beta.  The maps however are well done and offer a plethora of tactical possibilities.  Each of the assault maps are pretty huge and traverseing the map can be a bit of a drag.  The payoff  is plenty of room to manuvere and outflank your opponent, no bottlenecks here. (image of Operation Metro runs through my head)  There's also plenty of foilage and rolling hills for infantry to conceal themselves in (AMBUSH!).  Additionally, the tops of buildings and open windows are fair game, making the towns more dangerous for infantry and armor alike.
POSITION, POSITION, POSITION.  This is a tactical shooter and a single bullet can be fatal.  During my 50+ hours I've played mostly infantry/paratrooper and I can tell you that my most successful encounters have been due to superior positioning (attack from the rear, flank, above, or ambush).

A decent game suffering a lot from the "walk a long distance to do A, B or C (delete as appropriate)" style of play that a lot of large open-world games have.
Lots and lots of cons... but 1 pro that makes this a must play: Vaas is probably the best villain in any game I've ever played. His voice acting is simply incredible, his character is supurbly well written and his menace really makes this game special. He makes this a must play all by himself....
As for those cons:
- The story is dull and, with the exception of Vaas's content, all very predictable.
- You and your friends are unlikeable: your girlfriend is a nag, you're a jerk and the others are caricatures. Dennis, Buck and Willis (main NPCs) are entirely predictable with only Vaas and Citra actually being interesting.
- Money and  Exp: you'll end up with vast amounts of both. If you spend any time exploring the beautiful open world you'll easily have more of either then you can use. Having too much money can almost become game-breaking as your backpack fills up with useless junk you cannot sell and CBA to drop piece by piece.
- Controls: when I first played this I gave a negative review because of some of the movement bugs (specifically getting stuck on 'flat' surfaces). Those bugs have been fixed but it still feels that at times you are battling the controls  not the game (especially while climbing towers).
- poker: tedious and unavoidable... enjoy.

I guess now would be a good time to write a review though I have never done one before.
Planet Explorers I feel reminds me most of an old mmo called Star Wars Galaxies. This game combines house building, vehicle building, armor crafting, weapon crafting, and technology. As well as the normal monster huting and looting, though it is unlike you will find a weapon on a random creature.
This game does have its bugs as is seen when a creature some how manages to float up a tree without moving, but hey... its alpha. The combat is fun though a bit repeatitive on the actions, same swinging animation. But to be honest the game is very fun, and a different trend then the MMO that we are used to. The graphics may fall short but this does not mean that the sceen is any less beautiful. The landscape is vast and its quite daunting to consider how long it will take to explore all of it... and thats just for the main story line.
Now I believe something I should touch base on is the crafting system. As I mentioned very indepth but a bit hard to understand first off. Items you need to make you first must get the recipe from mobs or NPC's. After that you then have to find the resources and craft the specific item which is normal enough. But when you look to create a vehicle you must make sure to have the specific items your going to use when crafting it in your editor.
The mining, herb picking, and diging is all very fluent and easy to get the hang of. I would highly recommend this game if you are looking for something to keep you interested while waiting for the next big mmo. I personally have not tried the multiplayer yet, but from what I understand it does work... and to be honest whats better then exploring a massive span of land with some friends.
I look forward to the future updates this game offers, and I hope many of you enjoy this game as much as I do.

The levels were rather small, enemies were in a reasonable distance from each other and it was all a very compact format, which lent itself rather well to its very melee-centric combat. You kill fast and die fast, one hit and everyone's out, unless you throw your weapon or punch them when not wearing a tiger mask.
The second game is the same in core principle, albeit with some changes. It feels a bit slower, heavier in a way.
But the most jarring part of it is the level design. Initially rather well done, soon you can't help but feel that they are too big for their own good. Hotline Miami is a concept that doesn't lend itself to large levels. Here's a list of problems that arrives with the large level format.
Here comes some story stuff.
Hotline Miami has several characters that it focuses on.
One of the key components of the Hotline Miami series is the music, and it is delivered in spades on that front. The music far outmatches the first game which was also fantastic, and the soundtrack is in my opinion worth picking up.
Hotline Miami 2 is a hard game.
An unforgiving game, yet very forgiving at the same time.
The levels are long and large, but you can instantly respawn if you die, and you will die. A ton.
You will probably die a lot more in the second game than in the first one, the reaction time on enemies seems to have been reduced slightly and they can therefore react to you quicker. The most successful tactic so far is baiting out and taking your time with the enemies, as in some of the larger levels it is very, very hard to get a complete combo going.
But it is overall a compelling and certainly an unique experience, and if you liked the first game I'd recommend picking this one up too.

Deadlight is one of the very few side-scrollers that I have enjoyed in modern gaming.  The graphics, even though they are just from the side, looks really impressive throughout the game.  The story line is interesting, although not very original.  However, the ending is good, even a little profound.  This counts for a lot.  It's game is just downright fun.
The negative side of things are somewhat inherent with a PC side-scroller.  First of all, this is an xBox port, and its not the worst port out there but I hate seeing those xBox buttons pop up on the screen.  The other issue is that PC controls for the type of game are always a bit odd.  Most of the time they work quite well.  However, in the last parts of the game the challenges get really tricky just because its difficult to mash your keyboard in the exact right way.
All said, this is a fun game, good for maybe 3-5 hours, which is just right for this type of game.  You won't regret buying it.

One of the finest games I've played recently, Deadlight is set in a zombie post-apocaliptic world where zombies (called Shadows) have overrun the city. The game mechanics perfectly capture the idea of the old classic Flashback (which also influenced other titles like Another World, Blackhawk or Bermuda Syndrome, among others): a puzzle plataformer where you must find the right way to get to the next screen while avoiding as much damage (and of course death) as possible. It rewards exploring, observation and cleverness, without being too hard, but you will die often. Dying is a way to understand the mechanics of the current screen. Deadlight also introduces some interesting ideas like doing noise to attract the Shadows to a concrete place. The interactivity with the scene is well done, where elements of the fore and background can be used in different ways to help you progress. Even if the background story is not very original, the character story is compelling, and you cannot wait to see what's going to happen next. The ambience and the graphics are very well done, which fully immerses you in the story. Resuming: for 12€, this is by far one of the highest quality/price ratios out there right now.

Wow, what an incredible game.
Played it for a couple hours and then bought it on sale. About 15 hours in I think. Since a pint costs about £4 and I bought this for slightly less, and it takes me about 10 minutes to drink a pint, I'd say that pretty much works out to be a very worthwhile purchase even at full price. The same can't be said for games like Last of Us which is inferior in every way to this.
The combat is hard to get used to in the first 20 mins, but it is incredibly fun and satisfying as soon as you get the hang of it. Whether you've defeated your final opponent in the arena, or chopped that last head in an important battle, when it works it is extremely satisfying. If you're anything like me you will actively train yourself and blocking and countering etc. It's doesn't quite look as real as some games, but damn does it FEEL real.
And if you don't like the combat, well, you don't have to. The game is so rich that you could a full experience without ever even drawing your sword. You can Tyrion Lannister your way through the game if you want. No, seriously, you can, and it works, and it's great fun. You can be a general or a king. Not a Total War general who floats above the realm on a jetpack and controls everyone through mind power. You ARE the general, on a horse, with your men, commanding only as far as your voice can carry. The unit command is tricky to learn but very fluid. It's realistic. It requires more than one general to co-ordinate a large force of 1000s with flanking manoevres and real time combat. You will need some practice before you can perform anything as complicated as a flanking manoevre, but not everyone is cut out to be a leader. But a true leader must be at the helm, and you can be that leader. (I haven't tried multiplayer, but I bet it becomes very interesting on voice chat with commanders and leuitenants etc.)

Alright, I'm a pretty big fan of Hotline Miami 1. So naturally when Wrong Number was announced I had my preorder in as soon as I could without hesitation. Everything about the first was great and I could even see myself now going back and replaying it still (Which I have multiple times).
But this isn't 1, this is Wrong Number. Which had a lot of good qualities that the first did like soundtrack and story. Those two aspects if anything are a ton better in the sequel and I even spent the extra 15 dollars to get the soundtrack downloads off steam. The downsides to wrong number aren't really numerous, but the ones there are can be a real downer to anybody who loves the first.
To start, the game is a lot more oriented around shooting and guns. The floors/levels themselves that you are in are substantially bigger and you will be using the shift-to-look function 100% more than you would in the first. This is a big upset for a lot of people but it still made for some interesting gameplay. I think the problem with the gun-focus is that it turns a lot of the levels into more of a puzzle game, figuring out patrols, the best routes to take and things of that nature. The first was more about going through the same level over and over to try and improve your reaction times and how fast you can plow through enemies.
It's still a great game though, and honestly you can tell they had a bigger budget. There seems to be a lot more replay value on an already large 9-10 hours of gameplay which is about double what the first one is.
Overall the game is a good 8/10 for me. Was an awesome purchase but didn't completely live up to the first one.

Very good game, especially for the money.
The graphics are top notch when it comes to lighting and reflections; I was very impressed by them. Textures are decent and the animation isn't very good, but when considering the size of the dev group, I think they're totally acceptable.
The game has a lot to offer for 20$. There weren't as many maps whe the game first retailed (retail, not early access), but they've done good work and put in plenty enough maps to keep you occupied.
There's a game mode called hunted that is very different for a zombie game but totally fun. It's human vs human, with zombies in between. The objective is to kill all other humans while becoming the last to live. Most important, however, is that there is no wait between play. When you die, you become a zombie instead of spectating. And you also get to control your own group of zombies through special skills.
However, if this sounds unappealing to you, you'll probably like the escape mode. It's your traditional objective based gameplay where you must follow the hints to escape the map and the impending hordes of zombies. There's lots of shooting, zombies, and teamwork, the three essentials for a zombie game.
All in all, this game is worth the buy.

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is the explosive finale to the Hotline Miami series but will it hit the mark or fall flat on it's face ? Hotline Miami 2 is a way bigger sequel and is larger then the first one in almost every aspect. The game takes place Before, between and after the events of Hotline Miami. Showing diffrent perspectives on the murders and what happend after them. I could go in depth with the story but i would spoil an already amazing story. So how is this game ? So far this is my favorite game of 2015 and is my personal pick for GOTY. Even though the game looks the same it's not and actually it's quite diffrent. The game is even harder than 1 and at some times could feel harsh but it never is too unfair that you want to stop playing. Unlike the first game the story takes the stage as the more important factor to the game and it nails it perfectly. Every story you play through is engaging and you want to see how everything wraps up together. The levels are bigger than the ones you see in the first one which could lead to many deaths. The game is also pretty buggy at the moment but like the first one it should be patched this week. The soundtrack which was important in the first one is ten times better in two. The soundtrack will keep you on you're toes the entire time. Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is a thrilling ride which you all should expierence at least once. This game is full of twists and turns along the way. After the ending i sat in my chair because i was speechless how good the game was. Without a doubt get this game right now because it's one of the best games i have ever played. I give Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number a 10/10

I had a good time with Deadlight for a little bit. The side-scrolling puzzly genre, reminiscent of Out of this World is nice, and Dealight's presentation is gorgeous. Early on, the game is forgiving enough that its numerous flaws are forgivable. Then it gets more frustrating. I'll be clear, I'm not opposed to difficult games, and this esn't even a difficult game. But it does pack a LOT of frustration due to poor design in its short running time.
The story is incredibly lame. From the opening cutscene, you should know exactly how this one plays out.
Check pointing is pretty bad. There are some 3-minute or so segments without a checkpoint, usually with trial-and-error
gameplay, which don't checpoint where they should. This would be fine except for the biggest problem which I'll cover below: inconsistent controls.
The silouhette presentation sometimes messes with things. You won't know which objects you will trip over, or which objects you can grab onto, or are merely part of the pretty window dressing.
Melee combat is miserable. Start your swing a smidge too close and zombies will interrupt your attack. You're told a strong swing when a zombie is on the ground will kill them. It does so about 80% of the time. Zombies lurch out of the background, which is a very nice atmospheric effect, but you can't attack them until they're exactly in the same 2D plane as you. Giving a little bit of wiggle room.
Trial and error gameplay. We should be beyond this. There are segments that you will repeat over and over again until you get it right, because something jumps out from a darkened corner to gotcha. That's bad enough but:
INCONSISTENT CONTROLS. There were three chase segment in the game which I had to repeat about a dozen times.  Why? Well, I knew *exactly* what I had to do, but sometimes the main character wouldn't follow along. Sometimes I'd get a running start, jump, and have the avatar lamely fall well short into the water to drown. Sometimes I'd do it and he'd clear it no problem. Sometimes I'd jump to clear a fence, and he'd clamber over in a seconds time. Sometimes he'd stutter at the bottom, jumping in place, before finally getting a handhold. Sometimes you go for a wall jump and bounce off immediately like the Prince of Persia, sometimes he lands on the wall and lamely slides down before taking a miserable, half-hearted leap.
This had been a problem throughout the game, but I didn't much mind, since I wasn't timed. Sometimes I'd stutter over the fence, but no big deal. He got over it eventually. This changed when there was a helicoptor chasing me down, and If the character botched a single jump out of about ten, I'd be mowed down.
In short, the controls feel... arbitrary. Tight controls are fine. Loose controls are fine. These are just weird, where you have to be precise with your inputs, but there's significant lag between button presses and the avata's response. Something as simple as taking a running jump from the edge of a ledge can become an absolute chore. Early on in the game, they seem to realize this and leave room for error. The second half of the game is different.
A couple winning examples:
There's a segment where you slide down a hill into some spikes. The game very briefly tell you to roll after the jump (and how to do so). That's all well and good, but to succeed in this segment, you have to press the button *way* late, when you're actually *in* the spikes, and should've been impaled.
There's another segment where you're on a timed run, and any hesitation means death. You have to jump several fences in a row. That's fine, thought it takes a little work. The LAST fence, the devs intended you to crawl under. This is difficult to discern since
A) It's the same height as all the other fences
B) It's darkened, so it's hard to tell it's an opening
C) You're have to be very fast, and don't have time to take in your environment.
Try to jump this fence, of identical height as the others, and your character will jump lamely in place, failing to grab the fence before biting the dust.
TL; DR. This game would have been a nice way to spend an evening with more polished controls. As it is, there are far better zombie games, and far better 2D platformers to play.

Deadlight is a game with an incredible atmosphere with spectacular world-building that happens to be saddled with the unfortunate burden of having the worst characters in the world.  Every time the main character opened his mouth to deliver yet another non-pithy, bordering on psychotic observation of the degradation of the human race, I was reminded of Rorschach from The Watchmen, only less compelling in literally every way.  By the end of the game, which reaching is itself a tremendous exercise in masochism due to the god-awful controls, I was actively rooting for his death.  Thankfully, again due to the controls which makes controlling Randall about as easy as steering a three-legged rhinoceros, these deaths come frustratingly often.  I would recommend this to people as a trick, to get them to enjoy the wonderful atmosphere in the first ten minutes and then laugh at them as their face fell in despair the first time Randall opens his mouth to speak.

Initially I was unsure about the game. You might be to. The UI is clunky, windows don't stay where you put them, fast travel breaks things, etc etc... welcome to alpha. KEEP GOING ANYWAY. They are making a tremendous effort to voice act the whole game. I found myself actually listening to the quests. I am enjoying a storyline that is becoming increasingly compelling as you not only struggle to rescue stranded colonists but unravel the secrets of this world. It is truely a gem. However in the interest of disclosure I am playing alpha 0.752. So I will list the pros and cons given this version, so that you can decide for yourself if its worth the money.
Cons:
- Alpha bugs (these will go away but player beware them) Fast travel breaks quests and resets window location. In fact theres a long list of bugs, many specific to a persons game. None of them were game breaking for me personally. Very polished for an alpha imho.
-Mining is INCREDIBLY slow. Painfully even if you've ever played minecraft. If you think you are going to change the basic terrain in any meaningful way, you are wrong.
-AI is often baffeling. They apear to be nearsighted and terrified of jumping over obsticals. Often I found them on an impossibly vertical surface stuck in place. Time to break out the pickace and carve em off, slowly though, because the pickaxe does nothing quickly. Or just standing around uselessly while I fire away at giant robots getting cut to ribbons by death lasers because they can't see far enough away to be useful. Same goes for turrets, which more often than not get blown up before even firing. Layerback quest is poorly designed as one of the npcs is not invincible and imediately dies unless you bury him in a hole and cover him over. Alpha is alpha.
-VTOL (Vertical Take Off and Landing) design has basically nothing to do with reality, and a redesign of the controls for making them in general could use a looksee. You can do it, its just not easy to scale parts, and they don't go bigger than their original size... you'll see what I mean. They fly like they're on rails, and really need tuning up to 'feel' more realistic. See: Battlefield 2142 transport.
- Geometry in general. There is no ryhme or reason for running through the base of trees. Accessing the meat from a carcase is an artform not a science. ETC. I'm guessing this is an alpha issue as well but if they don't go back soon and unfrak the situation its going to be a depressing amount of work later for the devs.
-Grass... the amount is as staggering as it is GPU shattering. The sensativity of the levels isn't intelligent. Theres basically several options including: none, Too much, holy good god, 1fps, and the all important personal home computer melter level in case ur tired of your pc. I set it at too much. I advise you to do the same, unless you're running a quantum based supercomputer.
Pros:
-Amzaing story with believable motives, and real characters, which you actually care about because its...
-Voice Acted. Hoorah for immersion. Keep it up. Some bits are misssing here, especially when traveling and they randomly talk. I really hope they continue with this effort because everyone who's ever played another MMO has been in a TL;DR accept, kill, turn in kinda mood. This game slows it down, and makes you care, without pulling teeth. Its glorious.
-Great Characters. Had to add this on its own. Everyone is believable, at least human-side. Very important to stay away from the classically "I'm evil, because I'm a jerk like that. No reason." *Kicks a puppy*
-Build your own: Vehicles ground and air, swords, shields, guns, and more with a voxelbased system that with a little more time and polish will have you wondering: How do I port this to my 3d printer?
-Mining, hunting, farming, gathering, crafting, building, sandbox explosion of fun. Some people just wanna horde a million items. Personally I think its a bit in depth, and found myself just buying the finished products... which you can do. So play it how YOU like. Something there for everyone.
-Varied quests. Nothing is a grind, everything has a point. None of the go here kill 40 of these because I want their guts for garters crap. If you are gathering, exploring, or killing its for a reason. IE: learning to craft something new, saving a colonist who will sell you some new interesting gear, so on and so forth.
-Hang Glider. I know you are wondering, if I've got space copters with lazer beams, why do I need a hang glider? Trust me, once you get this baby and a jetpack, you'll be sold on this game. Soaring through the trees (Which you can't run into don't worry ^.^) you'll notice the terrain is actually quite beautiful.
-Fully developed universe. It has history, conflicts, and you get to learn about it all. More than that it effects you, and I found myself going from npc to npc just to find out more about the lore. Tedious reading goodbye. 90% voice acted so the story is 'told' by the characters who its happening to. Immersion is not just important but an expectation these days, and Pathea aims to deliver.
-Critters. Mobs. Animals? are varied, interesting, and best of all, capracious. Initially I started with the  run and gun, and getting myself murdered, because they designers clearly favor realism, and I have the suicidal heroistic tendancies of most gamers. Then I found myself cautiously aproaching new life forms. Everything has a power level, and some are over 9000. Descretion is important, almost as much as learning to run like hell. I apreciate this, however some of you would put this in the con group. Some of you can bugger off.
Theres more to it, this is a highlights list. I'm telling you I've played enough games to wonder what I'm doing with my life... and I recommend this game, even in its alpha form. Give them your money, and say goodbye to the next week until you come up for air.
