That will be a 2-Part review:
FIRST PART> general gaming experience
SECOND PART> comparison to Left 4 Dead and possible future of Vermintide
----
This game feels like a AAA-title since the get-go. The graphics are georgous and it performs very well. Since my new graphic card crashed I was forced to use my old 560 GTX and I can play it on high details - I have no idea how the developers accomplished that but it's wonderful. Maybe the game is very CPU-heavy though since I'm running a Xeon.
The combat feels satisfying and the opponents are a real threat. It's a pretty hard game if you are a casual player, be warned! The loot system adds replayability and I read that the devs added about 8000 different set ups you can earn. All in all a fun game.
----
This game has A LOT of similarities to Left 4 Dead and if the developers are smart, they will include a PvP-Mode (which could be easily be done since all the ingredients are there already). I can see myself playing a lot of hours with co-op only but if Fatshark will add PvP this could basically be called "Left 4 Dead 3: The Warhammer Prequel" and I wouldn't play any other game anymore till Valve will release the real sequel. You get random mobs, you have to do "events" and escape while hordes of rats are chasing you. I played over 2000 hours L4D and it was the most fun I had playing any game, so I beg the devs to add PvP at some point.
They even included almost exactly the same mechanics for the opponents as in L4D. You got a Smoker, a Spitter, a Hunter, a Tank and a rat with a minigun who keeps you busy. So if any of you want to support the game, buy it and and keep begging Fatshark to include PvP as soon as possible since I doubt that it would be a very hard thing to do at this point. If they really do it, Vermintide could become one of the most addicting multiplayer games out there.

Interesting game modes and tactical thinking required.  The game has a lot of potential and has a lot more depth versus left 4 dead.  Unfortunately, the game attempts at creating a confusing unknown environment only leads to game modes with no description, levels made as confusing as possible and no sense of direction at any point in any match.  In fact, you don't even know what the controls are.  It's also exceptionally buggy and requires constant restarts.  I would wait until the bugs are fixed, more content is added and at least some amount of in-game tutorial/briefing before getting the game.  Otherwise it ends up being a boring exercise in confusion.
UPDATE:  So I tried this again months later and it seems there's zero UI improvements, it's still extremely buggy and no new content.  One of the problems is that I don't see how new players can jump into this game.  There's absolutely no description of what to do in any game mode anywhere, so anybody just starting just stands there confused and does nothing.  Good game design means people should know what to do; the fun in a game isn't trying to learn what buttons you can press but how to strategize in a level.  Everything ends up basically being the same; stand there, shoot some zombies.  It only seems tactical on paper until you play.

I liked the game for the time I was playing it but for some reason I just have no will to return to Contagion. I guess the game just got boring for me. Like the game says, it's a true zombie game where headshots lead to instakills and body shots are very ineffective. You have to manage your ammo,there are no crossahairs (you have to use the sights of your gun to aim), every bite has a possibility to turn you and you getting swarmed pretty much means you're dead in the next 3 seconds. However, the game seems to cover up many of its faults with random generated maps.
Besides the fact that melee combat seems clunky and whiffs happen more than it should, the other thing I hate the most are the maps.
The maps are randomly generated, meaning that while this game has only about 3-5 maps in total, they try to artificially make it seem like there is more content that there really is by closing/opening up one or two paths or lanes to the to the very same destination in the game. This doesn't seem too bad at first but some maps like the park one where EVERYTHING looks exactly the same, changing the map makes the game more than annoying.
Guns and equipment are also randomly generated and placed in random locations which is sort of fair, but in a way, this  holds the game back because every game is kind of a clusterfck of people just scrambling around, playing super passively and trying to live long enough to get lucky.
PVP is extremely boring as well since there's the random map and weapon generation and placement going on. Sure that adds a LITTLE extra time to get used to the game but the game is just so focused on hiding and hoping you can get the drop on the other guy  before they can get you or the zombies get you. The only interesting part about this game is that you can come back as a zombie and kill your friends. That's cool and all in the pvp but if you're playing the campaign why would you want to do that?
My biggest gripe with this game is that there is no reason for you to come back. You get nothing extra for winning like exp or skills, and the gameplay feels so shallow (aim down sights, click on head or swing melee weapon) and boring that it's no L4D.
I really liked this game. It's a shame the linux and mac ports never came. In the end when it was alive it was really fun. I'd certainly recommend it when played as the developers intented.

This game is full of twists and turns along the way. After the ending i sat in my chair because i was speechless how good the game was. Without a doubt get this game right now because it's one of the best games i have ever played. I give Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number a 10/10

Pros/Cons
Pros;
+Gameplay basically the same as Left 4 Dead 1-2. Its a great formula. It basically means you and three other people run through maps to accomplish an objective and escape from the rampaging hordes of rat men. It varies between levels. Sometimes you pick things up. Sometimes you open doors.
+Warhammer lore
+Believable characters. Seriously, the Elf is downright antagonistic.
+Very good graphics and sound. Sound effects really set it apart from L4D in that department. You hear and see the impact of your weapons.
+Weapons are divided into melee/ranged specifically for ALL characters. There is no running around looking for weapons to pick up although you do find bombs, potions and healing supplies around. Look for tomes for extra exp and dice rolls. Grimoires give garunteed dice rolls, but half the health of every party member when you get both of them. Not for noobs. You can die very quickly with both of them.
+You can upgrade your weapons in a make-shift salvaging/forge area in the "Lobby". Weapons come in generic white, then green and then blue and then orange. Higher quality weapons have a different weapon texture and they ahve "traits" that you unlock in the forge to get bonuses such as "replenishes stamina on a pushback".
+Experienced gained at the end of a stage to boost your level, and get a reward per level, is based on specific factors and NOT who gets the most killed. THis is a major factor. It encourages teamwork.
+The Lobby is essentially an "inn" that everyone can enter when they join a game before a match starts. There you see inventory chest, forge and ammo replenishment. You start a mission by interacting with the map on the center table. This is also where you change your hero.
+you can dodge by pressing space plus a movement key; love that feature.
+You can press T to outline objects and specific monsters in a blue outline that EVERYONE can see. Your character will probably comment on it to.
These are lot of things I really like about the game. There are a few cons though.
Cons;
-there is some sort of optimization issue concerning particles such as smoke from gunfire. I run on high/max settings for 80 FPS almost at all times because that is what I have the game capped at, but when the Witchhunter fires his guns and it covers my screen....I get shunted down to 40 fps. Its a minor issue.
-there are slight issues with hitbox detection at certain times almost on a consistant basis for some of the "special" mobs.
-there is no option to customize the outfit of your characters. This is something sorely needed as you can change the weapons and even "hats" on the characters.
-L4D brings noobs and people with attitudes. Expect that from L4d and expect that here. Lucky for us that we dont really need voice chat because of how talkative the characters are.
-BOT AI is absoltuely atrocious. If you insist on going alone then you better be godly in your gameplay.
Those are most that I am aware of. The rest generally boil down to personal taste. The game is absolutely worth it. It has a lot of "soul".

Had it for about a week now, and so far the impression is good!
First off, the creation system is amazing and to be commended. Honestly it allows for nearly unparalleled design freedom, limited only by the resources available to your character, which to be honest aren't too difficult to obtain. Making vehicles and weapons that you can use in-game without having to mod them in is spectacular, and overall the system is fairly easy to use and understand.
The mining is effective, if a bit on the clunky side, as the camera often jumps around or makes it hard to see what you're doing, but it ends up being more a minor annoyance than anything game breaking. If you find it unenjoyable enough you can always skip it by hunting and buying all the resources you need from NPC's with meat.
Combat is fun but unfinished, the animations and hit detection aren't the best, especially with melee weapons. It can be hard to tell when you've landed a hit, as the sound effects are placeholder and creatures don't really react much to it. Guns I feel are a lot more effective and fun to use, and hunting is overall a fun part of the game. It just needs work, which apparently it will get in the alpha .8 versions.
The controls for the game are all-in-all pretty good. They get the job done, they don't feel too counter-intuitive, and they aren't a big hindrance in most aspects of gameplay. The only negative for me personally when playing was I found it annoying to switch weapons, particularly if you're switching to a sword and shield, because there is no way to scroll through weapons currently you have to assign both to number keys, which means you have to equip both the sword AND shield. With guns it's less of an issue, but it would be nice to be able to scroll through weapons easier, and to be honest if you have a shield it should auto-equip the best one with a sword.
The world is definitely one of the best parts of the game, with a HUGE variety in both the flora and fauna, in different parts of each biome, and different biomes. Creatures have basic behaviours, for instance herbivores will form a herd and fend off predators as a group, whereas some predators may hunt in packs. When a creature is wounded it may attempt to run away, and predators will actively hunt prey. They do not eat prey yet, which means you can get free resources if you chase a predator off a carcass, but that may be added in later as well.
Each biome also offers different herbs you can collect which have different uses, adding extra incentive to explore (as if the beautiful world with interesting creatures isn't incentive enough), and the various NPC survivors you meet will fill you in on the backstory of the game, including events that happened on earth/mars, and what causes the divide between earthlings and martian settlers.
The Quest system is pretty basic; go here, do this, do that, save this person, escort them, collect these resources, etc. Nothing revolutionary, but the rewards make them worth doing I guess, and the backstory is interesting.
Build mode (what you use to construct buildings) is overall pretty intuitive and fun, with many different shapes to choose from and ways to place them, you are pretty much limited by your imagination. Want a Dark Tower of Doom? Build it. Want an underwater castle? Build it. Want to live on a mountain, or IN a mountain? Go ahead. The free build mode allows you to place things anywhere you want around your character, which is waaaaay better than the minecraft way of doing things, where you have to move your character everywhere to build things.
Crafting is very, very complex and deep, with each component being craftable, and in turn being used to make something even bigger and more complex. You will need to craft the components and have all the resources on you if you are to import a vehicle/weapon from the creation system, which makes perfect sense to me.
For an early access game, and especially an alpha, I think it's one of the most polished ones I've played. It's fun, and it has so much potential, I honestly would recommend it if you can see past the few small issues there are and you enjoy exploration, building, hunting, and driving things you design.

Apparently im playing the role of a police officer who due to his talents and training has survived the undead takeover. I have a pistol and a flashlight and im feeling pretty good about how quiet these streets look. The houses are nice but show signs of being boarded up and busted in, whatever happened here... it happened fast!
Journal Entry 2
This is like an episode of Leave it to beaver... but there isn't any happy singing folks jumping around. I creep quietly along a white picket fence and take cover behind a white car. I can see someone up on the road walking really slowly.. Ok it looks like another player maybe? I turn off my light slowly creep up behind him, the closer I get the more odd the players behavior becomes. I get right up behind him and then he turns... well ... that's not a player at all, before me lies the bloodied face and nattering jaws of really nasty looking undead monster.
Journal Entry 3
I whip on my light and take a steady aim down the barrel.... The creature gives out a shriek and starts running at me, I take very careful calm aim and fire. A perfect headshot, I can see the exit wound clearly pop open from the back of his head like a straw going through the pre-cut slits in a slurpee lid. He instantly goes silent and falls to the ground with a thud, now I hear more noises and more shrieks from all around me. It appears we woke up the rest of his friends....
Journal Entry 4
The undead are now locked in on my position and waves of them from dirty back alleys and busted up backyard fences moan and scream as they come towards me. I begin picking off the closest targets that I can get, headshoting to the best of my ability. I kill probably a dozen but they keep coming, wave after wave. I'm running low on ammo now, I've only got 5 rounds left and there are about 10 zombies close enough to deserve the bullets. I've stupidly backed myself into a fenced yard with no escape route. The only way out is in the direction that the zombies are coming in... crap this is bad... well its been a good run... I take very careful aim and shoot the next 5 zombies with perfect headshots, behind them comes a hoard of about 7 more. I don't think I will be able to charge through them, I accept my defeat and wait for them to get me....
Journal Entry 5
All the sudden I hear gunfire... wtf.... I see flashlights bouncing off the cracks in the fence and footsteps running. I hear machine gun fire and pistols going off everywhere. A group of 3 other players rush in and save the day, a feeling of relief and awesomeness washes over me as they pick off the 7 zombies that were about to make dinner out of me. I join up with the group and follow them onward into the street.
Journal Entry 6
The hoards are getting worse and worse as we progress up the blocks of this pleasant valley neighborhood, Another player states that we need to go hold up somewhere until the waves calm down a bit. We find a reasonably well boarded up house and decide to take it over, we move in clearing room by room. I now have ammo again and am able to help out with the room clearing. Suddenly the waves of zombies decide to start charging the house, the doors are shut and the windows boarded.... it is here that we make our stand, we load up our guns and take our positions.... the screams of zombies makes it sound like thousands of them are outside... we begin to hear the doors getting kicked and smashed.... they are coming through... lets do this!
9/10

Zombie survival FPS
This game was surprisingly good.
The good:
- Random map objectives, makes for good replayablity. The route from start to finish on escape missions change each game.
- You never feel completely safe when wandering around, and death lurks around each corner.
- Good atmosphere
- Multiplayer co-op is great fun
- Populated MP servers
The OK:
- Graphics aren't awesome, but they are good enough.
- Map selection is limited on most servers. The player made maps, which are few in number, aren't applied to any official servers. Which kinda sux. If there were an official server dedicated to player made maps, then maybe more people would play them and make new ones.
Because of the Map limitations, I'd have to say this is a 5-10$ game. It's fun and the servers are populated, so you'll get your moneys worth.
If they ever make a sequel, i hope they add more maps to it though. Give me 5-6 escape mission maps, and i'll drop 20$ easy.
I rate it at 7/10

'Deadlight' is definitely one of the better cheap titles out there in the Steam store. It's story follows Randall Wayne, a man trying to find his wife and daughter in a ravaged Seattle. "How did Seattle become ravaged?" You may ask...Shadows...that's how. I could just say "zombies" but that wouldn't do the writers justice. They're mere title (Shadows) implies that they aren't just the monsters that protagonists have been battling since the 80's, but the remnants of people. This is what makes killing "Shadows" feel much different to taking on wave after wave of zombie. Not only that, but Randall usually fights the creatures one-on-one or just a few at a time, further empasizing the fact that these were once individuals with lives, personalities and families...much like Randall himself.
The gameplay, however, is much less deep but still extremely entertaining. It's a blend of free-running, shooting (of the side-scroller variety) and the odd puzzle here and there. The free-running is extremely smooth and feels even better on a controller. Randall sweeps through buildings and barges through doors with a certain fluidity about him. The shooting also feels solid...most of the time. The scarce ammo makes every shot taken feel like a little life lost but those tense times are near and far between. Now the puzzles are my only true concern. They are simply 'pull this thing here, jump on it, jump to the place you need to go' kind of puzzles. I feel like the devs could've put a little more effort into them and made them slightly more difficult, which would not only make the game better but also give it some more length ('Deadlight's very short BTW).
All in all, 'Deadlight's a solid game and could be considered fantastic for it's price, plus there's a twist which is delivered in such an awesome way. If you were lucky enough to snag this in the sale, don't let it go un-played (or un-installed), as it is one of the best pieces of storytelling I've seen in the post-apocalyptic genre.

I liked a lot about this game.  I disliked some things too but they didn't taint the overall experience.
I'll talk about the likes first.  The game's backgrounds are amazing.  It is obvious that a lot of work went into the aesthetics of the game.  I really liked the story too; I've read that others thought it was weak but I disagree.  The overall plot line was very good; although there were probably things in the story that could have been improved with better editing.  I thought it was very cool that the main character would find various things that helped bring some humanity to the game.  Things like findiing I.D.s, audio tapes, pictures and a diary of the main character really helped add immersion to the story.  I thought that part was excellent.
My dislikes of the game included the occassional difficulty of getting all of the jumps, rolls, etc. perfect in order to pass to the next scene.  There were a couple of areas that took multiple tries to get through.  The worst offender was a helicopter chase scene that must have taken about 15 tries; really?  That was very frustrating.  There was also a big defect that I ran into where the main character fell through the bottom of the world and didn't die; he just kept screaming and falling.  A reload of the checkpoint got past that problem.
My overall impressions:  I think that this was a touching and immersive game with some very cool artistic backdrops.  I loved the artistic details and attention to little things that helped make the world seem more real.  I recommend the game but warn others that it isn't a total masterpiece and has some technical problems.  I felt that this should have been an immersion game with story and beauty first.  If the incredibly restrictive timed button mashing sequences had been removed, the game would have been improved.  Going through these difficult to master sequences of button mashing broke that immersion to some extent; however, never totally ruining the experience.

The golden rule of game development is this: "The game should never kill the player. The player should kill the player." That means that in theory, you should be able to beat a game in one go with no deaths, no matter how implausable that is, because you should never be confronted with a challenge that you cannot beat. Hotline Miami got that right; it was incredibly hard, but in a way that said "You died because you made a mistake in that situation."
Hotline Miami 2 is hard. Extremely hard. But it's not the kind of hard you're going to want.
Let me get the good things out of the way first. The game brings a lot of new elements in, with a plethora of characters with their own fighting styles. Fight as two people at once, dual-weild a pair of machine pistols, play straight up Hotline Miami with the detective, play some levels as a complete pacifist, you have all sorts of new mechanics at work here. Second, the style is the same. Great 90's neo-noir filth everywhere, more pixilated violence than you can shake a stick at.
It all goes wrong with the levels, and when I say "wrong," I mean absolutely insanely wrong. Hotline Miami is designed to be melee-focused, yet entire levels will be devoted to gunplay now. The levels are massive, where enemies can and will shoot you while you are far, far off-screen, or quite literally through two walls. The game might work if you could play it at a slower pace, but it's always on you to kill faster and harder, chaining entire levels together in combos of trial and error, even when the game no longer really supports that playstyle.
Not to mention, the windows. Windows are EVERYWHERE in this game, and they do not help at all. Now when you clear a room, you must also be conscious of the ten people in the rooms surrounding said room, who will gun you down with impunity from every angle. The game's favorite move consists of putting rooms in that seem clear, but unless you distinctly stop and look well ahead of you, will turn out to be a nigh impenetrable fortress of machine gun fire.
Then the small things start piling up. You frequently have to rely on guns, but if an enemy who takes a few hits to down is in front of an enemy with a gun, he acts as a bulletproof shield that you can't fire though, but the AI can. You will frequently die from being shot well off-screen. The combo window is far too short for levels this large. You can't buff the combo window like in the first game either. The executions are a necessary part of playing, because if you don't finish a downed enemy, they can grab a gun instantly and shoot you when they get up. But executions are still difficult to pull off, as sometimes the game just won't let you perform it. They also don't halt your combo window, so if you down an enemy, and get a longer execution animation, kiss your 15x combo good bye.
OH.
AND WHEN YOU PICK UP A GUN FROM A PILE OF GUNS.
IT ALWAYS.
ALWAYS.
GRABS THE EMPTY GUNS FIRST.
I have tested this extensively. It's not random. It's not picking up the last gun you used. It's not the one you're standing closest to.
It's always the empty one.
This is a poor excuse for the original Hotline Miami, and if you buy it, be prepared to smask your keybaord to bits over it, because in all its excitement to add new characters, it doesn't balance things any more.

Though this game is still in an early stage of release, it does manage to make a great gaming atmosphere. Think battlefield crossed with World At War. It's pretty much exactly what you would expect from an open-battlefield World War II game, but it is done well. There are still things to be implimented into the game, but everything that is already in the game is pretty solid.
Playing infantry is probably the most cost-effective, and it does get your pulse pounding a little bit when you are hiding in buildings from a patrolling enemy tank. From the infantry subtypes (Recon/Paratrooper) to the main "Jack-Of-All-Trades" line of infantry, it is certainly enjoyable if you like FPS-style games.
Playing armor is a lot of fun, as having all the power of a tank is an absolute blast. You are still very vulnerable to anti-tank infantry though and aircraft, so it balances out nicely. Stay alert and you will do fine, but if you think you are invincible, you will fall fast.
Playing aircraft can also be a fun experience, chasing enemy fighters out of the sky, blowing apart paratrooper's transport planes, or bombing ground units is all included on the pilot branch. It is an expensive line to play, so fortunately you aren't limited to one soldier.
I have only had the chance to play the "Heroes" side of the game, and have not yet reached the more strategic "Generals" side. However, if you enjoy FPS MMOs, or just like World War II in general, give it a try. The worst that could happen is you try it and not like it.

Most Potential for an Alpha
(written 4/4/2014)
Althought this game currently in alpha it already shows a lot of potential for the future. At the moment however their are many different surface level issues with the game. For example the textures seem somewhat bland, the animations for the characters while correct for the movements involved are a bit offputting and somewhat unnatural, difficult camera controls and the currency for multiplayer is way to easy to obtain. However I suspect that these problems will fizz away, not unlike a can of soda after being poured into a glass.
This games gameplay is fantastic. Creating unique weapons and vehicles puts this a teir above any competition that does not feature said mechanics. The building is smooth and is easy to master. Combat could be better though, using swords has a bit of an mmo feel to it. The online multiplayer works great too. I love the environments and unique creatures featured in the game, even if some of them don't seem to match up from time to time. While Contagion may sound like another generic FPS with tons of zombies, it has much more to offer.
Contagion is developed by Monochrome LLC, the same guys who previously created Zombie Panic: Source (you probably know that one). Game's Source based but don't get all disappointed - the graphics still look pretty amazing for a Source game, as obviously effort was put into that. This doesn't mean that the game isn't optimized - I personally didn't have any lag spikes due to the maps not being optimized, and I could play on max graphics with a Radeon HD 4850. This doesn't mean that your grandma's computer will be able to run this, though - the graphics do take their toll on your hardware.
The game has Workshop support as well, making customizing the game as easy as never before. It also has an SDK for those guys who know how to release skins for Source games and such ;)
Contagion takes place in some sort of global zombie apocalypse event, in a city called Roanoke or something. There are a few gamemodes in this game, probably the highlight of all of those is the Escape gamemode. It's a co-op multiplayer gamemode which supports up to 4 players in a match. The premise of this gamemode is that you have to wander around the map to find the exit, but it isn't your simple hit n' run match - maps are usually randomized, that means that there is more than one possible way to complete the game, that gets chosen while the map loads. So if you beat the map once, don't expect the second time you play it to be the exact same - you will have to find a new path. The maps are fairly large as well, you'll spend probably an hour on each map.
The downside to the stuff I wrote above is that there are 2 maps at this very moment which actually support the Escape gamemode. There might be more made by other people, but I didn't look into it.
Another gamemode which I really liked was Hunted - that gamemode has 4 maps, which I won't spoil. The premise of that gamemode is pretty simple - only one human must survive. This gamemode supports up to 8 players, which randomly spawn around the map. You look for supplies, guns, anything useful and attempt to hunt down the other players. The map is still full of zombies though, so you will have two things to worry about - the zombies and the other players sneaking behind you and killing you when you are completely unaware. Trust me, that happens a lot ;)
Now this game offers some more gamemodes, such as Extraction, but I didn't look into them as well - just those two gamemodes I mentioned before are more than enough for this game already, but it's nice to know the developers added even more to accomodate to different tastes.
When I got the game, it was just a few days after release, so lots of updates and bugfixes were being pumped out, which really made me angry. Not the fact that you had to download the updates - the fact that the official servers had to be updated as well, which usually took a long time and you had no choice but to host a server yourself because you can't play anywhere...
So, the final word; should you buy this game?
YES.

Probably the last game I'll finish for a long time. Deadlight is an atmospheric, post-apocalyptic 2D platformer with some combat in it. I'll keep it simple and tell you what is good and what is, well, bad.
Good stuff:
Atmosphere: graphics, sound, music: everything is chosen very carefully in order to create this amazing post-apocalyptic world. Without a doubt the best part about Deadlight. I also liked the graphic novel artstyle used in the cutscenes.
Combat: while melee combat can be somewhat klunky, gunplay is solid and doesn't feel forced like in other platformers.
Story: while the twist wasn't too much of a surprise for me (OH BOY I KEEP FINDING THESE ID TAGS I DO WONDER IF MY SUBCONSCIOUSNESS IS TRYING TO TELL ME SOMETHING) the story still is solid and Randall is a character you'll truly care for, although it's obvious he has got a few screws loose. The many collectibles, including Randall's diary, are also a great addition to the main story and may make you want to replay the game to gather them all.
Voice-acting: voice acting is solid and while Randall's gruffy voice isn't everyone's cup of tea, I kind of liked it.
Bad stuff:
Controls: platforming often feels a little awkward. Now, I didn't make too much of a deal out of this, even in the parkour segment in the second chapter (to all those people that are whining about that part: git gud plebs), but I still felt frustrated by how often I died because Randall sometimes controls like a stone with legs and sometimes like Sonic The Hegdehog's long lost alcoholic brother. And don't get me started on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fence climbing. WHY WOULD YOU ASSIGN THE KEYS YOU USE TO GO LEFT AND RIGHT TO JUST SWITCH. You just should've made it that if I press right, I go right on the fence, and if I press left, I go left on the fence. But no, we had to find ways to make the player die so he needs more time to play the game so we can justify the price tag.
Length: you can easily complete Deadlight in 6 hours and, besides the collectibles, the three minigames and the Nightmare Mode, there isn't a lot of stuff left to do. I bought the game for a key and one refined metal (thanks for that one David, by the way) and I consider that to be a fair price.
Some really dumb design decisions: most notably the autosave system. Plenty of  checkpoints, sometimes, but you always have to restart from the beginning of a chapter instead of said checkpoint. Why? It just doesn't make any sense. Some of the clunky controls earlier mentioned go here as well. And let's not forget about the sometimes confusing 2.5D: is that one object over there one I can use to climb on or background that will make me fall to my death?
Overall, I give Deadlight a 7/10, and that's because I was a fan of/didn't hate the majority of the game to death. Buy it for a few keys from a trader, though ,because it's not worth the 12 EUR you normally ought to pay to play it.

Hmm. This is a bit of a tough one. I can't say that I've 100% completed it, but as things stand I seem to have beaten the main game assuming there's no secret ending or something.
For starters, this game IS good, but I have issues with it. A lot of them. These are all in comparison to the original.
1. Enemies have bull♥♥♥♥♥♥vision. The new maps are almost all super open hallways, which is alright, except for that even with holding shift and looking at the maximum distance enemies can see you first. Meaning you can be walking up while looking up and die instantly from nothing. Also windows are ALL over in this game, making this game essentially unfair at points. Hotline 1 was a bit cheap at times, but this game goes overboard with it.
2. Levels are too long with too many enemies. This would be fine if not for the game's nature of kind of being a score attack. I loved getting A+'s on the original game. But here almost single zones/levels have more enemies and are bigger than entire stages in the original. This combined with 1 makes reattempting for an A+ incredibly frustrating.
3. This is really opinion based but I enjoyed the story telling of the first much better. Here the story is directly told to you, but there are so many characters and things are split up so much that it feels... Bad? I guess for a lack of a better term.
4. Masks are not done well at all. I initially loved the idea of different characters and extremely different abilities with only a few masks. But then they started to reuse masks between characters, and the 4 playable character thing only takes place for a small amount of stages.
5. Bugs bugs bugs bugs. I've never had a bug force me to restart an entire level but I had dogs walk through walls, guys get stuck on doors and become invincible, guys pick up guns with no ammo and shoot me, etc. Lots of frustration. I hope they patch this game.
On the positive side of things...
1. The soundtrack is FANTASTIC. I'm not sure why they're charging $15 for it, but nevermind that, they outdid the first game's music quite easily. Lots of different artists and they go so well together with a massive OST.
2. When the game plays well, it plays well. Some of the stages that aren't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t are incredibly fun. When the game spaces enemies out and doesn't jam 40 Russians into a single hallway it's usually quite good.
3. The twins are awesome, seriously, one of my favorite things, a bit overpowered but still awesome.
All in all, I don't like it as much as Hotline 1, but I'm still happy to have played it. The game needs some serious tweaking in areas, but I look forward to the level editor and hope the developer will fix some of the design choices.

I have conflicting feelings about Hotline Miami 2.
It has the same visceral action and epic soundtrack that made the first game so memorable, and I really want to like it.  But It feels .... forced.  The level design has changed from being a series of small sandboxes which gradually increased in complexity to sprawling, empty rooms that you are forced to play the same way every time.  Instead of giving you the choice to play the way you want, it seems the developers wish to force diversity on you.   How about we make a character who doesn't use firearms so you have to play a mission using only melee weapons?  Ugh.   Outside of the gameplay there is also a greater emphasis on story this time around,  but that does nothing to improve the game , as Hotline Miami has never really been about story in the first place.   It expounds on the events of the first game in a way that I don't think anyone ever asked for.
It's not a bad game, but it's not the game Hotline Miami 1 was.   I would recommend it for die hard fans of the series who can look past the bad level design, everyone else should just buy the soundtrack instead.  That♥♥♥♥♥♥is legit.

The developers have managed to create fantastic visuals, incredible sound, really good character animations for Deadlight. It plays fluidly, difficulty ramps up gradually and the backstory is pretty enjoyable. The game itself is fairly short, clocking in at a couple of hours not including nightmare difficulty and secret levels and is generally worth playing. The post-outbreak atmosphere is captured well especially in the first few levels and generally throughout the game. Slightly more action-packed than the Walking Dead, but the setting and the overall feeling are very similar.
The big downside to the game (as other reviews point out) is the ending, which detracts from the experience quite a lot. The overall pacing is weirdly off as well, which throws the feeling of danger to the side every once in a while - for example finding pages of your diary all over the place does not help the suspension of disbelief - but if you don't concentrate on the poor pacing, overall the story is alright up until the last 30-ish minutes where pacing and difficulty start to be very glaringly off (there is a sudden and unexpected difficulty spike as well, that doesn't seem to serve any purpose towards the end - possibbly it's to extend game hours slightly). If it wasn't for the rest of the game being genuinely great, I'd probably not recommend it, but as it is, the gameplay is 9/10 and the narrative is a passable 5/10 mainly due to the pacing and the ending so all in all the game is a strong, enjoyable one. Recommended.

I honestly was not expecting much from this game, the developer is unknown and lets be honest, only about 1 out of 5 Warhammer games are even considered passable, let alone good. But I really am enjoying this game.
EXPLANATION AND POSITIVES
________________________________________________________________________________
It is essentially Left 4 Dead 2, combined with a loot/upgrade system, character classes, and set in a Warhammer Fantasy setting.
The combat itself is about 80% melee (depending on what character you are playing) and the melee itself is a mix between Skyrim and Mount and Blade. A mix as in, a lot better than Skyrim (but similar), but not as good as Mount and Blades melee combat.
The Skaven (Rat people that take the places of zombies) are honestly fairly fleshed out, and seem to have alright personalities, they have their own banter towards the characters, and some even cower in fear when you show up, until they decide to mass rush you.
The loot system takes place after each wave, you are given a number of dice (That number changes depending on the difficulty, and what optional things ((Such as carrying around bulky tomes the entire map)) you have undertaken that map) You are then showed a scale of items, and the higher you roll, the better the items. Those items you can go on to upgrade in other ways as well.
The character classes have a bit of overlay, some weapon types are shared (Dwarf and Empire Soldier both get Two handed hammers for instance, but the hammers look and function slightly different), and they can all function well in both melee and ranged.
The characters also have a fair bit of...character....banter is common, and they are all fairly well fleshed out and voiced.
The graphics in this game are, honestly, fairly stunning, the metals, woods, and characters all look very well textured.
________________________________________________________________________________
NEGATIVES OR APPREHENSIONS:
This game is honestly, fairly Warhammer...with that comes a very "grimdark" and different setting, compared to many fantasy games - If killing Ratmen in a claustrophobic cityscape with the help of an alien looking elf is completely distasteful to you, you may want to think twice (But I would urge you to still give it a try).
As I said before, the company is an unknown, a few past interviews have said that they wish to continue supporting it with additional character classes, maps, and enemies. And while I hope they do, only time will tell if they live up to that promise.
The last gripe again, is potentially the setting, I need to stress this: Judging by early access and the games very screenshots, the majority of this games setting is within a giant city, filled with winding streets and cobblestone buildings, I hope that it does not get boring and dull over time.

Reviewed 12th July 2014, full released version
+ Sticking to Romero-esque zombies, no "special infected" zombies that don't really belong to the universe.
+ Basic Gunplay and movement
+ A more grounded L4D in concept
- immserion breaking objects placement: Tools and weaponary that seemingly can be used in the game are more often than not just decorations in maps. And there are literally littered everywhere around the map. Fences that act as wall barriers to make you go through long alternate routes is fine until you see not only zombies, but other suvivor NPCs climb over them with ease.
- Very bad guns balancing. It's ok if I have to do head shots to kill zombies, but it's a bit ridiculous if I have to do a headshot with a shotgun in pin point distance to kill them too. SMGs, ARs advantages are really only just a higher fire rate for me to spam more bullets to hit heads rather than doing more damage or more stopping power.
- Bad resource management and feedback. You will have to guess how much of a type of ammo you have if you don't have the corresponding guns that use the specific ammo. Dropping ammo for team mates that require them is pretty much gonna be a disaster of mess, which it really shouldn't be for a game that is suppose to rely on good team work.
- Each co-op playthroughs has no or very little and quite meaningless variant in paths and objectives, despite what's being advertised to you. Randomization of weaponary really doesn't mean much when the balancing of them are so bad that your pistol will normally do the job.
- The game is fun with friends for the first few times until you have ran through each map once or twice.
- If you are looking for an experience similar to L4D campaign co-op, there is a grand total of 2 maps of that that will take at max 2 hours to complete, with a high chance that you have missed a key somewhere and spending 20 minutes being frustrated looking for it.
- If you don't have friends to play this with, your best bet is the pvp hunted mode as it's the only mode that still has a few players playing in and it's the mode that require the least team work if at all. In which I really have to say that there are just about hundreds and thousands of other shooters that plays and look better, do yourself a favor and play those instead.
- There is not much content, or variations as of this review is written. Surely you can always keep an eye on steam workshop for actual extra content, but keep your expectations in check until the free DLC hits.

I just happen to come across this game by chance and thought it might be interesting to play. I didn't have the cash to purchase it at the time but a friend of mine actually gifted it as a present and I was on my way. At first glance getting into the game was quite interesting with different styles of maps, modes, and objectives. My personal favorite were escape modes which is pretty self explanatory. After getting well adjusted into the game I decide to move up to harder difficulty seeing as that was the only viable option instead of doing straight PVP (hunted). Reason being the overall game lacked content so you often found yourself in repetitive situations ultimately remembering specific locations to give yourself an edge versus other players. To my surprise the difficulty was quite challenging however certain mechanics left the overall experience bland if not just right out horrible. Some examples of this were random disconnections, hit-box for zombie head-shots, and the overwhelming powerful armored zombie that required an large amount of ammo to take down if you aren't good at using melee attack (which by the way wasn't an easy task on extreme). Putting that aside, another problem facing this game was the community. Now, by community I mean specifically the typical run-of-the-mill ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s you'd often see in any online game. See, this wouldn't be such an issues however, with the open mic feature and team killing enabled... Well let's just say the overall game experience dropped to below average. You'd often join games hoping to have some fun but run into horrible people that would kill you on purpose, disconnect and reconnect (which auto-turns you into a zombie) to sabotage the team, or have players just abuse the mic privileges by spewing some toxic things out of their mouths. Now, in order to have fun in this game emphasis on teamwork is required without doubt, it is a must or the game becomes virtually impossible to complete or even be slightly successful at (speaking for average players). To put things in perspective, ultimately the game itself will fall into one of these headings for the majority of players either death by fellow teammate, accidental shots (leading into arguments), players turning into zombie (on purpose), players throwing away valuable in-game-items needed progress (by hiding it), player stalling the game when everyone is dead (on purpose) by hiding in specific areas before progressing to far, players mass looting all items which should be shared leading to the teams inevitable death, or completing the game successfully without any issues. In team-based games such as this one, it is important to work together to better the overall gaming experience however Contagion fails to really address these issues thus the problem persist even today. Granted there is a mute feature which is nice but doesn't do justice. So, in conclusion, if you decide to play this game with friends consider it a decent game but overall short (content wise). If you decide to play by yourself, consider yourself warned and tread lightly. The game itself would best be described as a "pick-up" game in which you can start and stop at any time with no real commitment towards progression or anything of that nature. If you find yourself in the long-haul playing a lot more (for the competitive gamer) I'd recommend a pass on this game altogether, save yourself a headache personally. There are much better games out there. I don't recommend this game.

It's a very good take on WW2 as an FPS. Although it is free to play and it IS doable to unlock all the guns and characters for free it's ridiculously time consuming. I've been playing for about 5 hours at time of review and I've just got a character to lv3. Up until lv3 you are stuck playing in small Domination style maps with 3 points to capture and hold against the enemy. 2 points increases your overal team score. XP is earned through captures and defense of your points. It's the fastest way to level up and forces you to rush the points. XP can be gained from kills but at most you're looking at 7 XP total for a kill (2XP for injuring and 5 for the kill). However a defense kill is worth a lot more and the most I've got from capturing a point excluding kills was 128XP.
Paying out for veteran status increases your XP totals. I'm not sure how much by but considering the "and here's what you could've won!" bar at the end of the match I'm guessing about double. Veteran status however looks quite expensive and is time limited. IE pay x amount of money and you can have double the points for a whole week,
Gameplay-
Standard capture the flag but so much more open. Good use of vehicles and what looks to be a nice variety of weapons (more on them in a minute) A lot of people are still playing CoD style and just running up to the point and don't seem to take notice of the huge space around the edge. Seeing as both teams are coming from opposite sides that does mean you're so very easily flanked. Needless to say I'm taking full advantage of that at present but it's only a matter of time before people realise.
The career path is simple to understand as well. Start off as a grunt with your basic rifle and hand grenade. Get kills and level up and eventually you can start branching out: Tank Driver, Pilot, Paratrooper, Sniper and eventually General. This is nice because it means that you won't just have a full team of snipers hiding out in some burnt out blown up building as you have to earn that right first. Sniper is also one of the last to unlock as well and you have to stay as basic squaddie racking up the points until you get there before branching off into your charachter of choice. General I have no idea how it works as yet but appears that instead of taking part in the FPS aspect there's some kind of strategy game going on. I'm not a huge strategy fan and haven't even got close to being that high ranking yet so I'll hold judgement for now.
Graphically the game IS lacking, but it's also in beta and they're still adding gameplay mechanics and modes and honestly I'm all for that first off. A recent update has just added the Russians in to the game including their weapons and vehicles. Previously it was just the Allies (Americans) and the Germans. Eventually we may even see the other countries join as well. Although it's a bit dated looking the basics are down pat. This game has the potential to be a big deal, but like any other indev game, it needs work.
First, I'll talk about the positive things the game offers at the moment.
Environment- The world has such an original look to it. There's a huge variety of trees, greenery, and plants, all of which are obtainable, can be interacted with, and all have their own uses. This brings such a rich experience to adventuring, something a lot of other voxel games don't seem to understand. Variety.
Wildlife - I absolutely love the critters you come in contact with in this game. They are all so unique, and so diverse. It really does feel like a world that could exist. I have to admit, this is what pulled me in to this game. Some creatures are hostile towards you, some are passive, and some are only hostile if provoked. There is also a touch of ecology with the animals. Some animals prey on others, so again, this is something that really helps make the world feel alive. You got the Hoolock Gibbon, a small goblin/monkey type creature that travels in packs and will attack with rocks if threatened, the Testudo Mariturtle that is breathtakingly massive, and much much more in between. Just watching them walk around is an experience (especially in the forest). What I hope to get out of this game in the future is more AI with creatures. I would love to see specific creatures eat and forage their own favorite vegetation, and interact with the player and other creatures in many other different ways.
Interaction - Imagine playing a game like Skyrim, now imagine that you can interact with everything in the world. Chop down trees, dig a hole in the ground, carve your own cave out of the side of a mountain, whatever you wish. This is what Planet Explorers offers. You can mine loads of different materials, whether it be marble or limestone, and build with it as you please There are loads of shapes to choose from. You can make ramps, stairs...ummm...pointy thingies. Seriously, there is no limits here. This is voxel at its finest.
Customization - Planet Explorers takes interaction to the next level. With the materials that you obtain in the game, you can make your own weapons (Whether it be guns or melee weapons), and vehicles (whether it be for the ground or the air). Literally create the look, the size, and the color. This is an amazing feature. Now, I have to say, it can be a bit overwhelming, and it requires a good deal of learning, but in this case, learning is rewarding. There is truly no limit to what you can make.
Now, for the things that need work.
Controls- This game begs, and I mean begs to have better first person controls. I find that the game is so much more immersive in first person, and it DOES have a first person perspective, but a lot of things you need to do are more convenient in the 3rd person. Doing some things in first person makes it feel as though you're taking an extra, unnecessary step. I find myself accidentally going out of first person because I forget you can't scroll through your items in your hotbar. You have to use the number keys. Also, while in first person, interacting with some things is very tedious. You can't look down as far as you need to sometimes, and this makes it difficult to mine.  I understand that being in first or third is all about preference, but first needs a lot more love.
Difficulty - Now, this is a tricky one to explain. Simply put: Most enemies in this game are too damn hard to fight. Yes, with good equipment, it can get easier, but there is a very thin line between weak enemy and strong enemy right now. Some enemies take too long to put down. It's not about enemies taking time to figure out as much as its about their HP being too high. Like I said, better equipment makes battles go by quicker, but a lot of these enemies can be encountered waaay before you get the equipment suited to fight them. You can go through a whole set of arrows and still not have taken down an enemy. It's time consuming in a weird way.
Item display - This isn't really a big one on my list, but it is an issue for me. It can be very hard to see what items are, and what your quantity is. I find myself squinting to see how much meat I have, and most of the time, just guess. I would like to see in the future a way to hover over items which would allow for a zoomed in display of them.

Okay, I'm done. A lot of these cons are simply things that need work, and by what I've read, it's going to get it. This isn't actually negative criticism. I'm simply reviewing the game for what it is now. As a whole, the game is well worth attention, and I have no doubt that when completed, it will be amazing. I recommend this one for sure for people who enjoy watching games grow.

What a disappointment.
The level design is a disaster. The maps are far too large and full of enemies with guns. As a result, the fast gameplay from the first game doesn't work at all. You're forced to bait enemies around corners if you want to kill them with melee weapons, because you will die the moment you get out of cover. Walk out just enough for an enemy to see you, walk back and wait for them to come to you. Repeat for every single gun-wielding enemy. This slows the game down immensely and prevents you from getting combos, one of the cornerstones of Hotline Miami 1. The size of the levels means that you will get shot by enemies that you can't even see yet. It will happen again and again and again. Being out in the open simply does not work in this game.
The levels are also filled with windows. You will get shot through them over and over again. The far too common windows combined with gun-wielding enemies prevent you from moving around further. If you dodge one enemy with guns, you will walk into the line of sight of another and get shot. This is another reason why you have to bait enemies around corners, one or two at a time.
Not only are gun-wielding enemies ridiculously common, they have almost perfect aim and incredible reaction times. Sometimes you get shot when you try to bait them to chase after you, simply because they react and shoot you before you can make it back to cover.
Your worst nemesis in HM2 is the door. Doors are very common. Like in the first game, they can knock enemies down. To kill an enemy that has been knocked down, you have to execute them, which takes a few seconds. Doing so in the open and gun-filled environments of HM2 makes you very likely to get shot. It also seems like the ability to briefly dodge gunshots during executions that existed in HM1 was removed, making it even riskier. Doors are also dangerous because they're buggy. Sometimes enemies won't see you if a door is covering even a pixel of you. Sometimes they spot you right away and shoot you before you even can react, although this isn't a problem exclusive to doors. It's a bigger problem with doors however, because if you're looking to bait an enemy through a door, you have to let them see you. Sometimes when you try to do that they won't notice you unless you walk out in the open where you can't avoid getting shot. Sometimes they will instead see you right away, before you expect them to. Trying to shoot or hit an enemy on the other side of a partially open door will often make your attacks go straight through them because of how the hit detection works. It's jarring, not to mention a likely cause of death, to see your melee weapon swing straight through an enemy that is standing in a doorway. That happens fairly often, because enemies like to bug out and stand shaking in doorways.
Instead of mostly following one character like in the first game, the story now has you play as several different characters. That doesn't seem like a bad thing, until you realize that it means that you have a very limited selection of masks on every level. If there's a mask that you particularly like, you don't get to use it on the majority of levels. This also lowers the replay value.
The game is full of odd or outright stupid design choices, some of which are new and some of which were present in HM1. When doing an execution on enemies that are leaning against a wall (and on lying enemies with some guns, I believe), you drop your weapon. That's not only annoying and slowing, but trying to pick up the weapon you want in a pile of weapons is very clumsy. If you want a gun to kill the fat enemy (just like in reality, fat people can only be killed by guns and are immune to all forms of physical contact that isn't a chainsaw or a fist belonging to a tiger-masked man) that is rushing you at just below lightspeed, you're going to grab all those metal pipes instead. If you want to grab a specific weapon in a pile, you have to sort through them one at a time. Random chance still plays a major role, as enemy weapons and behavior is partially random. Sometimes you hit an enemy and he starts crawling instead of dying right away, letting your combo timer run out since he doesn't count as dead. Sometimes that gun-wielding enemy walks to the left instead of the right, seeing and shooting you (quite possibly from outside your own field of vision) as you kill another set of enemies. Sometimes they react slowly and let you rush them, other times they react very quickly. Random chance should not be a factor like this in a game where the goal is to get a high score.
The story is similar to the story in HM1 in the sense that there are a bunch of seemingly random things happening and you never know if something is hallucinated or real, only there doesn't appear to be any sort of point or meaning to it.
The music, while not bad, isn't as good as in HM1.
Hotline Miami 2 is a very disappointing game with severe flaws in its basic design. These flaws can't be fixed with patches, because the trio of overly large levels, gun-wielding enemies and windows would require that either the entire gameplay or all the levels would need to be redesigned. Hotline Miami 1 was a fast game, but Hotline Miami 2 prevents you from being fast due to the inherently broken design. What's left is a mess of a game that clearly doesn't know if it should be a fast arcade-style game or a slow and tactical shooter. The design elements are directly at odds with each other. Play Hotline Miami 1 instead.

There are so many mixed opinions about Ghosts. I have never seen a Call of Duty game debated so hotly, and as a dedicated fan of this franchise, I felt I needed to give an honest review of this game. For those who don't like long reviews let me sum this up in one sentence: THIS IS NOT THE WORST GAME EVER MADE, THAT DOESN'T MEAN IT'S THE BEST EITHER. It ultimately comes down to a matter of taste. No one can agree on everything; it's impossible, there is just to many people.
CAMPAIGN: The single player experience is the primary reason I play Call of Duty games; they always deliver an intriguing story with intense gameplay, action sequences, and mostly interesting characters. So does Ghosts hold up to this formula? Well, yes and no.
The campaign was advertised as being a very deep experience were the player would develop emotional ties with the characters. Well, sadly, I have to say that character development is actually the most disappointing part of this game. The player is only given a few seconds to meet the to main characters and then is pretty much instantly thrown into action without any real time for character development. Yet the whole time I feel like I'm supposed to know these people, but I don't because they never gave me any proper time to learn about them. In fact the most character development you get is from intel that you collect throughout the campaign, but it's viewed seperately in the main menu.
Not to mention the characters themselves just seem bland and uninteresting for the most part. The only truly memorable characters in this are, ironically, the villan, Rorke, and the dog, Riley. Rorke is the only one that seems more developed than the rest, this is mostly because they had an entire mission about his past which explained what happened to him and in turn enhanced his character. No other characters in this campaign got that kind of treatment. Also, he just has a more interesting and lively personality. Now the only reason I consider the dog (Riley) a memorable character is because he is a unique addition to call of duty campaigns. In previous games, any dogs that were encountered were hostile and needed to be killed or avoided. This dog is actually part of your squad; and I need to be honest, I actually liked having him with me. The problem is that he is only with you for 5 OUT OF 10 MISSIONS IN THE ENTIRE GAME! (he also briefly appears at the end of a sixth mission) And after all of the trouble advertising this dog...
Let me give you a comparison. I actually think that the character developement in Battlefield 4 was BETTER than Ghosts. The 3 main characters and even most of the side characters were FAR more memorable in that game. Why? Because the developers took time out of their missions just to develop the characters. Ghosts never did anything like this (except for the mission mentioned above).
I understand that it's hard to get to know people in the middle of a battle, but they could have had at least ONE other mission were they take SOME time to develop these characters like what they did with Rorke. So to sum that up, the characters are easily the weakest I have seen in a Call of Duty game. They're not horrible (technically voice acting and animation is good), just not memorable for the most part. Hopefully, they can expand on them in future installments.
Now, with that said, there are definetly some very enjoyable moments in the campaign. Yes it can be over the top, but what did you expect, it's Call of Duty. That's what it's known for. The FPS mechanics are fast and fluid as always, and the sliding feature is really quite fun. The story itself is good but nothing super special and can be pretty predictable at times. However, the first mission is pretty awesome; it's an intense introduction to this new world. The next few missions feel a tad rushed however, and can be a bit difficult to follow during the first playthrough (and the bugs didn't help). Ulitmately you understand the main points by the end. The missions themselves are pretty fun for the most part, particulalry the last four. I won't give any spoilers about the ending, but it actually left me eager to see what happens next. Personally, I continue to enjoy replaying this campaign.
BUGS: When this game was initially released, it was not optimized for PC at all. Thus, the initial campaign experience was massacred. There were many visual and gameplay bugs including skipping audio, crashes, and broken models (particularly gun sights, making aiming impossible) . But there were two notable bugs that they never seemed to fix: low resolution textures on highest settings, and moving dynamic lights not working. It turns out that these bugs were happening because the settings in my configuration file for Ghosts were set incorrectly. So I had to research which code settings to change and go in to the config program file and change the them manually. Why Infinity Ward left these settings like this initially or forgot to change them back is beyond me. My point is that I should not have had to do all of that work just to make a few simple settings work properly, that's the game developers job! The sad thing about all of this is how much Infinity Ward negleted its PC fanbase initially, especially when that's were they started. Fortunately most of these bugs have fixed.
MULTIPLAYER: Multiplayer is essentially the same as it's always been in Call of Duty. I think the new perk system is an improvement, and some of the maps are pretty cool. I like the idea of creating you own squads, but I don't find myself using it very much. You do earn experience, but it's limited each match and you don't earn barracks rewards. There also doesn't seem to be that many major innovative improvements, even to the maps, though some of the DLC ones are a bit more impressive; however, overall, multiplayer is still quite enjoyable. And yes, the dog killstreak can be annoying; a counterattack of some kind would have been prefered, but I still like the idea of having a canine companion in multiplayer. Hopefully, in future games, they will continue to add more and expand on what already exists in more innovative ways.
EXTINCTION: Extinction mode was an unexpected surprise. This knew four player co-op mode is the first gamemode to incorporate aliens in COD history, and it features intense objective based missions that are quite difficult and long. These missions are all part of an interesting story that subtly and indirectly ties with the main campaign and even influenced a map in multiplayer, implying this could all be happening in the same universe. Unlike zombies, you can customize and level up your character with four unique classes, all customizable. In game, you progress further in an area with progressivly harder aliens as you go. In a sense, it's a bit more linear than zombies, but your objectives are much clearer which in turn potentially encourages more teamwork. Personally, I actually prefer extinction more (and don't get me wrong, I love Zombies mode). I like the more realistic, narrative based, objective driven, survival horde defense mode; also, I think the aliens are cooler to look at than the zombies. Ultimately, however, this comes down to which gameplay style one prefers. Endless hords (Zombies), or mission based survival (Extinction).
I would say definitely give this game a chance. It may not be the best in the series, but it certaintly is still a good game, despite it's initial bugs. Multiplayer is an enjoyable experience, Extinction is a new, interesting, and fun game mode, and definitely intense. The campaign is absolutely worth playing through, as there are very intense story and gameplay moments that Infinity Ward does still excel at presenting. Overall, in it's current stat would give this game a 6.5/10. This game sets the stage for a new series, hopefully Infinity Ward will implement even more innovative ideas in future installments.

Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide is a melee driven game with range attack combos. It has a co-op gaming experience where you play with a party of 4 to slay rat infested villages in the quest for loot.
The combat is set in first person and finding "tomes" in the mission gives you a reward once you complete the map. There are a maximum of 3 tomes you can find on each map. Once you become victorious at the end of the map you have a chance to roll dice to get upgraded loot. The more dice you have is dependent on the tomes your team collected and the extra bonus rolls you found in chests. In my video at the end you can see that you click the roll button and it throws the dice in the bowl. I ended up with a white item because on that run we only got one tome.
There are currently 5 difficulty you can play maps on. 3 are available to play until the game goes live tomorrow. Normal is kind of hard even with voice chat. You can get over ran by swarms of packs easily. Last night I played each map on hard for the first time and even with my blue weapons and trinkets it was pretty ♥♥♥♥ing brutal. We ended up completing each map but one was very close to a wipe. When you wipe in this game you have to restart from the beginning and you get no loot. I've had many wipes.
There are 5 classes you can choose from
Victor Saltzpyre, Witch Hunter
Sienna Feugonasus, Bright Wizard
Bardin Goreksson, Dwarf Ranger
Kerillian, Waywatcher
Markus Kruber, Empire Solider
Pros
-Game play is fun, addicting, and the difficulty is just right.
-Loot system based on completing objectives
-Loot can be obtained for other classes that you aren't playing.
-Forges allow you to upgrade your gear. You can disenchant items to upgrade a weapons unlockable passives or if you have 5 weapons of the same rarity you use them to craft a random item one tier higher. (example- 5 white weapons makes a random green)
-Good price. The game is usually 30 dollars but today you can get it for 27. Sale ends at 12am.
-Something to do when not raiding.
Cons
-Loot is RNG so theres a chance you'll get some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ items
-You have to enable voice chat in the game even to hear people and it's annoying to type this out everytime.
-Cinematic are unskipable. This needs to be changed.
-This one is a personal annoyance of mine that I fixed. I have 2 monitors and while I was in game my mouse wouldn't stay on the game monitor and kept running off to my 2nd monitor so it made combat impossible to turn around. I had to download Cursor Lock. It fixed the issue but made me irritated.
If you have the same issue
*Download and install Cursor Lock
*Check Open Program and search for your steam.exe Should look like
Program Files(x86)\Steam\Steam.exe
*Check Open Program Args: copy and paste this -applaunch 235540
*Check Lock Program Search for your Vermintide.exe file in steam apps
Should look like steamapps\common\warhammer end times vermintide\binaries\vermintide.exe
*Click create shortcut and whenever you launch the game use the shortcut.

This game wlil be enjoyable for anyone who has played its predecessor and found it to their liking. Hotline Miami 2 features longer levels and a greater focus on narrative, allowing the game's normal run of 26 levels to feel quite meaty. Take caution, however; the sequel will force you to adapt to new gameplay styles and situatiuons as the story jumps back and forth like children playing hopscotch. You may be comfortable playing Corey or Detective Pardo in the first two levels, only to find that Jake has a minuscule reach with his fists.
The biggest detraction to gamelay is the combination of oversized maps, long hallways, and the increased tendency of your enemies to be packing firearms. By themselves, these three points aren't enough to be a problem; together, they combine to make some of the levels ridiculously difficult. Some other nuances of level design are questionable, such as the cargo hold of the ship with a door that can hinder your own gunfire. I also thought that locating the ammo boxes in the Hawaii missions to be a chore, especially when you must take down heavy enemy soldiers with your gun as opposed to the knife.
If you can swallow the pill of artificial difficulty that pervades some of the later stages, Hotline Miami 2 is a musical and visual treat that is to be savored. It successfully captures the elements of the first game without being a direct rehash.

tl;dr at the bottom
This was a tough decision, whether or not I was going to recommend this game. I'm a rabid Hotline Miami fan, and absolutely couldn't wait for its sequel to come out. Now that it's here, I find I have mixed emotions on the game. And I haven't even finished it.
This review might change with future updates, but as of March 11th, 2015, this is how things stand.
I find that HOTLINE MIAMI 2 doesn't have the same kinetic flow as its predecessor. Where the first one rewarded you for recklessly slaughtering mobsters using creative combinations of weapons, the sequel builds massive killing grounds where it seems the only viable option is to gun down goons.
There are still plenty of weapons about to pick up, throw, and execute enemies with, but with how large the maps are and how often henchmen carry guns, you may often find yourself shot from offscreen if you go about swinging a baseball bat. This is a huge detriment to the game, as it forces you to hide and bait enemies in closer, or shoot them from afar, alerting everyone else in the area.
This sucks. The new executions are incredibly violent and fun to use, but I can't when I'm forced to bottleneck guys. I feel I'm being unfairly rated for just trying to survive. Having tried to go loud and reckless, I usually can't even kill 2 people before my head is bashed in. I'm sure with practice I can get better, but HOTLINE MIAMI 2 simply lacks the joyful carnage of the first game. It just isn't fun.
I welcome the expansion of the story. It's cool getting different perspectives of the story, and I think it's' appropriate that each character plays differently; each character has a distinct ability or trait that keeps gameplay feeling fresh and varied. However, it does lack the gradual spiral down into madness that characterized the first Hotline Miami; seems everyone is crazy from the get-go, at least where I am currently (about 4 hours into the game). Maybe my tune will change with the ending, but we'll see.
With the episodes of madness going on so often, it all feels like a novelty rather than a unique story point; the gradual degredation of Jacket from Hotline Miami 1 stands very tall over the insane ramblings found in HOTLINE MIAMI 2.
As I said, I was very on-the-fence as to whether or not I want to recommend this game. I almost did, and desperately want to. But as it is right now, it just doesn't hold a candle to the first Hotline Miami. I'm hoping future updates fix things up a little, though the biggest issue is the map layout, and I doubt Denaton are gonna rework entire maps with patches. Maybe they could change AI patrol routes? Who knows.
Also disappointed that the biggest bonuses that come with the digital collector's edition is for another game; HOTLINE MIAMI 2 gives you 6 remixed music tracks, and a character pack for Payday 2. Not even an artbook, not even the full soundtrack. Incredibly lame.
If you haven't played the first Hotline Miami, you can pick this up and enjoy it without having to worry about missing out on story. If you loved the first one, pick up HOTLINE MIAMI 2 with caution.
tl;dr
+Expanded story is creative and well-written
+Soundtrack is phenomenal
+Executions are brutal and feel wonderful to execute
+Unique characters change up the gameplay and add to the story
-Riddled with door glitches (AI and your character getting hooked on doorways)
-Guns are a larger focus in the game, minimalizes melee weapons
-Large maps, though creative, lead to unfair deaths and force players to hide and bait
-Scoring system supports Hotline Miami 1 gameplay, but doesn't work for Hotline Miami 2 gameplay
-Gameplay generally lacks polish in comparison to its predecessor
-Story lacks gradual degredation, everyone is crazy straight away
-Extra bonus content is lackluster, geared more towards Payday 2
Review may change with future updates

Hotline Miami 2 places you into the role of multiple characters with different agendas, with their lives influenced by the events of the first game. Cons -
Playing as Alex and Ash, Ash sometimes tends to be stuck (But even with that being said they were my favourite characters).
While it was expected, we no longer get to choose unique masks, but on a brighter note we do get to select things in certain levels.
Some personal expectancies in the story weren't quite met, then again either I've missed something...Or the end isn't the end.

The soundtrack. All of it. The menu song is just heart-wretching and tear-jerking, beautifully so, but it wasn't only the menu song that moved me. All songs are either groovy, melodic, or generally badass.
Unique graphical style.
Improved difficulty. Frustratingly fun.

Hotline Miami 2 is indeed a brutal conclusion, and the execution was great...
