A good, but short post-apocalyptic 2.5 action-adventure platformer. It's a shame it's so short, as it gives you very limited chances to use the various gameplay elements. An example would be the slingshot, it's literally only used in the second Act. But for the 4-6 hours of gameplay you'll get in a single playthrough, you will not be doing nothing. Something is always happening, which keeps the game from getting boring or stale. Which may have been the reason for it's short length.
The game looks great, and the atmosphere and effects are also good. Which is another reason I wish it was longer, I want to see more of this world. Another thing I like is how dangerous the shadows are. Your character is no super hero, in the times you don't have a firearm, groups of more than three shadows will be next to impossible to dispatch with the axe. So you must use your wits and the enviroment to trap or kill them. And even when you have a gun to use, your constanly worrying about running out of ammo. The platforming is good as well, as it is your character's one true 'power' so to speak. It's your best weapon and most used tool in Deadlight.
The few things I find myself disliking about the game, besides the short length, is the very final section of the game. It is full of glitches that caused me to die more than a couple of times. And the enemy soldiers are for some reason more stupid than the shadows. Even if there's only a few of them, they should have been done better. The story had the potential to be greater than it was, but the game's length probably contributed to it's rushed feeling. As the acting and interactive novel styled cut scenes were well done, even if the writing was a bit off.
Overall, I'd give it a 7.75/10. It's a good game that should be played by lovers of games like Limbo, and State of Decay. (Even if State of Decay is kind of meh)

Planet Explorers is to Space Engineers what Starbound is to Terraria.  More invironments, more things to do, and more work required by the designers.  Both PE and SE have volumetric destructible environments and player-built square blocks everywhere, which can be destroyed easily by enemies.  But PE tries to have a whole Story (actually a series of linked quests), AI enemies and helpers, and a world-based environment as opposed to asteroids.  Planet Explorers also tries to have you build up a colony.  It also channels a bit of the MMO Calypso, but with a colony that is just starting, rather than well underway.
Regards A0.7.5.2:
It is Alpha, and Unity based.  Highest graphical settings on OpenGL are not recommended, but DirctX is fine so far.  There is little optimisation as yet, and multiplayer parties should stay together as digging info is not correctly remembered by all clients if they are far apart.  But there is a lot of expectation, and a playable game as it stands.  I just hope that when they say the version number, (currently A0.752, or in the game 0.7.5.2) that they don't stop when the second part reaches 10.  Most basics are there, and now they need QA and more additional stuff regards the world size and colonies.

"Queues and currency (Hero's and Generals) is a new free to pay ww2 shooter. Players will enjoy action packed server queuing where they will sometimes sit for 15 mins to get into a repetitive, lackluster battle that does not even last as long as the wait to get in. You will face unrealistically spec'd weapons that you can't possibly contend with unless you give us money and unlock them yourself. Join the fun now and get a free veteran account and/or career boost advertisement in your face as often as possible. And remember, the war is not over until we've drained your pockets." <== This should be the description for this game.

Heroes and Generals looks like a Battlefield 1942 reskin, and it is, but much worse. After playing around fifty matches over the course of a week, I noticed a trend. Germany, no matter how far behind they were, would end up winning the match almost every time! As a player who plays the US, I lost a staggering 46 of my 50 matches. Over 30 of them, my team had held the flags for 75% or more, and were on the verge of winning. Yet somehow, Germany won. The game is imbalanced, not only in reguards to W/L depending on your team. The Gold premium currency turns this game into a pay-to-win. Don't want to grind to get a pilot or recon? You don't have to! Just buy the academy trained ones with the rank of Major, and you're all set to win! Don't want to grind for weapons? Don't have to! Buy a PPSH-41 or a sniper rifle right off the bat with real money! Don't want to play for numerous hours to get a tank? Just buy the best one in the game for gold and take it into your first match! Speaking of tanks, almost every time the enemy team had three or more tanks, and my side had none! How is that balanced? The map design is horrid as well. If you get lucky to have your base near the A flag on the forest skirmish map, you can shoot into the enemy's spawn if you move about 15 feet out of A. You can't do that at C, seeing as you're at the bottom of a giant hill with A at the top. Overall, this game is unplayable for me personally, from the gamebreaking pay-to-win weapons, soldiers, and vehicles, to the horrid map design, not to mention that Germany almost always wins, no matter how close to loosing they are. The only saving grace of this game is that it's free to try, so you're not wasting money on it. I would go into how they gave the Me-109 Hispano Mk1 cannons (Hispanos are British made) and the P-38 six MG 151 cannons (MGs are German, and the P-38 only had a single 20mm cannon along with four .50cal MGs.) I'll end my rant there. If you somehow do end up enjoying this game, all the power to you, but right now it's in an extremely unbalanced and broken pay-to-win state. Don't believe me? Look up Robbaz's video on this game, it'll open your eyes.

A sci-fi RPG game with mining and crafting parts but it's not Minecraft so don't come into this thinking you'll be doing the same thing as you were in Minecraft.  For one thing the mining is a bit clumsier and slower.  The crafting side is more powerful but does have a bit of a learning curve to get to grips with in the creation mode where you'll be building vehicles and buildings blueprints.

This game is pretty special and I'm only just scratching the surface of the tutorial.
The cliche would be to write something along the lines of "if you like Minecraft, were disappointed with StarForge and play MMOs then you'll be right at home" but there's so much more to this game. You are often dwarfed by the mountains and lakes, the beasts and the plants that characterise the landscape and there's a lot more to gathering and crafting than just digging until you get lucky and throwing it all together.
You can design your own weapons and vehicles, dig vast underground bunkers in a way I've not seen since Red Faction and create structures brick by brick, alone or as part of a team.
The price may put some people off but this is as good as "value for money" gets. I forsee this being an amazing experience online as the community grows, learns the game and gets creative.

A sandbox single/multiplayer tailored-story-driven or randomly generated RPG action shooter trader vehicular colony-builder farming mining creating exploring game.
Basically, it's the "everygame" at long last, and unlike many Early Access games it's not only living up to its promises but far surpassing them!
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
But the reason I really love this game isn't its gameplay, it's the incredible story they're weaving with the single player, one of the greatest science fiction tales I've seen!
You are one of many colonists heading to planet Maria, a seeminly perfect "garden" planet. When entering orbit a mysterious manmade looking object collides with the ship leading to you and many other colonists abandoning ship in escape craft and landing on Maria's southern continent, while the ship has crashed on the northern continent. You then spend the game rounding up survivors, unravelling the secrets of Maria, the possible secrets of the crew, the tensions between the colonists from Earth and Mars, and uncovering some INCREDIBLE vistas and revelations.
*Update 29/12/15* The 0.9 build was just released and so much has been improved since I last played back at 0.8.
- Movement is now fantastically fluid. A couple of animation issues on certain terrain but nothing you wouldn't expect in a sandbox game.

- MONORAILS!
- MORE STORY!
- Fantastic improvements to the UI. They've really been putting a lot of thought into it.
- Probably a ton of other features, I'll let you know when I've played some more!

Let me start off by saying I've never played Warhammer or Left 4 Dead. Matchmaking FPS's are not my thing and I do not like them.
With that being said, I absolutely love this game. I have stuck with my dwarf sword/board so far and even though right now in beta there are only 3 maps. The game has great replayability.
I will admit sometimes the hitboxes are weird with my ranged weapon and a few little glitches here and there, but nothing game breaking. The AI for the bots is very good, if you get stuck with them. It doesn't feel like you're escorting them.
The game has gear slots that you obtain through running these maps. Higher difficulty = Better chance at loot.
Slots include head, weapon, ranged, and 3 trinkets.
I really hope in the future we get a little more to customize our character, even if it's just cosmetic.
The combat feels like a fast paced and more responsive version of Skyrims combat.
The maps do a very good job at moving along, without feeling like that linear arcade style story.
Very happy with my purchase. I wasn't so sure at whether or not this would be something I would enjoy, but took a shot in the dark and it paid off. I hope the development team continues to make content/DLC/expansions for this game.

Having been mildly curius about Mount and Blade for years, I tried it during the recent free weekend.  Starting out at 2 in the afternoon, I figured I'd play it a bit, decide whether it was worth buying, and still have a fair amount of time to do something productive later in the day.  The next thing I knew, it was almost midnight and I hadn't even eaten dinner yet.
In-game, though, I had built up a mid-sized warband, been taken prisoner a few times, opened a brewery, considered running off to a far away land with taxes I'd collected, and won a tournament after several tries.  Not bad for a day's work.
The single-player is what really shines.  I started with the multiplayer, and while it wasn't bad, it wasn't immediately clear why I'd choose it over Chivalry.  But the immersion in the single-player campaign is great.  Lots of politics, an internal politics system, plenty of opportunities to makes mistakes (even on the easiest setting), and plenty of options for role playing.  And I've likely only scrathed the surface of it.

DEADLIGHT is an action-thriller platformer with Zombie theme. I really like the realistic environments and the slowly expanding range of skills you will need to learn and master in order to survive. It begins with simple jumping and crawling, but towards the end, you will be doing many different things at higher speeds.
The ever present "shadows" (zombies) are reasonably tough - you can easily outsmart them if they are alone, but in greater packs, they present a serious danger.
Environments are top notch - from city streets through sewers, from roof-tops to apartments, it keeps changing and it never becomes repetitive. The platforming puzzles have the right amount of vagueness to them - you will occasionally get stuck, but it should never become frustrating.
Overall, this is a really great game which I will certianly replay.
One playthrough is somewhere between 3-5 hours, with 1-2x replay potential.

I couldnt decide what to write in this review , so im gonna share with you guys my favorite apple pie recipe Enjoy! :D
Pastry
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon salt
2/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons shortening
4 to 6 tablespoons cold water
Filling
1/3 to 1/2 cup sugar
1/4 cup all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
1/8 teaspoon salt
8 cups thinly sliced peeled tart apples (8 medium)
2 tablespoons butter or margarine
1) In medium bowl, mix 2 cups flour and 1 teaspoon salt. Cut in shortening, using pastry blender (or pulling 2 table knives through ingredients in opposite directions), until particles are size of small peas. Sprinkle with cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing with fork until all flour is moistened and pastry almost cleans side of bowl (1 to 2 teaspoons more water can be added if necessary).
2) Gather pastry into a ball. Divide in half; shape into 2 flattened rounds on lightly floured surface. Wrap in plastic wrap; refrigerate about 45 minutes or until dough is firm and cold, yet pliable. This allows the shortening to become slightly firm, which helps make the baked pastry more flaky. If refrigerated longer, let pastry soften slightly before rolling.
3) Heat oven to 425°F. With floured rolling pin, roll one pastry round into round 2 inches larger than upside-down 9-inch glass pie plate. Fold pastry into fourths; place in pie plate. Unfold and ease into plate, pressing firmly against bottom and side.
4) In large bowl, mix sugar, 1/4 cup flour, the cinnamon, nutmeg and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Stir in apples until well mixed. Spoon into pastry-lined pie plate. Cut butter into small pieces; sprinkle over filling. Trim overhanging edge of pastry 1/2 inch from rim of plate.
5) Roll other round of pastry into 10-inch round. Fold into fourths and cut slits so steam can escape. Unfold top pastry over filling; trim overhanging edge 1 inch from rim of plate. Fold and roll top edge under lower edge, pressing on rim to seal; flute as desired. Cover edge with 2- to 3-inch strip of foil to prevent excessive browning.
6) Bake 40 to 50 minutes or until crust is brown and juice begins to bubble through slits in crust, removing foil for last 15 minutes of baking. Serve warm if desired.

It's exactly the kind of sequel you would expect after playing the first one.
Surreal atmosphere, outstanding soundtrack, gory gameplay. But i dont think its the masterpiece one would've hoped for. The story lacks highlights and is hard to follow, since there are quite a few characters/story lines and leaps in time back and forth. And there is a lot more dialogue compared to the original. This is of course related to the longer playtime in general, i think its safe to say its about twice the content of the original. There are hups maps with multiple floors in over 20 levels (i needed 7 hours for a complete playthrough, but i skipped a lot of dialogue).
And you will die thousands of times, since this part is heavily focused on gunplay and if you dont freelook all the time you will get sniped from the edge of the screen. Higher difficulty comes from special enemies with either bullet or melee imunity aswell, overall it feels like you have to play more strategic and cant just rush in and expect to kill everything if you have fast reflexes.
I didnt like the high amount of gunfights because they tend to become really frustrating and take the flow - who defines in my opinion the awesomeness of this franchise - out of the game. A great addition from my perspective are the different playable characters (sometimes fixed, sometimes you are able to choose) with different abilities (e.g. akimbo smgs, killing punches, gun&knife).
Some other weak points are: bossfights with little feedback on what to do to kill the boss, also quite a few glitches and bugs.
But dont get me wrong, i fully recommend buying it, i had a good time playing it and its definitely worth the price.

However nothing in the whole 3 hour experience left a lasting impression and the ending was anticlimatic.  I really didn't know I was on the last stage, and was surprised that the game was suddenly over, I really wanted to shoot down that helicopter that had been harrassing me over and over again... although I admit I was relieved it was over with after some of the ways they found to kill me by rushing my jumps during the journey.
I found a total of 3 weapons throughout the game; an axe, a pistol, and a shotgun.  Your melee attack with the axe is extremely weak, while every gun attack is too powerful, I never had to shoot more than one bullet to kill a zombie while it took about 20 bashes to get the job done with the axe (except for the few decaps, but I assume that was random because I couldn't decap on command).  The ammo is limited in what you can carry but replenished to full frequently, so I wasn't concerned about conserving ammo at all, sapping any element of strategy or suspense.

This game would have been at most mediocre if the developers hadn't decided to stop developing halfway through and let their five-year-olds take over. This game is such a broken, glitchy mess, I'm absolutely certain no one playtested it. I encountered so many bugs during my time with it, I thought I had wound up in the Amazon Rainforest. Turns out I was just playing an awful game. One time, I respawned and my character just spun in circles repeatedly until a guard shot him to death. Another time, I swung my axe and it got stuck in the middle of the air, and my character crumpled into a depressing little ball that probably never got any love from his parents or any other human being in his sad, pathetic life, and blood shot out of his back, and then I died. Oh, but my favorite part is the length of time it takes for you to press a button. They may as well have given you elevator music to listen to at that point, because it feels as if you're riding a hotel elevator that never finds its destination. Just like how this game never finds its destination. Maybe the entire game is just an allegory for life and how we human beings are just miniscule pieces of star dust in the grand scheme of things, whose lives ultimately don't mean anything. But I don't think five-year-olds have the capacity to construct something so compelling. Lord only knows why I actually finished this game. There is a section at the very end that has you running from guards while your character lolls around like a reetarded puppet, and I swear to you if you make it through that without having an aneurysm, I will give you $100. My favorite part is how every achievement is named after a popular song from previous generations. If it were 2007, I'd be dying from laughter. This is one of the worst games I have ever played.

With 20hrs under the belt I can safely say that this game is fantastic.  There is so much to do and so much life to the game.  I will break it down by features.
Graphics:
The graphics are great.  There isn't as much control over what features pertaining to graphics are used but enough to make sure your system can run it properly.  At full quality it looks stunning.  Light permeating through tree leaves, a nice not-over-done bloom effect, AA, it all works great and runs smooth.  Very pleasing to the eyes.  The voxel engine handles very well and even with an older video card, the game handles it all very well and even displays very far into the distance (im using a nvidia 560ti).    The weather is handled very nice and looks good.  Night time is actual night time.  You can hardly see at pitch black and need a torch or light.
Characters:
It is great that they allow you to create your own custom character like sims or elderscrolls games.  The NPCs are active but not to the extent of say skyrim where they have jobs.  They sort of just stand around and walk here and there. You can talk to them and get a lot of story background which is great.  You can even enlist some of them to fight beside you and you can equip them with armor and weapons and whatnot.  The mercenaries have their own set of special skills too.  Some are great with swords and others with guns and so on.  Adds nicely to who you choose to follow you.  I like that the mercenaries reappear beside you when you get too far from them.
Story:
Great story line.  Makes you want to learn more and more about what is going on.  This coming from a guy that usually is not interested in story.  I found myself wanting to know what happened.  That doesn't happen often at all.
Sound/music:
The sound was good.  The music adjusted appropriately depending on where you were and whether or not you were in the area of a hostile enemy. It was a little glitchy but I've read they are fixing that.  Sound effects fit weapons and whatnot.  It could use more attention to vehicles and sounds but overall still good.
Quests:
The quests are your run of the mill quests.  They are good and add to the the story.  They don't always feel quite at all like a grind.  Some can be, but that is normal it seems.  Other quests are more detailed.  I will say there are some bad bugs with some of the quests that require a npc to follow you.  That npc is prone to get stuck at a tree or rock and unlike the mercs that you hire, the quest npcs don't reappear at your side if you move too far away.  I have found that if you have a quest npc with you, if you bring out a vehicle and get in it, the npc will rellocate to your vehicle which is an unintended fix.  This leads to problems early game especially when you are travelling long distances.  When you have quest npcs with you, you can't fast travel.  If they get unexpectedly stuck in a tree you have to travel all the way back to retreive them.  This can be frustrating. There are some quests that you receive early in the game that won't be completed until later.  Many have had problems with this.  I imagine it will be fixed in later versions given this game is only early access.  SOme quests are a little buggy but that is mostly due to the fact that npcs end up getting stuck in random places.  There was one quest involving two npcs and I couldn't complete the quest because one of the npcs randomly got stuck in a mountain side and I couldn't get him down until I dug out the mountain side.
Building:
The game contains a lot of building which is great.  Kind of like minecraft.  You can make your own weapons and vehicles and whatnot.  You require schematics to build things and sometimes require to build one thing in order to build another.  It doesn't get overly complicated though.  The difficulty of the build is often representative of the usefulness of what you are building.  For instance, you can't just easily build a helicopter.  It requires you build a cockpick, rotors, engines, energy cells, etc.  It is a very intuitive building system that takes a little time to get use to but once you are it is very easy to use.  There is a lot of fun to be had.  A lot of creativity that can be used.  I will say the game could do better at helping you understand the proper needs of a vehicle.  I made a dune-buggy type car and I had all the pieces but in game I got this red text at the bottom that told me the car is overpowered or something.  It never really told me why it was overpowered or how to fix it.  The car still worked fine as it was.
Enemies:
There are a lot of animals and enemies in the game.  Many of the animals are docile until you attack them which is nice.  Some of the animals are hostile from the start and it is fun and interesting to see which animals will attack on site and which animals will run right beside you.  The enemies are dangerous too.  Some prefer to sit back and snipe you.  Others will come slinging swords and whatnot.  Some will even mount turrets and will sling rockets and bullets at your face.  The animals and enemies come in all shapes and sizes and the size of the mob usually indicates how dangerous they are.  There are a few points where you fight some extremely large enemies and they can prove quite hard to defeat.  I will say the ranged mobs seem a lot more easy to conquer given they can be dodged easily.
Overall:
Wonderful game with a ton of potential.  It already has a great deal built into and most of what will probably come from later versions is just more content.  I hope they fix some of the not-so-obvious bugs mentioned above (I am sure they will).  Creating your own camp and playing tower defense was really fun.  Being able to craft cars and helicopters and then drive them around was extremely fun.  The game does a great job easing you into the features and concepts of the game.  Very fun and leaves you wanting more (it is in alpha so that is to be expected).  I look forward to future updates and highly recommend you buying this game now if you enjoy rpg and open world sandbox games like terraria and minecraft.  There is a lot of replayability built into the game and right now about 20hrs worth of straight story line with some random quests thrown in.  It is a very balanced game.

Personally I would say this game is a great game, however, I feel there are a few details to know before buying this game. This game was made quite a good number of years ago and therefore the graphics are also a bit outdated so if that is something you can't get over I would not suggest buying this game. Also this game does have a bit steep of a learning curve but once you learn how to play it is definetly worth it.
Now as to why I think this game is so good:
Well first of all there is no story line which some would see as a bad idea but the way Warband uses it, it actually works. It allows for almost any possible course of action to achieve your own personal goals wether it be becoming rich, becoming King, or even marrying a noble lady.
Secondly, the modding community is huge which is constantly adding mods that can increase your experience in the game or even add even more to said experience such as a mod called the Freelance mod which makes it so you are now able to play as a regular soldier in a Lords army.
Thirdly, the multiplayer can have up to 200 players! How many "next generation" games do you hear of being able to have 200 players fighting eachother the the death in brutal and bloody combat.
Fourthly, there is a DLC for this game which I have taken a particular interest in. This mod is the Napoleonic Wars DLC which allows you to play in multiplayer games as a soldier from the time period of Napoleon conquering Europe. This DLC while not having single player (although there is a mod that is coming out eventually that will have singleplayer) seems to draw you in with its organized communities. While the initial prospect of running around in a line and having to listen to orders may seem daunting especially considering that there is generally no space between each person in a line, I assure you it is actually a lot more fun then it sounds. Imagine being able to play as a artillery unit that is able to shoot at unit such as that or playing as cavalry and gloriously charging your enemy and cutting down any that get in your way. Or getting a reputation as a deadly sniper as a part of a skirmisher or line infantry regiment. With 200 players able to play in one server at once all these units can all be in the same server working together. So imagine marching towards enemy positions with artillery flying overhead and the cavalry charging past you while the skirmishers snipe important enemy personel.
I love it, just the feeling that you ARE actually fighting people is amazing. Graphics are wonderful and just the whole game it self.

Contagion is an enjoyable take on the zombie genre that isn't quite as arcadish as Left 4 Dead, but also not as stupid hard as No More Room in Hell. It has a nice balance in difficulty and ease of access to be within reach of most gamers. Just easy enough to be enjoyed, but hard enough (in good ways) that you need to think before blindly spraying bullets.
I would say the weak points of the game are that the missions take WAY too long to play through. I suppose from a certain point of view, the length of the missions invest you in surviving in their latter parts, but the extraction gameplay mode just goes on for entirely too long, especially considering the "Counter-Strike-with-a-twist" nature of death in this game. I think this could be fixed easily, by simply having the server change maps each time a round ends to keep things fresh.
The zombie controls are a bit awkward, but I guess some of that goes with being a zombie. Still, it would be nice if you didn't grind to a complete halt every time you bounce off a wall.
The level design is clean and well put together, and their size is impressive, though the maps themselves are all "inner-city" and seem a bit repetitive. I'm not sure what the lore for Contagion is, but it would be nice to maybe see an underground "Hive" type map for a bit of variety. The objectives and content of the maps does change with subsequent playthroughs, for example playing the "Roanoke PD" map twice, once we had to extract by helicoptor from the roof, and another by car through the garage.
Overall, recommended. It's fun, and it doesn't hurt the wallet very much.

I'm giving it a thumbs down solely on the feelings I felt playing through it. If I had to give it a more accurate score, I would say it would be a 6.5/10, or a "Meh, could have been better."
I got this on sale last winter and I figured that it would be pretty cool. Parkour and zombies and what seemed like a nice looking game. Unfortunately, it has a lot of flaws. The writing is weak, and doesn't do much to flesh out any other character except Randall, and even then, he isn't even that developed. Even after reading the diary entries I still don't feel he's progressed beyond a flat character much, and it doesn't help that the jump in his development only happens about 30 seconds before the game ends.
Gameplay wise, the mechanics are fun, when they work. It doesn't happen often, but enough to aggravate a player when you're just trying to get through levels. The key bindings are all wonky (You need to do a roll by hitting D + SHFT + CTRL and this is pretty difficult in and of itself) and it seems to have been made with a controller in mind. Trying to jump past a part and having your key strokes not respond can screw you over in situations where time is of the essence. You will die. YOU WILL DIE A LOT. Thankfully, this game is merciful and has a ton of save points so it won't impede your progress much, but you will be repeating sections a lot, whether due to controls not responding or just the level design in and of itself. Melee is really weird, and you will probably rely on your guns often, or end up just shoving off "Shadows", as they're called, because scoring a fatal blow is difficult and I honestly don't know how I managed to achieve the few I did. The axe is pathetically useless.
The atmosphere and art are where this game really shines. The graphics are gorgeous; despite being 2.5D the background looks beautiful, and the models seem to do too (when they're not in shadow). Everything feels dark and gritty, and it immerses you into the apocalyptic world Randall lives in. The comic book + motion cinematics grow great with the game, and actually accentuate this atmosphere. I think it's great they stuck with black, white, and red for their cinematics, and kept with a predominately grey/blue for the world.
The voice acting, though, really killed immersion for me, as many of the actors are awful or moderately okay. Randall's voice actor, while sounding like his role, read his lines oddly many times, though for other times he sounded convincing and believeable. The only actors who seemed natural with their roles were the ones who voiced The Rat and Ben.
Overall, I think this is an alright game, but certainly not the best despite all the potential it had. I say get it only when it's on sale for cheap (less than 5 bucks), and get it for the atmosphere, art, and some aspects of the gameplay. Just be prepared for what's in store.

Deadlight is a platformer set in a zombie infested United States. First I have to say what I find refreshing about this game. The main character isn't trying to solve the zombie infestation or save humanity. Hell, he isn't even trying to find out how to cure it or what caused it. And I have to say thank god for that! I'm sick of seeing games where "only you can save us all". It's nice to play a story set inside a world where the characters must react to the environment rather than try to change it.
Ok, now that that's said let's get to the nitty gritty.
As a platformer this game is passable, it's not great but it's not terrible either. There are some moments where it seems the controls a unresponsive or laggy but that may have been my system. Combat is basic and is something of a last resort, you won't exactly be killing the undead hordes.
For the most part this game is a puzzle platformer, working out what what bit to shoot with your pistol or slingshot to collapse thing x or extended platform y.
The art style is nice, although I can't help but feel that it could've been made clearer what is part of the background and what is a climbable surface. Yes, there are hint "lights" to show you what is climbable but when your in one of the 'running' scenes I found little time to actually go looking for them.
It's a short game with not much replay value. If you complete the game on easy or normal it unlocks a harder setting but beyond making the enemies harder to kill there's no noticeable change. The levels have some collectibles that reveal your characters past in more depth as well as give background on world around you.
So overall, yes, it's a good game and you should play it but don't expect a long experience or anything too revolutionary with the control system. I would recommend for the price to drop from its current £9.99 pricepoint though.

This game is probably one of the greatest gaming takes on the zombie apocalypse of all time, and that is saying something for an indie game! It's everything I've wanted in a zombie game: Scarce ammunition, a large map to explore, the idea that any noise from the loudest Revolver gunshot to the simplest footsteps while running can attract an even bigger horde than the one you were trying to fight or avoid. The cell phone system for missions is perfect. From the amount of multiplayer I have played so far, this game is a great tool for teamwork. Survivors were relying on each other for different parts of the mission. Who has the keys so we can get to the armory with all the guns and ammo? Who has the fire extinguisher so we can pass the inferno in the offices? Who has the Fireaxe or Sledgehammer to pummel the riot gear zombie? The list goes on for the roles of each player in the mission, and the fun part is that there's plenty of room for participation. Even the guy who joined the server ten minutes late can still manage to play a pivotal role in the team's survival. This is a great co-op game. One of the best I've ever played. It's realistic, creepy, cooperative, and bloody all at once. Contagion, as of now, is near the top of my favorites list on my Steam library.

Have you ever played Dead Island? It's mediocre, does nothing special and has tons of bugs. Despite that, it's still enjoyable to play with friends and worth it if the game is on sale. I feel the same thing applies to Contagion and if Steam reviews had a rating between yes and no for recommendations, that's where I would put this game.
My first thought about this game was that it simply did not feel finished, or like a retail game. It was then quickly pointing out to me that this is based on a Source game, Zombie Panic. That's what this feels exactly like, a source mod, as opposed to a game you pay for. Although despite this, the game somehow manages to look dated and the animations are shoddy.
Gameplay itself can be quite fun in places, but feels bear. For example, there is one gamemode in which you are given a location you must get to, find supplies and kill zombies. At first, this seemed really enjoyable, there was no map apart from those located in-game as models which was a neat idea but soon we discovered everything felt extremely linear with many of the paths we wanted to take blocked off. You quickly learn this game is not as open world as it seems, which is disappointing since taking multiple routes to get to an objective in a zombie game should be encouraged.
The game also includes a neat mechanic in which if you die, you become a zombie and get to hunt down your friends. This is a good idea and proved to be some fun, however it is somewhat flawed. It is extremely hard to find other players, unless they're close. If you press a button, you get a red filter which is supposed to make things easier, I don't know, I didn't find it useful. Zombies have no trackers to find humans which is probably intentional but when some maps are so big and dark, it can be a nightmare and purely coincidence to find humans. So zombies are probably more fun for people who are actually used to the game and know the maps, but the first time it happens, especially if it's on Barlow Square, it's extremely tedious to do and you will spend ages just trying to find your way around the map.
Another problem this game suffers from is the surround sound is complete and utter garbage. I don't know if this is a Source Limitation or what but on a gamemode like Hunted, which is PvP and is vital for you to be able know where enemies are to stay alive, it can be absolutely frustrating and disorienting.
The game isn't terrible, we had quite a lot of fun on some gamemodes when a bunch of us got together but it just feels extremely hard to recommend, with the tipping factor how much you're being asked to pay for it. If you don't bother with it, you aren't missing much and should probably go download No More Room In Hell instead since they both generally feel on the same level.
However the SDK it comes with has a very nice interface and it's pretty easy to get css/gmod maps into the game.

A game released from early access... that still looks like it's in early access.
Picked this up on sale 75% off and even then it's only just worth it, what's wrong, well:
1) It doesn't look great, source engine may be old but it can still be beautiful, unfortunately this game is not an example, it's hard to put my finger on it, but all the environments feel too "clean", they look pristine, in fact, so much so they don't look real, especially for an apocalypse.
2) The guns, they all feel like toys, cannot tell the difference between any of the pistols, the shotguns have really stupid damage (point blank to the chest wouldn't flat out kill you?) and are buggy and the sniper scope is near impossible to use.
3) It really doesn't feel finished, you can do dumb stuff like run a long fences, the zombie climbing mechanic can never make it's mind up whether you can climb that thing - and will allow you to climb out of the map, and movement feels clunky. As an added bonus, as I found when launching the dedicated server, one of the things it printed to console was "Map is missing dictionary - DON'T SHIP LIKE THIS", even the developers don't seem to think it's finished.
4) The gamemodes - Hunted just turns into free for all, Escape (I think) is just like nazi zombies but with a vending machine that randomly spits stuff out and you all end up running out of ammo, then there's another one which is "lead the AI around" and then there's another one which I don't even remember so it must be great.
5) The phone, pretty much a gimmic, being able to ring people in hunted is good, but beyond that it just feels shoehorned in, in some missions you get to use it as a map, why not all? The game really needs one! Each time I spawn I have no idea where I am, most times because I'm in the dark.
Redeeming features: If you like L4D and got bored of it then you'll probably like this for a couple of days until the four maps get repetitive - more are coming though as free DLC (DLC or 'finishing off the game'?)
Oh and the English is really terrible in places and it behaves really weirdly with a controller.
TL:DR Pick it up for less than £5, no more.

In my opinion, this is the best game in the Far Cry series.  It isn't perfect, but it is one of my favorite games in the FPS genre as it includes stealth and exploration as well.
Story: 8/10  The story of the game is linear and very well done.  The acting is convincing and memorable.  Vas serves as a fantastic enemy, one of my favorite in all of gaming.  The levels are well-developed and super fun.  The downside of the story is the length.  It only takes a few hours to get through, granted you don't deviate from the story (wich I recommend, as it lets you get better guns, skills, etc.).  There are also some creative side-quests, but they aren't necessary to the main story's progression.
Gameplay: 10/10  I don't give out 10's lightly, but this game deserves it.  The game is an FPS, but the guns have very realistic recoil and accuracy, so firefights are often hectic and dangerous at harder difficulties.  The game does a great job of providing different approaches to missions and outposts to suit your preferred gameplay.  You can always go in guns blazing, but you can just as easily sneak around, picking enemies off silently with a bow and arrow or a silenced gun.  The weapon upgrade system is great.  The 'boss battles' are pretty fun too, albeit they use quick-time events.
Setting:  9/10  Rook Island is a tropical island with dense jungles, dizzying cliffs, and blue waters.  There is an abundance of dangerous animals to be found in the jungles, which provide useful pelts when killed.  The graphics are great (for the most part), and a good computer will help enhance the game.  The small villages are convincing and capture the setting well.  There are tons of caves, forts, etc. to explore too.  The only bad thing I find with the setting is the uniformity of the island.  It's all jungle, which can get boring after a while.
Overall, this game is a landmark in the FPS genre, and I would highly recommend experiencing the rich story and rewarding gameplay.

Who wouldn't recommend this game? o.o';
Like for real..? Who wouldn't?.
The game is great, and for a price of 22,99.. hell yeah.
I've been playing the game for 44 hours so far, and I can't get enough.
%Environment-
The world itself, feels incredibly smooth.
The leaves dancing around, as you walk through the forests.. just awesome.
It sort of.. brings the place more to life. It's all about the little things :3
And let's not forget the nature..
They've done a really good job, since it's set on a different planet, many lightyears away;
It'd only be logical to make a new type of nature, instead of the basic trees and flowers we see everywhere.
Let's take one of the tree's as an example :D - The C which fell. <- apparently what I call it >:o.
Like, it's literally a tree formed as a C, but with both ends in the ground; with a few branches sticking out here n there.
I personally haven't seen that one before.
And the awesome flowers which again doesn't seem like everyday flowers, but neither too fantasized..
Some are quite huge and others are tiny; but they're all pretty well made.
For an alpha release, this couldn't possibly get any better.
%Characters & Customization-
I'm all in for customization and eye candy.. I'm just that type of person.
But in this case, it actually doesn't hit me as hard as in other games..
The Character Creation System isn't too advanced(at the moment.)
But you're still capable of giving your character a personality.
Currently there is;
-FEMALE-
5 Female Face Types.
15 Female Hairstyles.(+any colour) (not bad for an alpha, huh?)
1 Female Voice.(no menu)
1 Body Type. (Though you can colour your skin to almost any colour you want.)
And an empty "Other" tab(wonder what'll be added here :D)
-MALE-
4 Male Face Types.
11 Male Hairstyles.(+any colour)
1 Male Voice.(no menu)
1 Body Type. (colour applies here too of course.)
And the "Other" Tab.
-
The characters aren't super HD looking in the Char Creator.
But in the game itself, they're quite good looking.
Plus with the visually shown armor types in-game, you won't need much more :).
%Game Modes-
For an alpha release, they sure have a lot for us to toy around with....
The game currently has three -(+VS Mode online)- game modes in the alpha release;
Story Mode (you follow the storyline + free roam..)
Adventure(+ VS Mode online) Mode (open world free roaming, where you decide what to do)
Build Mode (exactly what it sounds like..)
I won't go indepth with the game modes themselves..
Though I will say that my favorite mode, is Normal Adventure Mode(non-VS) online.
%Creation System-
This feature right here... FREAKISHLY AMAZING.
It's like an in-game simple to use modelling program.
So far it's possible to make:
Swords.
Pistols.
Rifles.
Small vehicles.
Larger vehicles.
Helicopters.
VTOLs.
Battleships(30x60x28 meters..'if i remember correctly..') (flying ones.. not a boat D:)
And Tiny, Medium and Large Objects.
And the best part of this feature? you can import your creations right into the game.
Well, yes in singleplayer, you might say.. NOPE.
The online multiplayer servers have an upload/import function, when you launch the creation system within them.
All of the creations require their respective materials to be made though.
Engines, metal, sword hilts.. fuel.... etc.
All something you have to have in your inventory, before you're able to import your creations.
Now, this feature is too big for me to indepth with.
It's something you have to toy around with.
%Minecraft Comparisons-
Here we go.. another minecraft clone. Right? - Oh hell no!!#$@&^
This epic piece of work deserves its own place in the spotlight.
I don't get why every single game, where crafting and resource gathering is available -
has to get compared to Minecraft.. It's truly sad to see the current generation of gamers and casuals..
And for some reason, everyone seems to forget that roughly 65% of minecraft is community made.
I know of nobody who play Minecraft Vanilla singleplayer/multiplayer anymore.. Nobody..
Everyone plays on modified servers which were made by the community..
Notch made the base game, we made the rest.
%Review-
This is only a lite-review.
I will do a proper in-depth review of the game, once it has been released in it's 'final' state.
Excluding updates of course. Well, perhaps a hotfix or two, after the release. (something always go wrong..)

Warhammer The End Times: Vermintide is a four person co-op action game, very similar to the Left 4 Dead series. It tasks you with making your way through a given map while fighting off hordes of Skaven (giant, humanoid rats) and scavenging for supplies like healing potions, grenades, ammunition, and other potions that augment your character (such as strength or speed).
The enemies you face range from the normal fodder Skaven that come at you in large numbers and are easily dispatched to more specialized versions such as ones that lob poison gas grenades, a hook pole weilding Skaven that will entrap one of the four heroes and slowly drag them away from the group, a poison tipped dual-wielding assassin that will pounce and viciously attack a hero until knocked off and several others. They are essentially mirrors of the special infected from Left 4 Dead, albeit there are a couple different types thrown in, and anyone familiar with how those games play out will catch on to Vermintide quickly.
Where this game sets itself apart from the Left 4 Dead series best (aside from the excellent atmosphere and setting within the Warhammer universe) is its loot and leveling mechanics. At the end of each mission you're awarded experience which allows you to level up and obtain a piece of loot in the form of a new weapon, trinket or headgear. During the mission there are chests containing various items such as healing potions or bombs, but they also have a chance at having cursed die which when picked up augment your chances at obtaining higher quality loot at the end of a mission.
With loot in hand you have the ability to use the forge feature in the game to upgrade green or higher quality items, which is essentially unlocking traits for the weapons. You'll need various types of materials in order upgrade your gear, which you can obtain by salvaging unused items.
Vermintide, while not reinventing anything, provides a very fun co-op experience. It adds some new mechanics that keep things fresh and is set in the excellent Warhammer universe. With the price initially set at $30, and offering five classes and thirteen missions I would say it is definitely a good buy if you're looking for some fun co-op action.

Incredibly similar to L4D with a focus on melee combat.  Overall a fun game but not without issues.
Performance is good overall though I wish the game would give you control over the post processing effects so people with sub-recommended specs could eek out more frames.  The game is CPU heavy.  I have a FX-8320 that I've overclocked to 4.0Ghz.  This is below the recommended CPU for AMD and I experience frame drops down to 30-40fps in heavy fighting and scenic open areas of maps.  My CPU temp approaches 58C and my mobo approaches 65C.  A little high, but doable.  If you have a comparable or lower end CPU be prepared to sacrifice visual fidelity for stable framerates.  I hope this improves after beta or we at least get more control over the graphics settings come launch.
With the exception of the gatling gun rat, the special enemies are carbon copies of L4D special zombies.  Managing supplies throughout the level works exactly the same as in L4D as well.  The developers played it very safe.  You have your main melee weapon, a secondary ranged weapon, a slot for a medical item, a slot for a buff item (extra speed/melee damage), and a slot for a bomb.  Sound familiar?  With Warhammer being such a diverse property, I'm disappointed the developers didn't try something new with special enemies or items.
As you play each level you find tomes.  Tomes are slotted in your inventory over medical items.  Having a tome in your inventory at the end of a level gives you a bonus die for the loot system at the end of each round.  You can also find bonus die on special Skaven.  At the end of each round, you roll dice to determine the quality of your loot reward.  The more die roll a glyph or rune or whatever it is, the better quality item you get.  Total RNG with no care given to what class you're playing at the time.  You could be playing a dwarf and unlock gear for the wizard.  This means you can swap heroes easily to try out new gear, but it also makes finding gear for a specific character you prefer a slog.  Gear can be upgraded to unlock special passive bonuses using material gained from salvaging items.  Alternatively, 5 items of the same quality can be upgraded to a random item of the next rarity level.
Co-op vs AI is the only game mode.  As far as I know, there are no plans for a competitive mode where players also control special Skaven.  At $30, I think it's a fair price for the amount of content promised and replayability via the loot system.  If you were expecting this game to be something more than L4D, you might be disappointed.
Edit:  Skaven have oddly long attack range for melee.  Melee attacks from even basic Skaven can hit you through objects and through other Skaven.  In choke points, you'll often be hit by melee attacks you never see because many of the models mush together.  All characters dodge the same distance and it's often useless unless timed perfectly since enemies will track you when telegraphing their attack.

I'm a bit confused as to whether I should recommend it or not, but I thoroughly enjoyed it a lot so I set the review as recommended, but here's my thoughts:
Hotline Miami 2 improves from the original game in many aspects, notably the art direction along with the music; by using a new, gorgeous soundtrack that perfectly fits the psychotic, drug fuelled violence that makes up the basis of the game and gorgeous pixel art graphics and colours that are actually superior to the first one's especially in animation quality. When the game has its highs, it is ridiculously fun, and you will yourself panting at times from the excitement a level has given you, where you then find yourself still recovering from the adreneline, when you are directed to the score window at the end of the level, it provides a great transition before the next one, but you're still left craving for more of that ultraviolence, whilst you reflect on what did which looked ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.
But, it falls flat in the aspect that some of the levels, if not the majority, fail to caputre the magic that the first game had presented: Quick, reflex based action where every split second counts, and had entire rooms with pools of blood in mere moments, with the body count continously adding up quickly until every russian in the build had his skull split in half. In Hotline Miami 2, some of the levels have taken a design direction where they are more open, enemies are more spread apart and the worse part of this game: Enemies actually see further than you do (if you do not use freelook), this ends up with the player better resorting to using hiding around the corner tactics and taking things slow, or memorising the level as opposed to depending on your reflexes. This completely removes the fun that the quick bloodthirsty action of the original game had offered. In some cases, the levels will also have melee resistent enemies, which just gives the player another excuse to resort to hide only tactics, and prevents the player from dealing with levels quickly through melee and simply stick to ''sniping''
On top of that, the controls seem to have gotten worse, the mouse aiming is incredibly clunky and 80% of the time my character either fails to pick up a weapon when prompted to do so or picks up the weapon furthest from him as opposed to the one he is standing up. The controls can easily be fixed and I hope to see a patch in the future, which could also apply to enemy line of sight. Unfortunately, as for the levels that suffer from poor design, the only thing that could make up for it is if Dennaton Games released a level editor, because they seem to have forgotten what made the levels in the first game so great, so the design may be better off left to the fans.
It's still Hotline Miami: Psychotic, mindless killing to a fitting and great soundtrack, complimented by beautiful colours in a pixel graphics format, but Dennaton seems to have forgotten what made the audience of the first game enjoy hurting people so damn much.

As a huge fan of the first Hotline Miami I had high hopes for this game. Even if this did not blow me away (pun semi-intended) it is still a really good game. Gameplaywise it's more of the same with some minor twists. I really like how the developers mixed up the masks and made them have a way larger impact on play, as well as removing a whole bunch of the superfluous ones, though you don't game to use them nearly enough. Other than some pretty annoying bugs it's great. The levels are long, varied and has a good amount of difficulty to them. One of the biggest parts of the first game was the music and I thought would have a hard time stepping it up from the first game. Luckily the music is outstanding, absolutely amazing work by all artists involved. Just like in the first game the presentation is almost hypnotizing at times as you execute a well thought out plan and bashing brains out to the pulsing beats. All in all it's well worth the money but thus far it isn't as memorable as the first game. In time it might grow on me but for now it sits as a worthy, though not perfect follow up to a modern classic.
TL;DR A good follow up to the first Hotline Miami, though not as memorable. The music is fan-freaking-tastic, some of the best I've heard in any video game soundtrack.

Contagion is a zombie game with a good portion of realism. It uses the source engine and allow us players to create custom maps which I love it so much.
There are many game modes out there but no tutorial so you are better off by watching the trailer first to get to know about the gamemodes before you get confused will all the new features. For example if you had enough with coop, you can play against other players in a level filled with the walking dead.
The main core in this game is that the zombies are slow and they won't die so easily if you don't shoot his brain! This is very important because headshot differs from brainshot here so aim it carefully on the forehead where the brain is located! There is also the infection rate which can be very high depending on the difficulty.
One of the unique feature is to turn into a zombie which will happen when you are infected or when you died. Your new goal now is to kill all the remaining survivors. Playerzombie are faster than normal zombies and can roar which makes the zombies follows you. You can command zombies to different places and the blending ability is a skill that will turn you into a regular ai zombie as camouflage until you stop the blend mode.
Furthermore the ammo and weapon spawns are all randomly located, the same thing happens on some objectives in escape mode too which boost up the replayability greatly.
The gore system in Contagion is pretty well made. If you have a sharp melee weapon you can cut off almost every bodypart from the zombie. If you cut off a leg they will turn into crawlers. Cutting both arms will disable their ability to attack. All the wounds will be displayed even on shooting. You can even do finishing melee moves if you manage to sneak up behind a zombie.

Far Cry 3 does a lot of things right.
The Open World in the game offers a lot of content aside from the main campaign missions.Racing,shooting challenges with various weapons,capturing outposts and hunting animals.There are probably 30-40 hours worth of game play if you want to 100% the game.
I didn't have problems with Uplay aside from the occasional failure of the Uplay overlay to connect to the servers.There are fixes for every single problem that you may have regarding Uplay and you can also disable the in-game overlay.Or you can simply use the key that you get when you buy it on Steam and play it on Uplay.There is no reason to not buy this game just because of Uplay.
In Far Cry 3 most of the time you will kill endless waves of enemies.Which is fun because each mission is unique in it's own way and there are enough weapons to spice things up.When you are not following the campaign missions,you can capture rebel outposts.You can go Rambo style and kill everyone or you can try to do it in a stealthy way without getting detected.
Hunting is another important part of the game.Without hunting animals,you can't improve your gear.It will be harder and harder to fight enemies so the game kinda forces you to hunt animals.Hunting for me,got boring fast.Most of your prey will consist of herbivores that will run once they see you,and you need to simply shoot them.Tigers,sharks,bears and so on are much more fun to hunt,but in the later parts of the game you can just snipe them from afar.
Driving in this game is very well done and there is a decent variety of vehicles on the island.
(Potential spoilers)
Surprinsingly,the plot is the weak part of the game.You play as Jason Brody.An American tourist that spends his vacation on the island with a bunch of his friends and family.But something goes wrong and everyone is captured by Vaas and his pirates.You go from Jason Brody,a young rich American to a killing machine and expert assassin in about 10 minutes.Most of the stuff that happens,doesn't make real sense.The island natives trust you for no reason,Vaas keeps trying to kill you in weird ways only for you to escape over and over and some characters were undeveloped.
Vaas,the best character in the game by far gets too little time on your screen but because he is such a good character you don't even notice that.Hoyt,the main villain after you kill Vaas in a weird vision/dream is undeveloped and is outshined by Vaas in every way.It's a shame both villains get to die in dreams/visions.
Your allies in the game are not particularly good characters.Only Sam the German stands out but he too gets too little screen time.Your friends are boring and you only get to interact with them when you save them and they don't have anything good to say.Dennis is the friendly NPC that helps you in the tutorial but stays along for the ride until the end of the game.Citra is a decent character but the plot doesn't make sense with her in it.
At the end of the game you can choose between two endings.Citra or your friends.Both endings are kinda underwhelming but one of them is particularly bad.
Far Cry 3 is a great open world FPS,with tons of content,a great villain in Vaas and a weird storyline.

This is one of the best single player games I have ever played. I has a rich storyline, with a lots of characters, heart booming events, and an awesome atmosphere.
Singleplayer, as I said, is the best part on this game. There are alots of exciting missions, side missions, quests, and colletcting items aswell, such as collecting hide of animals to craft holsters, plants to craft medicine, or just find collectable stuff, like Relics, Letters and other stuff. There are also a lots of minigames, like poker, racing, ski jet racing, shooting... If you dont like storylines, and rather explore, or do random stuff, you can still enjoy this game.

Its fun to do the missions, but the story of the multiplayer campaign is a bit short. Its still fun to play it, especially at harder difficulty, where its also a bit challenging.
Overall, I rate this game 8 / 10. Its awesome at singleplayer, but a bit boring on multiplayer

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Lets start with the elephant in the room. This game is "early access" which means bugger all. It has been said by many people of the game industry and I will voice the same opinion, if you are using microtransactions (I.E. you are running a in-game store) and are NOT merely testing the system, you really don't deserve to retain the "early access" title.
so that aside, is the game good? The short answer, no. The long answer is as follows.
Pros:
for a "free to play" this has a suprising selection of weapons and vehicles (indeed few WW2 games feature the FG42 for instance)
the graphical fidelity is reasonable given it is "free to play"
the game's core mode (and currently only) is an interesting concept
So what makes this game not worth your time? Lets look at the cons
POOR, POOR Balance, both mechanically and historically, the german weapons are laughable compared to the equally priced American weapons. The SMGs are superior to the rifles, even at range. I cannot tell you how many times I've been sniped by some yahoo trapising around with a Thompson on the other side of the map. the rifle require 5 or more hits to the head to kill anything, but only a few hits for the SMGs to kill.
bugs, latency, and hit detection issues are rampant, the bugs themselves are few, but particularly nasty, one such bug had prevented me from actually playing the game in the first place (like due to the update client they use, as I have similar issues on APB) this disspite running an Nividia 760 TI. The latancy is a particular bugbear of mine, since this actually causes some of the hit detection issues. Rubber-banding is a common issue, especially when the servers actually have people on.
PAY TO WIN. Remember the aformentioned thomson? It would normally take someone about 30 hrs of constant playing (assuming you do not have any wait time between matches) to unlock it, or you can pay $5 and get it instantly. Seriously, this unscrupulous behavior need to STOP.
This segways into the biggest issue of this title, the Devs themselves. The Devs do not take kindly to ANY form of crititism. using the "early access" title as a shield to crititism.
NO! BAD DEV! NO!
You had forfeit the early access perks when you started charging micro transactions. You no longer can cower behind the "early access" title saying "oh we are still working on the game,"
You CANNOT expect to keep your game running for long if you don't listen to your players and FIX the issues they have with your game.
For those whom are considering playing this game, I have a simple suggestion for you, Don't waste your time. If you are looking for a squad-based WW2 shooter, play Red Orchestra 2.

I'm a bit confused as to whether I should recommend it or not, but I thoroughly enjoyed it a lot so I set the review as recommended, but here's my thoughts:
Hotline Miami 2 improves from the original game in many aspects, notably the art direction along with the music; by using a new, gorgeous soundtrack that perfectly fits the psychotic, drug fuelled violence that makes up the basis of the game and gorgeous pixel art graphics and colours that are actually superior to the first one's especially in animation quality. When the game has its highs, it is ridiculously fun, and you will yourself panting at times from the excitement a level has given you, where you then find yourself still recovering from the adreneline, when you are directed to the score window at the end of the level, it provides a great transition before the next one, but you're still left craving for more of that ultraviolence, whilst you reflect on what did which looked ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.
But, it falls flat in the aspect that some of the levels, if not the majority, fail to caputre the magic that the first game had presented: Quick, reflex based action where every split second counts, and had entire rooms with pools of blood in mere moments, with the body count continously adding up quickly until every russian in the build had his skull split in half. In Hotline Miami 2, some of the levels have taken a design direction where they are more open, enemies are more spread apart and the worse part of this game: Enemies actually see further than you do (if you do not use freelook), this ends up with the player better resorting to using hiding around the corner tactics and taking things slow, or memorising the level as opposed to depending on your reflexes. This completely removes the fun that the quick bloodthirsty action of the original game had offered. In some cases, the levels will also have melee resistent enemies, which just gives the player another excuse to resort to hide only tactics, and prevents the player from dealing with levels quickly through melee and simply stick to ''sniping''
On top of that, the controls seem to have gotten worse, the mouse aiming is incredibly clunky and 80% of the time my character either fails to pick up a weapon when prompted to do so or picks up the weapon furthest from him as opposed to the one he is standing up. The controls can easily be fixed and I hope to see a patch in the future, which could also apply to enemy line of sight. Unfortunately, as for the levels that suffer from poor design, the only thing that could make up for it is if Dennaton Games released a level editor, because they seem to have forgotten what made the levels in the first game so great, so the design may be better off left to the fans.
It's still Hotline Miami: Psychotic, mindless killing to a fitting and great soundtrack, complimented by beautiful colours in a pixel graphics format, but Dennaton seems to have forgotten what made the audience of the first game enjoy hurting people so damn much.

As a huge fan of the first Hotline Miami I had high hopes for this game. Even if this did not blow me away (pun semi-intended) it is still a really good game. Gameplaywise it's more of the same with some minor twists. I really like how the developers mixed up the masks and made them have a way larger impact on play, as well as removing a whole bunch of the superfluous ones, though you don't game to use them nearly enough. Other than some pretty annoying bugs it's great. The levels are long, varied and has a good amount of difficulty to them. One of the biggest parts of the first game was the music and I thought would have a hard time stepping it up from the first game. Luckily the music is outstanding, absolutely amazing work by all artists involved. Just like in the first game the presentation is almost hypnotizing at times as you execute a well thought out plan and bashing brains out to the pulsing beats. All in all it's well worth the money but thus far it isn't as memorable as the first game. In time it might grow on me but for now it sits as a worthy, though not perfect follow up to a modern classic.
TL;DR A good follow up to the first Hotline Miami, though not as memorable. The music is fan-freaking-tastic, some of the best I've heard in any video game soundtrack.

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Far Cry 3, what a masterpiece.
Far Cry 3 has to be the best out of the lot they've made, far cry 4 never met the same expectations that I wanted it just felt like a slightly re-textured game and the same engine doing the exact same things. Far Cry 3 kept me playing, Far Cry 4 failed to do that. The Reason Far Cry 3 gets you to this, is engaging a relationship between you the player and Jason. You set out to find your friends after things hit the fan from a planned peaceful holiday. You meet all sorts of unique characters, you're up against an exceptional anti-hero (vaas) and have one of THE most enjoyable experiences playing through the story.
The reason this game is so captivating, is it takes a personal perspective on your own life at home. You have all this deep rooted fun in the jungle, freeing your character (giving you the illusion of freedom of choice) from the basic life you have had. You start to loose your way between your old life, and your new one in the jungle, and the game takes serious advantage of your swayed opinions. The game even drops hints, as your friends/aqquantinces say that you can get lost in the jungle, forgetting who you are - which is exactly what happens. You participate in all this killing, being told by the warriors that you are one yourself and that the people who brought an end to your brother will pay.
The game takes you through a heavy handful of interesting characters and gameplay, with jungle exploration at its best.
Why are you here? To save my friends. Is that truly your answer?

I don't know about this one to be honest, but hear me out.
It's a good game, don't get me wrong, but it sure has it's issues.
There are a whole bunch of features, mainly little things, that differ from the original, but the core gameplay is the same. On the positives, the story is great, and it ties up a bunch of loose ends from the first game. Very trippy and very gruesome. Gameplay is as satisfying as it ever was, more so even, with some awesome new abilites depending on who you play as and whilst I do enjoy all the different characters, I feel that the fact that you are forced down a specific playstyle in most missions makes it much more linear and less replayable than the first. There are only a few missions where you get to choose who you play as, which is a shame.
This is a much, much harder game than the first. I like a challenge, but there's way too much gunplay in this game. It doesn't suit the gameplay. Some missions are basically entirely gun based, and using melee is not a viable option. This makes me sad as the melee combat is the strength of both this game and the orignal. Some missions will be so open, with little cover and enemies that can spot you before you've even seen them (whilst using the shift camera function I might add). It does become very frustrating, not the fact that you die in one hit (I love this feature I should add), but the fact that you will die over and over by no fault of your own.
I'd still reccomend it to fans of the orignal, due to it's awesome story with some seriously awesome plot points. Just be ready to play the same level over and over and over much more that you did before.

Note: I originally had this as a thumbs down, but the creation kit has changed my mind.
This game has great potential, but has a number of issues associated with its alpha state.
The game basically has four play modes: -
- Story; which does exactly what it says on the tin.
- Adventure; in which you jump into the world with some friendly NPC's and the foundations of a settlement to build upon once you have collected the prerequisite materials.
- Build; in which you are given free reign and unlimited materials to build whatever you want.
- Multi-player; in which you can set up a server with friends/ family.
The Bad: -
The combat is sluggish, locks you into animations and largely involves swinging a stick in the general vicinity of monsters.
The controls for vehicles (especially helicopters) need a rework (they are simply poorly realised currently).
The build and multi-player modes barely work, the map in build mode has such short draw distances that the use of any vehicle results in you driving off the edge of the map and dieing.
The story mode is the most complete, but it does involve some needless time sinks, and needs a lot more polish.  It also stops part way through while the remainder is in development- but provides circa 20 hours of gameplay currently.
The Good: -
The story mode is fun (but is orientated towards gathering and crafting).
The creation system, in which you can design weapons and vehicles (wheel based or rotor based), is the high point of the game.  Certain pre-made items are required such as a cockpit or energy cells, but beyond this you can create almost anything you set your mind upon.  Of course to use these items in game (other than in the buggy build mode) you will need to collect the materials first.  There are limitations to the system, for example, building a vast rectangle with rotors all over it will give you better overall stats than taking the time to build a realistic, aerodynamic chopper.  Look at the time I have spent in game, most of them have been spent in the creation system.  If this appeals to you, this game is worth buying.
In conclusion; this is clearly an alpha game, and as such it lacks a lot of polish and features, and is fairly buggy.  Once the development has progressed it should be great fun.

Warhammer End Times - Vermintide is a fun and brutal representation of only a small part of the Warhammer fantasy world. However, this particular part is done with much care given to the universe it has been developed from and the fans who cherish it.
Playing with others I have often heard "I'd never played/heard of Warhammer before this" because this is truly an untraditional take on the Warhammer (typically RTS or top-down squad-based RPG), that does not mean that it is bad. This game is very entertaining, both to those who play and watch broadcasts of it, likely due to the intensity of the combat and beauty of the graphics.
I have a 6Gb GTX 980 Ti and the game looks perfect, I have yet to see any visual errors.
The damage dealt to the opponents is accurate depending on where you slash, bash or blast - with much satisfaction, just you wait.
Granted in its current 3 map stage, it is mostly a grind, but the loot system makes it a fun and challenging grind. Teams work toward obtaining more die to roll at the end of each
that helps them get better gear. Loot dice can either be found in chests, or earned by making the challenge more difficult
. In such an event the game quickly becomes next to impossible without effective teamwork. When one has excess gear that they do not want, they can use them for crafting - which is an easy and intuitive system.
Each character is unique and fun to play, with satisfying and humorous unique interactions depending on the characters chosen (4 of 5 possible).
TL;DR : Similar L4D2 but way more beautiful, engaging, lore-driven, with an intuitive (and potentially very challenging) loot system and easy crafting, features unique interaction among the unique character classes and teamwork is integral to success. Highly recommended, fun to play and stream. ALSO AFFORDABLE.
