Pros:
* graphics are good and are well optimized
* being on the source engine & steam workshop support allows for mods
Cons:
* zombie ai is terrible to say the least. Zombies will freeze (not even from lag) on objects and not move. Other times zombies have gotten close enough to you to attack but then just freeze and not move.
* there are barely any servers and joining a game mode from the default "find game" menu has never worked for me
* BALANCE - zombies will almost always win, even if the survivors outnumber the zombies. I get that it's meant to be a "realistic" game but you should not die from a couple of hits from a zombie irl. If your neighbor turned into a zombie and attacked you a few punches and bites (except to some areas) would not kill you.
* realism - again, this game tries to be realistic but fails miserably. Shots to the main body do almost no damage while headshots do exponential damage; only one headshot is needed to kill a zombie, from any weapon. For example, a shotgun blast to the stomach doesn't even phase a zombie but a glock bullet to the head will kill it. A lack of weapon variety is also unrealistic with only ~20 weapons in the game.
* content - with only ~20 weapons, most of which are uninspired, almost cookie cutter, melee weapons, and only a few maps, most of which are reused for multiple uninspired, boring game modes, this game is not worth $20
* replayibility - again, there are only a few game modes, most of which get tedious fast and are unbalanced. The extraction game mode, for example, has you running around to multiple houses trying to save survivors. However, the game mode is extremely unbalanced due to the game mechanics themselves being unbalanced and unrealistic. I have never seen humans win the round ever, even on "easy" mode.

Since I bought the game I have been playing it for 4 days straight and not even stick of truth was able to keep me engaged so much. This game is basically Minecraft plus with better graphics (compared to other Minecraft-ish games), better mobs (from the cute little woodland critter to giant dinosaur roaming the plain), somewhat better crafting (you can craft modern tools and equipment) and a better story (does Minecraft even have a story except killing the dragon?) Of course there are many aspects that are not on par with Minecraft such as water/lava physics, processing items on other items (putting meat on fire to cook) etc. but we shall see how the final edition will be.
Pros:
1. Best graphics among Minecraft-ish games so far (DON'T YOU EVER COMPARE THIS TO CALL OF DUTY. I AM SICK OF STUPID COMPARISON. CAN YOU DIG YOURSELF A KHAZAD DUM IN CALL OF DUTY?)
2. Somewhat cool story (as a Black Isle worshiper, I can't say I am impressed but the story is at least solid)
3. The world and the atmosphere are awesome. It does give you a feeling of adventuring in an unknown planet with cool (sometimes crazy looking) creatures and weird plants and landscape and ancient ruins.
4. The ability to drive land vehicles and fly helicopters and construct missile launcher/laser cannon etc.
5. The ISO system is fascinating. You can literally create anything you can ever imagine.
6. JET PACK AND GLIDER! seriously, try it out. get to the top of a mountain, run, fire your jet pack, switch to glider at max height and enjoy ;)
7. other minor pros listed by other reviewers
Cons:
some technical issues
1. memory leak crash. It seems quite some people have this problem and I encountered it a few times in the game as well. luckily it does not seem to happen too frequently (for me) and the game autosave every 10 minutes so you won't lose much.
2. lag? not really a con but the game somehow confuses people by including an option in the launcher where you can choose video card. THIS IS NOT WHERE YOU CHOOSE GPU FOR THE GAME. if you are using Nvidia card you have to manually set the game (PE_client) to use your gaming GPU in Nvidia control panel or I guarantee you that your game will lag as cr*p.
3. possible problem with fast travel and sleeping and saving at meteor crate. Some players report bugs that delete all your autosave files when they fast travel from meteor crate and sometimes it involves them sleeping or saving at that location. Personally I didn't encounter any problem but just to put it out here.
4. if you delete your steam and then reinstall steam and play the game using your old save (the same version)... you may see some empty texture in places where you dug. when you jump through the empty texture you will somehow reappear in the sky...
5. I somehow encounter a bug where if you put a roof closely on top of your defense cannons. they will magically appear on top of the roof...
6. multiplayer is still quite buggy so don't expect too much fun from there
gameplay issues:
0. NEED CHANGE ASAP - monster corpses disappear too fast. when you are fighting a pack of monsters, before you can finish the last one, the other corpses may start dissolving already. it is like you have less than 1 min to pick up the loot and it is not cool.
1. NPC SELLS TOO MANY STUFF. you can literally buy everything from NPC with meat. In multiplayer you can even access this one global shop where everything is on sale. I think it is better that only the uncraftable/uncollectible items and some basic starting tools are purchasable.
2. combat still needs a bit of work.
3. can't dig and move at the same time. when you start digging you are rooted.
4. monsters are not very threatening, except that black crab thing. don't know why but black crab can sometimes one hit kill you.
5. can't use weapon while flying with glider (imagine how cool it can be when you rain death from above :D)
6. the bottom of the lake/ocean is always flicking... also the color of your vehicle will be changing randomly if you alt+tab out and get back in the game
7. many objects are not solid, for example, trees. only a small part of a huge tree is solid so you can walk through a tree and fly through a tree but sometimes you can't because that part of the tree decides it wants to be solid and you hit the tree and crash :(
8. the mineral scanner does not seem to work properly when you are moving so you are forced to stand still in order to scan.
9. unlike in MC where you craft items by placing materials in specific ways, this game uses crafting scripts and the crafting script list can be a bit overwhelming later when you collect a lot of them or when you play multiplayer where you are given all scripts at the beginning. although you can search them by types it is still not very convenient.
In summary, a cool game that is still at alpha with alpha problems but definitely playable and just look at the cool features the devs are planning so if you like Minecraft-ish games then try this out. You can't be disappointed, unless you are that kind of player who likes hand holding all the time then why are you playing a Minecraft-ish game in the first place?

The game IS kinda' more difficult than the original, but.... It's not more difficult because of good design. A better word to describe it would be: Frustrating.
For the most part, the difficulty in Hotline Miami 2 comes from a very different place than in Hotline Miami 1. In HM1, the difficulty came from well-made levels and good design, but in HM2, the difficulty generally comes from bad controls, bugs, and horrible level design.
HM2 is a much more gun oriented duck and cover version of the original Hotline Miami. Melee is fairly useless in HM2 and you are punished for trying to use it instead of guns.
I have to say.... I was really disappointed in Hotline Miami 2 when i first played it. It seemed to be a huge let-down.
After i got over that, i tried it again and went much farther into the game.
My opinion has changed and i think i was too harsh on it: Hotline Miami 2 is worse than the original in many ways, but it is definitely its own game. It doesn't completely copy HM1 and it has a feel of its own. While i was disappointed in many ways and i still prefer the original, Hotline Miami 2 has many things that make it special and fun, as well.
The new characters are interesting and fun to use, and the music and art are still very good. I also really like the look of some of the new menu screens and such, like the pause screen and level select.
Overall, Hotline Miami 2 is not quite as good as the original, in my opinion, but that's all it is:
My opinion.
It is possible that many people will like Hotline Miami 2 MORE than the original, as it is just very different.
I would definitely not say Hotline Miami 2 is a bad game, but i would also not say that it completely succeeds as a sequel. That said, i think that every Hotline Miami fan should at least try the game to see if they like it because it's still a good game and brings many new things that the original did not have.

This review dragged on quite a bit, so here's a condensed overview:
Gameplay:
As addictively twitchy and frenetic as HLM1, perhaps a little more
Despite what some are saying, HLM2 is not really any more or less unfair than HLM1 was, but it does throw some curveballs (just like HLM1) and adds additional layers of challenge for even HLM1 veterans
Variety of masks has been condensed, with only a few per level :\
Some missing weapons from HLM1, but some pretty cool new ones
No more human shield mechanic, unfortunately for those who actually managed to be able to effectively use that
Larger levels
Presentation:
As trippy, colorful, and exhilirating as HLM1
A serious crap ton more music
Came with the same sorts of bugs that HLM1 came with initially
Levels are now sorted into VHS tapes by act number
Playstyle indicator is gone
No more loading screen tips
HLM1 tutorial was more effective
Story:
Cryptic and viscious narrative, as before
Larger scale story than HLM1, due to the many sides of the story we get to experience (no longer the story of merely Jacket, but the ripples of his actions through the rest of the world)
Longer dialogue segments
Many playable characters
Unpredictable plot
Not going to be comprehensible to those who haven't beaten HLM1
Now for the more rambling in-depth look into the game I wrote originally. There's probably three questions on your mind if you're looking at reviews for Hotline Miami 2.
1. "Is it good?"
Long story:
♥♥♥♥ing GOD yes. This game, like the first, will blow your ♥♥♥♥ing mind on a pretty much constant basis. The visuals and audio are simply euphoric, some of the best I've ever experienced, and playing the game feels like the closest thing you can get to a cocaine high. It's fast and frenetic and twitchy as all hell, and it will kick your ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥left and right, and yet you love the pain, you keep coming back for more. This game... is THE definition of brutal. And upon beating the game, I immediately continued to play it, even after putting the whole day aside to play it all the way to the end in a single marathon on day 1, getting killed nonstop every two seconds. Usually when I beat a game, I'll retire it from there, or at  LEAST take a breather! And, you know, reflect. But I STILL couldn't get enough of the game. That, my friends, constitutes a very special game. There is something truly ADDICTIVE about this game. This game is one (two?) of a kind. There is no other game out there quite like this.
Short story:
If you want a challenge that will have you shouting profanity at the game in justified anger at every death and yelling with ecstacy the next second at every kill, if you want a game with such a creative and unique style that sets it worlds apart from just about any game you've ever played, if you want a game that is doing something fascinatingly different with how it tells its story, if you want a game that is pleasing in a primal way to all your senses, or if you simply just want a bit of the old ultraviolence, you gotta buy this ♥♥♥♥ing game. And it's filled with so many special moments, fans of the original game just have to see for themselves this new dimension of madness Dennaton Games has constructed. This is the encore performance Hotline Miami deserved.
2. "How does it compare to the first game?"
Long story:
If you enjoyed the thrills and challenges of Hotline Miami 1, Hotline Miami 2 totally delivers, and then some. The gameplay is mostly the same goodness as the original, as good as ever, but with some cool new surprises. Most notably, you play as a whole slew of different new characters, completely distinct from each other, and at alternating points in time. This makes the story much more large scale. It's not just Jacket's personal story anymore, but the impact Jacket's actions have made on the world and its people's lives. You're playing as characters on completely different sides in this web of chaos and killing sprees. The free digital comic illustrates that as well, I recommend checking that out before playing the game. And this large cast of characters makes for a different gameplay experience too, since each level is played with only the certain character for it, and they only use the certain masks that they use. In the first game, you had the full mask selection at your disposal, but in Hotline Miami 2, you can only select from a defined handful for each level. Kind of disappointing that we didn't have just a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton more masks on top of all the Hotline Miami 1 masks. But it's not necessarily better or worse, just different. There unfortunately doesn't seem to be any special hidden collectible like the puzzle letters in the first game either. The play style indicator on the results screen is gone too. I thought that added a little bit of extra fun to the results screen aside from the letter ranking and score, and I don't see why they would've decided to leave that out. Also, you really have to try a lot more just to do what you can to survive, and be happy with your C- and that you even made it to the finish line at all. In Hotline Miami 1, it allowed for a bit of reckless rampaging, but in this one you really can't afford it. You've gotta be a lot more meticulous and controlled with your pace here. There are a lot more enemies in this one, and yet it is harder to get combos, since that just makes it so much easier to die. And they are always placed in just the precises spots to♥♥♥♥♥♥you off the most. Definitely tougher learning curve to these layouts than the first game.
Short story:
I wouldn't consider one game superior over the other. It's an apples and oranges kind of thing. They both are fascinating and mindblowing and fun, but serve a different purpose from each other. It continues to deconstruct the premise, world, and characters of the first game in a really merciless, brutal way and in bold, ballsy new directions. Dennaton did not give you any sort of typical sequel that you would have expected, and it really plays with your emotions and expectations from the first game. Hotline Miami 2 doesn't reinvent the wheel, and yet it does. This game is not a rehash, it's a tangent, and it achieves something completely different from the first game in terms of the narrative, with the same addictive gameplay we fell in love with. Hotline Miami 2 truly nails what a sequel should be.
3. "I never played Hotline Miami 1. Is Hotline Miami 2 a good starting point?"
Long story:
From my experience with it, Hotline Miami 2 is noticeably harder than the first game, even for a seasoned Hotline Miami player such as myself who got all the achievements. Hotline Miami 2 also doesn't really bother much with a tutorial. Certainly not like the first game did, at least. It kind of just throws you right in and expects you to just already understand how Hotline Miami works. The loading screen tips are also mysteriously absent in this one. Also, the story hinges a lot on you being familiar with the events of the first game, and if you just went right to this one, it wouldn't make nearly as much of an impact, and would be just really confusing.
Short story:
No. Definitely play the first game first. It's the right proper thing to do, AND it's cheaper! Hotline Miami 2 would be unnaturally hard for a first dip, since it amps it up even further from the first game, and the story would be baffling and seemingly nonsensical if you aren't familiar with the roots it's stemming from.
By the way, there is a disclaimer when you start the game that there is sexual violence. For those who might be concerned about that, don't be. Coming from the famously depraved Hotline ♥♥♥♥ing Miami, you'd expect it to be a big deal, but it's not. It's right around the end of the tutorial prologue, and all it is is a man hunching over a woman and his pants drop with his bare♥♥♥♥♥exposed. Nothing particularly graphic like the rest of this game is, and it doesn't really warrant that alarming disclaimer in my opinion.

I suppose for a 20ish quid game I cannot complain too much. I have put a lot of time into L4D 1&2 as well as the many mods all you kind people out there took the time to make and perhaps to some degree I am still burnt out from that. Make no mistake this is L4D with a Warhammer skin and a greater focus on melee combat, though there are ranged weapons in the mix.
Even the "Special" Skaven are just reskinned versions of their L4D counterparts, the ogre is the tank, gutter runner is the hunter and I believe its called a pack rat ? (Sorry not down with my Warhammer lore) is the licker thing that pulls you away from the group but just with a rope as oppose to a tongue. These don't even work as well as they did in L4D and it just feels a bit lazy that they just used exactly the same ideas from L4D. There was a chance here to really mix things up and come up with some original new special mobs, though as far as I have seen the gunner is the only one I could say stands apart from the L4D cast.
Despite the several classes each of their play styles soon becomes quite repetitive and new loot in respect of weapons and trinkets do little to change how you play, though you level up there are no skill trees for example.
On top of this there is no PvP at all, one of my favourite aspects of L4D the 4V4 was so much fun (though admittedly flawed) it just added to the package.
Loot is just based on RNG though thankfully you can use items you do not want to upgrade your existing weapons and though a basic loot system it does work well.
Graphically it looks very nice, and runs extremely well though I have heard others complain of tech issues I have suffered none at all other than some minor lag in a couple of games.
If you love L4D and Warhammer or just yearn to kill hordes of rat beasts with a huge hammer then this is worth a look, and unlike L4D it does have some sort of character progression system albeit quite basic. I would say wait til it’s in a sale for £10 or less.

Sometimes there are bad games with good intentions.  This is one of those.
For awhile Contagion sat on my Wishlist, being watched.  I read the reviews and stayed away, but still, it sat there because I have most zombie games worth owning.  It went down to five bucks, and I picked it up.  It's a good thing I waited, because that's all it's worth.
Everything about this game screams that some game dev interns at a college somewhere did it in their spare time, and packaged it as quickly as they could just to have something to sell.  It's a bizarre mishmash of the zombie mode in Call of Duty, the old Resident Evil games, and Left 4 Dead.
Firstly, did you watch that video when the store page opened?  I hope you enjoyed it, because that's all the story you're going to get.  It's also the prettiest graphics you're going to get.  We don't play games like this for story, necessarily, so let's move on.
The sound isn't anything special, and is low budget and forgettable.
One of the features of the game is the ability to use a cellphone.  You'll get text messages on where to go.  The only problem is once I hit the button of "recommended settings" in the graphics options, the cellphone's text was too large for me to read - at 1080p resolution.  So, basically, this neat little feature was useless.
The maps are few, you've probably already read that elsewhere.  Basically instead of making numerous maps, they made a couple, and randomized which gates would be open to provide routes through the map objectives.  It's not a terrible idea, I'm sure it saved them lots of time they spent on - nothing.
Your weapons are varied but aren't particularly satisfying.  The zombies have few animations, get stuck on things constantly, and have no ragdoll physics, so a shotgun blast has no kick, it simply does damage.  1990's, anyone?
The combat's critical in a game like this.  I found it kind of refreshing having to use ironsights on my gun since there's no crosshair.  You can configure your character's bob when they run, and the look and ironsight speeds separately.
You get a flashlight on some weapons.  You can tell they tried to make the lighting effects cool and bounce off different colors on different surfaces.  What it turns out to be is bizarre effects that make you think you're viewing the world through a riot mask that has grime all over it.  Almost useless.
If there's one thing you have to get right in a zombie game, it's the headshots.  Unfortunately, the hitboxes are unreliable.  Much of the time you'll shoot right where your gun is pointing.  Sometimes you'll score a surprising headshot.  But then there are those times when you are DEAD CERTAIN you scored a headshot, but you missed the quirky hitbox.  This is completely unforgivable in a game that specifically limits the ammo it gives you.
Melee is a joke.  There are multiple melee weapons in the game.  As far as I could tell, you cannot score a headshot with them, and they all do exactly the same damage - 3 swipes per zombie.  Since the zombie animations aren't terribly well synced with the damage, they'll frequently get you when you know they shouldn't have, and vice versa.
In a mode that was basically Call of Duty boards-on-windows, one vending machine spews weapons at slow intervals when you hit the buttons, one spews ammo fairly regularly - almost always for guns you don't have.  It was almost fun.
I never did get around to playing on servers with other people.  You can solo, technically.  You'll sometimes require bolt cutters or fire-extinguishers to proceed, and since the game is "realistic", you'll wind up backtracking in a game with no map.
I tried the other map, and at one juncture I emptied 8 or 9 shots into a zombie at POINT BLANK RANGE, and hit nothing but air.  That was it for me.  I have better games to play with friends, and so do you.

Contagion is a standalone zombie survival/campeign/PvP/cooperative game run on the Source Engine. Created by the developers of Zombie Panic: Source, aswell as being inspired by it, the game really stands out apon high quality graphics, gore level L4D2, and it's confusing, long lasting objective campeigns.
ZP:S was my favorite mod for some time. I loved the ambient environment the developers gave to the maps. I enjoyed the concept of NEVER waiting after death, and you get to return as a zombie to infect the unsuspecting,
helpless humans. The objectives it gave to the map were not confusing like in Contagion.
The "Escape" gamemode is rather confusing and really long, I do like long objective based campeigns, but I find it repetitive when the campeigns get you lost all the time. The maps are randomised, so they are incredibly confusing. I, aswell as many other people have been lost countless times looking for a button to open a door.
The gore and graphics are astounding. It's what peaks my eye, it looks fascinating for the Source Engine. This and, 'No More Room in Hell' (another Source mod) are the top 2 for graphically awesome Source games/mods I've ever seen. (This one is number 1).
Contagion still seems incomplete in only some areas, which may be fixed by frequent game updates. If there's anything I can recommend for the game, I recommend adding some maps from Zombie Panic: Source, remastering and implementing them in the game, I think that would be an awesome expirience for the people that have played the mod in the past.

I suppose for a 20ish quid game I cannot complain too much. I have put a lot of time into L4D 1&2 as well as the many mods all you kind people out there took the time to make and perhaps to some degree I am still burnt out from that. Make no mistake this is L4D with a Warhammer skin and a greater focus on melee combat, though there are ranged weapons in the mix.
Even the "Special" Skaven are just reskinned versions of their L4D counterparts, the ogre is the tank, gutter runner is the hunter and I believe its called a pack rat ? (Sorry not down with my Warhammer lore) is the licker thing that pulls you away from the group but just with a rope as oppose to a tongue. These don't even work as well as they did in L4D and it just feels a bit lazy that they just used exactly the same ideas from L4D. There was a chance here to really mix things up and come up with some original new special mobs, though as far as I have seen the gunner is the only one I could say stands apart from the L4D cast.
Despite the several classes each of their play styles soon becomes quite repetitive and new loot in respect of weapons and trinkets do little to change how you play, though you level up there are no skill trees for example.
On top of this there is no PvP at all, one of my favourite aspects of L4D the 4V4 was so much fun (though admittedly flawed) it just added to the package.
Loot is just based on RNG though thankfully you can use items you do not want to upgrade your existing weapons and though a basic loot system it does work well.
Graphically it looks very nice, and runs extremely well though I have heard others complain of tech issues I have suffered none at all other than some minor lag in a couple of games.
If you love L4D and Warhammer or just yearn to kill hordes of rat beasts with a huge hammer then this is worth a look, and unlike L4D it does have some sort of character progression system albeit quite basic. I would say wait til it’s in a sale for £10 or less.

Update:  Since writing this review, I am pleased to say that Fatshark have done outstanding work on the networking and stability issues I highlighted.  The game is now incredibly stable, and I've had no issues at all since launch.  In spite of my skepticism that a week's beta time would be enough to smooth out these problems, Fatshark have actually done it.  Kudos to them, and two thumbs up for an excellent game.  Whole-heartedly recommended.
My original review follows below.
-----
The game itself is fantastic; an updated Left 4 Dead with some fun new mechanics, that makes superb use of the Warhammer IP (if you're a fan and concerned that this is going to be another of the myriad shovelware cash-ins coming out right now, don't be; I haven't seen the Warhammer world depicted so perfectly since Dawn of War).  I'm also a big fan of the way it picks up on Left 4 Dead's trick of storytelling without breaking up gameplay, and the banter between the characters is genuinely brilliant, moreso because you'll only ever have 4 of the 5 on a mission, so you get to pick up different conversations each time.  The weapon and load out choices add a whole extra layer of replayability, and there's more than enough variety to let each player find something they like.  The missions themselves are fun, albeit repetitive, and the game will definitely need a few injections of content to keep it entertaining.  On the other hand, the developers seem to be planning lots of extra levels and characters, so I could definitely see myself putting plenty of time into this, and at a $30 price tag it can get away with being a little lighter on content than some other titles.
So why don't I reccomend it?  Because the game isn't ready for launch, plain and simple.  It's brilliant, and cracking good fun, but the networking issues and frequent crashes (and the fact that a host crashing ends the entire session) make the game barely playable.  Fatshark need to get these problems figured out if they want this game to survive its first four weeks, and I seriously doubt that 5 days is enough time for them to do that.  Another four weeks in beta would have been ideal.
I'm hoping these issues will get fixed, and if they do I'll glad change my review.

For all those who cry about "Pay to Win" there are a few non-cash solutions:
0. STOP THINKING THIS IS COD and play like you actually care about conserving resources!
1. Stop spraying bullets like an idiot. You don't pay repair bills on ammo you don't fire.
2. Learn to Aim: Spending the extra couple fractions of a second to lineup the headshot on the guy who doesn't know your there earns you more rewards.  And learn to lead your target, if he's running and your shooting behind him every bullet is a waste.
3. Surprise: If you just shoot at anybody that moves they know where you are too.  Keep your eyes open and only shoot at what you KNOW you can KILL.  If you win more of the engagements than you lose, your earnings will go up.
4. Consumables, CONSUME money, there is no reason to throw grenades like they are candy.  Just because you have two doesn't mean you have to use them every time every life!  Be judicious and only throw them when you have a reason (i.e. Quad 50, room full of guys, etc.).
5. Your RPG costs you, but the ones that spawn in the boxes on the ground don't.  If you pass that box and don't pick one up, your an idiot.  That is the fastest way to destroy a vehicle (which nets good money) and it costs you NOTHING.  They are very effective anti-infantry tools too. :-)
6. Rank up.  You Pay2Win comment based on your rank 3-4 character doesn't carry much weight.  Your rank pays you more with every match, (see guide below for a good article).
7. Weapon Mods: Just because you can, doesn't mean you should.  Can I trick out an MP40 to be almost as fast as an LMG, sure, BUT that doesn't mean it's a good idea.  Find your play style FIRST, then pick the gun that fits you. Then and ONLY THEN should you start picking mods that compliment you playstyle.
8. Custom Ammo: DON'T USE IT!  The standard ammo is more than enough for almost every gun.  Until/unless you build your OneHitKill gun or whatever you pentultimate weapon is, don't use special ammo.  The ROI is NOT worth it.
9. Steal guns from corpses:  Guess what, you don't pay reapirs on guns you don't have.  I pick up weapons from enemies all the time and there are no repair costs when using one of their guns.  This is a fast, easy and brainless way to cut your costs.
10. Learn the maps: There are places on every map for every playstyle.  If you are trying to take a SMG into a long range engagement your going to waste a lot of ammo (and the cost for it).  Find the best places on the maps for your style (or better yet learn to use multiple weapons effictively and pick them up off the battlefield as needed).
As someone who has several hundred hours in the game I can tell you that it gets easier as time goes on.  Heck just the few gold a day for playing is nice, but you don't need that much.  LONG before I unlocked Recon to get my Sniper Rifle, I had the ingame currency to buy it, all the mods and the custom ammo to make my one-hit-kill beauty.  Given that I run that gun, conserve my ammo, don't use grenades, only shoot what I can hit, lead my target, put myself in the right places and go for headshots, I still earn a tidy 2-5K Profit PER match after repairs.  If I went back to the stock guns it would be higher, but what can I say (Once you go scoped you'll never go back).
Pretend your paying the way for yourself, so make all those shots count.  Remember ammo and parts were scarce in WWII and there were times that people were told to only shoot at things VERY close. The game IS kinda' more difficult than the original, but.... It's not more difficult because of good design. A better word to describe it would be: Frustrating.
For the most part, the difficulty in Hotline Miami 2 comes from a very different place than in Hotline Miami 1. In HM1, the difficulty came from well-made levels and good design, but in HM2, the difficulty generally comes from bad controls, bugs, and horrible level design.
HM2 is a much more gun oriented duck and cover version of the original Hotline Miami. Melee is fairly useless in HM2 and you are punished for trying to use it instead of guns.
I have to say.... I was really disappointed in Hotline Miami 2 when i first played it. It seemed to be a huge let-down.
After i got over that, i tried it again and went much farther into the game.
My opinion has changed and i think i was too harsh on it: Hotline Miami 2 is worse than the original in many ways, but it is definitely its own game. It doesn't completely copy HM1 and it has a feel of its own. While i was disappointed in many ways and i still prefer the original, Hotline Miami 2 has many things that make it special and fun, as well.
The new characters are interesting and fun to use, and the music and art are still very good. I also really like the look of some of the new menu screens and such, like the pause screen and level select.
Overall, Hotline Miami 2 is not quite as good as the original, in my opinion, but that's all it is:
My opinion.
It is possible that many people will like Hotline Miami 2 MORE than the original, as it is just very different.
I would definitely not say Hotline Miami 2 is a bad game, but i would also not say that it completely succeeds as a sequel. That said, i think that every Hotline Miami fan should at least try the game to see if they like it because it's still a good game and brings many new things that the original did not have.

This review dragged on quite a bit, so here's a condensed overview:
Gameplay:
As addictively twitchy and frenetic as HLM1, perhaps a little more
Despite what some are saying, HLM2 is not really any more or less unfair than HLM1 was, but it does throw some curveballs (just like HLM1) and adds additional layers of challenge for even HLM1 veterans
Variety of masks has been condensed, with only a few per level :\
Some missing weapons from HLM1, but some pretty cool new ones
No more human shield mechanic, unfortunately for those who actually managed to be able to effectively use that
Larger levels
Presentation:
As trippy, colorful, and exhilirating as HLM1
A serious crap ton more music
Came with the same sorts of bugs that HLM1 came with initially
Levels are now sorted into VHS tapes by act number
Playstyle indicator is gone
No more loading screen tips
HLM1 tutorial was more effective
Story:
Cryptic and viscious narrative, as before
Larger scale story than HLM1, due to the many sides of the story we get to experience (no longer the story of merely Jacket, but the ripples of his actions through the rest of the world)
Longer dialogue segments
Many playable characters
Unpredictable plot
Not going to be comprehensible to those who haven't beaten HLM1
Now for the more rambling in-depth look into the game I wrote originally. There's probably three questions on your mind if you're looking at reviews for Hotline Miami 2.
1. "Is it good?"
Long story:
♥♥♥♥ing GOD yes. This game, like the first, will blow your ♥♥♥♥ing mind on a pretty much constant basis. The visuals and audio are simply euphoric, some of the best I've ever experienced, and playing the game feels like the closest thing you can get to a cocaine high. It's fast and frenetic and twitchy as all hell, and it will kick your ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥left and right, and yet you love the pain, you keep coming back for more. This game... is THE definition of brutal. And upon beating the game, I immediately continued to play it, even after putting the whole day aside to play it all the way to the end in a single marathon on day 1, getting killed nonstop every two seconds. Usually when I beat a game, I'll retire it from there, or at  LEAST take a breather! And, you know, reflect. But I STILL couldn't get enough of the game. That, my friends, constitutes a very special game. There is something truly ADDICTIVE about this game. This game is one (two?) of a kind. There is no other game out there quite like this.
Short story:
If you want a challenge that will have you shouting profanity at the game in justified anger at every death and yelling with ecstacy the next second at every kill, if you want a game with such a creative and unique style that sets it worlds apart from just about any game you've ever played, if you want a game that is doing something fascinatingly different with how it tells its story, if you want a game that is pleasing in a primal way to all your senses, or if you simply just want a bit of the old ultraviolence, you gotta buy this ♥♥♥♥ing game. And it's filled with so many special moments, fans of the original game just have to see for themselves this new dimension of madness Dennaton Games has constructed. This is the encore performance Hotline Miami deserved.
2. "How does it compare to the first game?"
Long story:
If you enjoyed the thrills and challenges of Hotline Miami 1, Hotline Miami 2 totally delivers, and then some. The gameplay is mostly the same goodness as the original, as good as ever, but with some cool new surprises. Most notably, you play as a whole slew of different new characters, completely distinct from each other, and at alternating points in time. This makes the story much more large scale. It's not just Jacket's personal story anymore, but the impact Jacket's actions have made on the world and its people's lives. You're playing as characters on completely different sides in this web of chaos and killing sprees. The free digital comic illustrates that as well, I recommend checking that out before playing the game. And this large cast of characters makes for a different gameplay experience too, since each level is played with only the certain character for it, and they only use the certain masks that they use. In the first game, you had the full mask selection at your disposal, but in Hotline Miami 2, you can only select from a defined handful for each level. Kind of disappointing that we didn't have just a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton more masks on top of all the Hotline Miami 1 masks. But it's not necessarily better or worse, just different. There unfortunately doesn't seem to be any special hidden collectible like the puzzle letters in the first game either. The play style indicator on the results screen is gone too. I thought that added a little bit of extra fun to the results screen aside from the letter ranking and score, and I don't see why they would've decided to leave that out. Also, you really have to try a lot more just to do what you can to survive, and be happy with your C- and that you even made it to the finish line at all. In Hotline Miami 1, it allowed for a bit of reckless rampaging, but in this one you really can't afford it. You've gotta be a lot more meticulous and controlled with your pace here. There are a lot more enemies in this one, and yet it is harder to get combos, since that just makes it so much easier to die. And they are always placed in just the precises spots to♥♥♥♥♥♥you off the most. Definitely tougher learning curve to these layouts than the first game.
Short story:
I wouldn't consider one game superior over the other. It's an apples and oranges kind of thing. They both are fascinating and mindblowing and fun, but serve a different purpose from each other. It continues to deconstruct the premise, world, and characters of the first game in a really merciless, brutal way and in bold, ballsy new directions. Dennaton did not give you any sort of typical sequel that you would have expected, and it really plays with your emotions and expectations from the first game. Hotline Miami 2 doesn't reinvent the wheel, and yet it does. This game is not a rehash, it's a tangent, and it achieves something completely different from the first game in terms of the narrative, with the same addictive gameplay we fell in love with. Hotline Miami 2 truly nails what a sequel should be.
3. "I never played Hotline Miami 1. Is Hotline Miami 2 a good starting point?"
Long story:
From my experience with it, Hotline Miami 2 is noticeably harder than the first game, even for a seasoned Hotline Miami player such as myself who got all the achievements. Hotline Miami 2 also doesn't really bother much with a tutorial. Certainly not like the first game did, at least. It kind of just throws you right in and expects you to just already understand how Hotline Miami works. The loading screen tips are also mysteriously absent in this one. Also, the story hinges a lot on you being familiar with the events of the first game, and if you just went right to this one, it wouldn't make nearly as much of an impact, and would be just really confusing.
Short story:
No. Definitely play the first game first. It's the right proper thing to do, AND it's cheaper! Hotline Miami 2 would be unnaturally hard for a first dip, since it amps it up even further from the first game, and the story would be baffling and seemingly nonsensical if you aren't familiar with the roots it's stemming from.
By the way, there is a disclaimer when you start the game that there is sexual violence. For those who might be concerned about that, don't be. Coming from the famously depraved Hotline ♥♥♥♥ing Miami, you'd expect it to be a big deal, but it's not. It's right around the end of the tutorial prologue, and all it is is a man hunching over a woman and his pants drop with his bare♥♥♥♥♥exposed. Nothing particularly graphic like the rest of this game is, and it doesn't really warrant that alarming disclaimer in my opinion.

Some people when seeing this game will immeditely think "Yay... another Minecraft clone... again!" and would be partly right since this game offers a lot more.
First : the story mode, which could potentially be considered a big tutorial for the adventure part, is actually worth doing if you are (like myself) an amateur of the "stranded adventures" type, in many occasions I almost expected Captain Janeway beam down and give me a new assignment.
Second : the customization possibilities go way beyond what Minecraft can do (coming from the madman who made the casle of Akashi on minecraft-europe server mostly by himself), both in terms of objects AND in vehicules with some really impresive designs you can import in the game just with a drag and drop in the right folder, even while the game is till running.
Third : the environments are gorgeous ! I was a bit scared to end up in pretty barren lands like you could see in Anarchy Online but through the visual style (which reminds a lot of Consortium and/or Star Wars - The Old Republic), props and mobs runing around you already have, despite the game being in alpha, the impression of being in a living world. It really is a joy to see a pack of wolf like creature attacking a herbivore in the middle of a forest. Some may argue that the graphics are not "Next-Gen" but as Yathzee Croshaw would say "Golden pixels are detrimental to the quality of all other aspects of the game" yet even though the game is definitely not the absolute best looking you can tell the guys put some serious work in making the environments colourful and interesting to travel in (I had to pick up my jaw on the floor a few times in fact).
On the less good parts :
- The game currently has some issues with quest in story mode blocking (a character giving a quest that pops up and dissappear right away or conditions not validating being the most common issues), some people apparently didn't had much problems but I'm currently stuck after 12 hours of questing. Probably somethings patching will correct so I don't mind that much.
- You can shape the land as you see fit in theory only because it is actually quite difficult to accurately mine things, for example trying to mine a perfectly straight tunnel at an angle can become a nightmare really fast because the character is always sliding on slopes, which brings to the next point.
- Controls are a bit cluncky with a big hindrance of the camera not always placing itself in the best angle for the action and the vehicules being a bit difficult to accurately tune in regards to the power/weight ratio and turning angle, meaning a vehicule can have a tendency to do a 180° as slowly as an narcoleptic sloth or beat Sonic the hedgehod to it.
The last point is nor good nor bad, it's actually something any off roader knows : there are no roads (that I've seen) on this planet so do not build a low hanging vehicule as the slightest slope will probably damage the vehicule. So unless you manually build roads leading to New Rome you will always travel in bugies !

The GOOD the BAD and the UGLY:
The Good-
Great Graphics and Audio.
Great environmental ambience.
Great character models and skins.
The Bad-
Combat is too fast paced.
No 3rd person makes it hard to know whats around you.
Not many Hero choices.
The Ugly-
Motion blur must be turned off, its not off by default and will make you puke from motion sickness.
Depth of Field adjustments beyond default results in a mind bending fish bowl vision that will make you puke from motion sickness and make you cross eyed.
A massive gear grind at a snails pace.
Forced to do a few maps over and over and over.
Meager XP.
No loot in maps.
Loot determined by a dice roll and you get only ONE item for all your work.
Players are forced to be greedy, if players each  dont run off at some point and leave your party to the fighting you will not find any healing potions.
Players are forced to run as fast as they can thru dungeons and maps, if there were traps they would die a hundred times over, yet you run and run and run and fight between running and if you stand still for even a second you get dragged off by rats.
In Conclusion-
As much as I love Warhammer and for a short period of time actually enjoyed this game, it gets OLD FAST!
Even worse, the potential of what this game could have been is heart breaking.
Wait for it to be on sale to get your few hours worth before it becomes stale and I cannot even bear to play the game anymore.

I recently started playing Deadlight for the second time and although I was a bit underwhelmed after my first run through, I was suprised to have found a new apreciation for it this time around
Firstly this is one of the most visualy stuning side scrollers I have ever played. The ruined landscapes of a post apocaliptic Seattle and the eerie draemscapes that apear throughout the game help craft the tone and ambiance of the game beautifully, the arwork is in one word "awe-inspiring" but that will be obvious upon first starting the game.
What I noticed this second time arround is the much maligned slugish and sometimes frustratingly inconsistent controls that many saw as on e of the games major flaws actually help illustrate the dire state and mood of our hero and gives us a glimpse of what it must be like to survive a real zombie apocalipse ,remember, this is a guy who is malnourished, tired from constantly having to dodge the undead and incredibly demoralized by the harsh reallity of this ruined world. There is no hollywood glorification here, just a glimpse of this bleak existence on the edge of a chaos.
All of these elements actually helped to draw me nto the game and got me to care more about Randal and his plight.Once I got out of that "rush to the finish line" game mentality I found I was able to pick up on these nuances that made it a much more enjoyable experience this time arround. So if you have already played this game once and felt you would never play it again I urge you to give it a second shot, but this time around relax and enjoy the game dont just rush trough and I guarante that you will enjoy it as much as I did.

Left 4 Dead in the Warhammer universe. Simple enough.
Pros:
-Familiar gameplay (Left 4 Dead)
-Decently smooth graphics on mid-range systems
-Edge of your seat moments when you get cornered by the swarm
-Complimentary classes (currently 5 classes Witch Hunter/Elven Waywatcher/Dwarven Ranger/Bright Wizard/Human              Soldier)
-Special Skaven enemies that keep things interesting before/during/after fights
Cons:
-Rare issues with graphics causing enemies to stretch over terrain
-Item drops will be a grind for now since you get random class drops only after you finish a level
-3 levels at this time, but more will be unlocked once final release hits
Game runs extremely well even on mid-range systems and gameplay isn't overly complicated if you're familiar with L4D. Full release hasn't hit yet, but definitely feels like they put work in to polishing most of the game. There are the occassional grahpics issue where bodies will be stretched from one point to another when they die, but it's not often enough to be any issue. Classes are fun and different depending on which playstyle you want (tank, cc, dps). New items are awarded at the completion of the level which can become frustrating when you can't finish off the level right at the end. Items that are awarded are random based off of a dice roll and can be for any class even if you don't normally play it (I've received a bunch of Waywatcher stuff when I play as Witch Hunter). Fun game that'll keep you busy for a few hours, and looking forward to the rest of the levels becoming available once full release hits.
The base game is worth the money, but the collector's edition is if you really want the rest of that stuff.

Given the fact that the "WW2" type of first person shooter genre is over-saturated, this game holds its own.  While many complain, myself included, that the German BF-109 is overpowered compared to the American P-38, the rest of the game seems mostly balanced.  I've seen an increase in visual quality compared to its beginnings and the weapon damage and accuracy seems to be fixed as well.
My biggest thing however, is the "premium" portion of the game.  It is a free to play game, but if you want a little "boost" to your arsenal and gameplay it costs money.  The Heroes and Generals team call it "Veteran Status".  You get an additional Combat Badge Slot for various tools and perks, as well as increased experience to rank up your soldier.  The reason why I mention this specifically is because the Premium cost for Heroes and Generals is FAR less expensive than other "Free-mium" games such as War Thunder, Star Trek Online, etc.  90 days is about $20 US... which isn't bad if you play a lot, like I do.
Overall I would give this game an 8 out of 10 stars.  It has come a long way since its initial release and I think that if the developers continue to listen to the community and balance out the air combat portion, this game may be high on the replay-ability list for a lot of gamers.
That said, if you're reading this Developers, great job so far.  Keep up the good work, balance air combat a little more (maybe add a British Spitfire or American P-51 to battle the BF-109) and I plan on playing this game for a long time to come.

Okay, lets get something straight -- I do not think that Call of Duty: Ghosts is anything new. It is absolutely not worth $60, nor would I recommend that anyone purchase it for $60; it's essentially DLC with a few minor gameplay tweaks. Call of Duty, starting with Modern Warfare 3 (in my opinion), has been and will continue to be nothing but a rehashed version of previous games with maybe one or two adjustments and a $60 price tag. I don't necessarily think Call of Duty: Ghosts in particular is a disaster, but rather, the whole franchise has become quite a disaster.
However, with that said, I bought the game on sale a couple of days ago and I am actually quite suprised how much am I am enjoying it. It may not be "game of the year" or anything close to that, but I think it's something moderately fun to pass the time. It seems that a lot of the reviews out there for this game are something along the lines of: "This game is AIDS, do not buy.", and no one who actually likes the game is willing to say anything against the popular opinion. It may just be me, but I'm not seeing nearly as many bugs/glitches/crashes as everyone claims to see happen. If you are like me, a very casual gamer, then Call of Duty: Ghosts just may be the game for you.
This is based off multiplayer gameplay (because who buys COD for the storyline anymore?):
- Originality
- Lag
+ Matchmaking system
+ Graphics are pretty good (On my PC anyway)
+ Customization
Final Review: 7.5/10 -- If this game is on sale, or a free weekend comes up, just give the game a try. You might like it.

To get the negative out of the way first: There's around 9 playable characters, but each is available for at most 4 stages. None of them get much plot or any real chance to find a groove like you could in the first game. Things are built up, but never paid off on. I'll be getting in to some low level spoilers from here on, so bare with me.
As an example, The Fans. From the start it's apparent each of them has a different idea about their little vigilante escapades. Tony loves the violence. Ash feels like he's cleaning scumbags off the streets. Corey has reservations about it. But it never amounts to anything. Maybe it's a meta commentary about fans and sequels but if it is, it's really ham fisted and limp.
I can't help but feel the game was rushed, despite it's long development time. Some levels are beautifully detailed with little traces that make them look like real lived in places, but others feel like incomplete user made maps. The Soldier's areas in particular are very unenjoyable.
But what about the good? Well, the soundtrack's a good starting point. I like it even more then the first game's. Some of the gameplay concepts fall flat on their face (again, the Soldier) but others work out great (The Fans are all unique and interesting).
If you liked the first game, you'll probably like Wrong Number. I did. But bare in mind; It most certainly is not the sequel the first game deserved.

This game is either as good or perhaps better than the original. It had the music we all love and the blood gushing action we all yearn for. To make it even better would be the large cast of characters you can play as with their own unique abilities. It allows you play as the character that matches with your preferred playstyle perfectly. So far so good. Surprisingly, I haven't encountered any bugs or glitches yet so that's a plus. My only complaint would be the dumb as rocks AI we're probably used to by now. For now, i'm giving it a 9/10.

After playing two hours of HM2, I can assure you that this game was worth the wait. Brand new levels, characters, "plot", weapons and a great soundtrack. Overall, if you loved the first one you'll love this one.
To start, the level design once again is superb. Playing the different levels was like a breath of fresh air compared to the original HM. The levels were all compatible with the new characters and gave each of them a fair chance to still win, where in the original HM, if I picked a mask that was horrible with that map then I would restart almost on the spot. In some levels, you can see where a certain mask would be used.
There are Five main characters. Corey, Mark, Tony, Alex and Ash (You play as Ash and Alex at the same time). There are also many side characters that you play as, but I feel they are only used to support the plot. I was upset that there were only 4 mask in the game, but these mask are more helpful then most of the mask in HM. Corey allows you to dodge under bullets, helpful for getting away. Mark Allows you to shoot in 2 different directions (see trailer). Tony is the same as in the first game. Alex and Ash are my favorite, as it allows you melee and shoot at the same time. One of them wields a chainsaw, while the other holds a pistol. This is really important for those moments when you need to melee an enemy when another one is far away. Currently, there is a bug that makes ash teleport. I hope this gets fixed soon
I don't understand the plot, but I know that there is more plot then the first game, which is nice.
As for weapons, there is the standard shotgun and lead pipe. With the inclusion of the Chainsaw and the AK, the whole gun lineup seems to harmonize. Although there are a LOT less melee weapons. So if you loved the ninja blade, bad news.
I feel that the new soundtrack is better then the old one. It's a lot more upbeat when it needs to be. Which I felt was something that needed to be changed in the first game. The new soundtrack is a great addition to the game.
Overall. This game is a great sequel that I have been waiting for a long time. Although much more graphic then the first (Hard to believe isn't it). That doesn't change the quality of the game.

Had tremendous diffculty straight away because I couldn't get uPlay to work. Heard the horror stories, but I wanted to believe that as a fairly savy tech guy I could overcome them. I couldn't authenticate with the uPlay servers even after making an account (to play an offline single player game), and the ironic thing was that you can't enable Offline mode unless YOU LOG IN ONCE ONLINE. This kinda put me in a catch-22. After logging on through the website and doing a bunch of googling, it turns out the game doesn't install well over Steam. It was missing a DLL which some helpful dude provided via a standalone uPlay installer.
After getting the game to successfully launch, the servers still were rejecting me (I assumed that they took down the FC3 servers). Every time I pause after a death, it will try to connect to the servers. Super, super annoying, since all of the crafting and stuff is done through that menu.
On to the controls. I know this is a console port, so I used a controller. Even still, the control scheme is horrendous. I thought that it would be like a 'getting used to' situation but it's just wonky and bad. Can't switch weapons with the control pad, but you can accidentally administer syringes with it. Gun selection is on shoulder button, but you can't be pressing another button while it's happening or it gets messed up. You have to open the menu, THEN point to what gun you want.
Back to the start menu gripes: There's a hot tip system that hijacks your start button, I e. If there's a tip bubble on screen and you try to pause to look at the menu, it goes immediately to the help entry for the tip. And you can't just B button back out of it. Say for example the tool tip is for grenades : if you press B it goes back to the special weapon submenu. B again to weapons. B again to inventory. B again to main pause menu.
All in all, it's just really poorly executed. Which is a tremendous shame because it is a giant game with tons of cool stuff inside. I don't even mind the repetativeness of the towers. The base assaults are cool and the skills are fun. The campaign is absolutely bananas and one of the coolest stories I've played in an open RPG. You think it's over and then they hit you with another five hours of gameplay. All in all, really glad I picked it up and would absolutely recommend it. However, if you tend to hyperfocus on niggles, then perhaps it might distract you.

Overall an enjoyable game with a few polarizing design choices that generate a few mixed feelings.
Vermintide's combat feels weighty and refreshing at times; a little frustrating during others. Having played only 5 levels of the game over the course of a few beta tests I can only say that what I've seen so far is pretty solid.
For it's $26 asking price it's not a bad experience at all and it's more than enough for me to overlook some of the smaller issues. The developers seem to take responsibility of their oversights and have done their best to fix what they can in a timely fashion and I respect that.
+Characters are well-voiced and charming
+Weapons feel good, unique, and well designed to fit the setting
+The design of the skaven, their behaviour, and overall aesthetic is good
+The game offers different challenges for all sorts of play
-Progression is entirely based on RNG if your rolls aren't that great then you'll be stuck on lower tier content for quite a while. 16 Hours played and my favorite characters still carry common melee weapons due to unlucky RNG. I'm on my way to unlocking a 3rd trinket slot soon without a single trinket. There's no way to work toward anything and everything is left up to what the game wants to hand to you. Trading would fix this issue, but it doesn't seem to be an option currently.
-Weapon drops themselves are somewhat scarce and makes the RNG Loot issue even more frustrating. If you spend 45 minutes on a level and choke in the last 2 minutes you get no weapon and about a tenth of the EXP you'd normally get. The game punishes failure far too harshly. Something to alleviate this would be to allow you to roll less dice for more common loot depending on how far you got and I hope the developers take this into consideration
-Some of the bugs can prematurely end a game from falling through the floor to instantly causing death. Dying to a bug in the last minutes of a match and then losing a roll for loot is more frustrating than it needs to be,
When the game works it's a fun experience with solid mechanics. The weakest part of the game is simply the loot being far too randomized and scarce. I still recommend the game if you're looking to have fun with friends in a unique and well-established setting.

Far cry has changed a lot over the years. It has gone from a linear story to a more open world setting. Far Cry 3 set the bar for what an open world game should be. Beutiful enviroments with lots of exploration and challenges. The over the top story and set pieces don't take themselves too seriously and that makes for some of the best action in a video game ever.
The game has always been at the front of graphics technology. The original Far Cry pushed the limits of what PC's could handle and 3 is no exception. The huge view distances create a vast and detailed world. Jungles are beautifly rendered and are probably the best since Crysis. Running through dense foliage was one of my most memerable experiences. Getting lost and navigating the tropical island is half the fun. There are also a lot of detail settings in the options menu. Scaling the game to match your PC's preformance is easy but does provide enough options to keep even the hardcore crowd happy. There were also some interesting options that I had never encountered before and had to learn what they did.
The story doesnt take itself seriously, which is great. If it did, it would fall completely flat. Over the top set pieces and characters allow for huge action sequences. While not overly complex, the story did provide at least some interest, enough to keep me playing. It was interesting to think about what good I was realy doing for the Island. Was there any real point to trying to liberate the island from one dictotor just to become another? The love interests of the game try to play on your emtions but in the end it comes down to your own choices. At least half of the villans in the story are interesting. Crazier villians are always more intesting. Far Cry loves to play with your perceptions and make you question weather or not you are crazy. Mind over matter is not always cut and dry. It will make you question your own sanity. Also the jungles in Far Cry are amazing.
Far Cry 3 is a great game, but stumbles in a few key areas. The endgame is shallow and doesnt provide enough to do after the story is completed. I was able to conquer the whole island and was left with nobody to shoot at since all the missions were finished. The only thing there was left to do was some hunting missions which get repetative quickly. The second half of the game lacks much of the beautiful terrain of the first. It becomes more like a desert and a dense jungle. It feels more like this section of the game was rushed.
Overall Far Cry is a great game and has set the bar high for open world games. I would strongly recommend it to any far of FPS games or who loves exploration. It has a lot going for it and has provided me with some of my most memerable moments in gaming.

Overview:  Deadlight is a side scrolling part platformer, part puzzle solver, part action game set in a zombie apocalypse.
Pros: Decent story and production quality for such a simple game.  The gameplay is fun and easy to pick up.  The scenery is vivid and colorful.  The background realistically embodies a zombie apocalypse.
Cons: Short and simple.  The game only last about 4-6 hours and doesn't provide much of a challenge.  Most players will likely breeze the game only taking a few deaths along the way.
Conclusion:  This is a simple game that only does a few things, but does them well enough.  The production quality is what sets this game above over such mini games.  If you really want to play a zombie game or just want to kill a few hours, pick this up.
Score: 7.8 / 10

Deadlight is among my top 10 favorite games. The atmosphere in this terrific game is intoxicating, voice acting is great, the scenery is gorgeous, and the story will keep you coming back time after time until you finish. There's a perfect mix of tense action, puzzle solving, and quiet down moments.
Gameplay consists of simple platforming and challenging combat. However combat is so discouraged in the game that it's almost always better to avoid the Shadows than to actually confront them, which only makes every forced encouter a hair raising experience. Unfortunately, there are some frustrating "trial and error" times where you might have to restart 5 times to get it right. This breaks the atmosphere and absorbing nature of the game, but not enough to make it an experience changer.
I cannot say enough about the art direction of this game. The background is truly the star here. To just pause for a moment and look at what's behind you is sometimes breathtaking. This is a beautiful game. The music is also fantastic, which is actually best experienced by just sitting at the main menu and listening. The cut scenes are drawn comic pages with something moving in them. This is slightly offputting as the rest of the game is so gorgeous, it would seem that the cutscenes deserved more love and attention than they received. However the great voice acting makes up for most of this.
The story follows Randal Wayne as he attempts to find and save his wife and daughter while alos taking care of other survivors he's grown close to. The story is gripping and sometimes heartbreaking, with a ending that is completely out of the blue; I never saw it coming. The game somehow manages to change your entire perspective on the main character and the game itself, all in one final extremely well put together cut scene.
So should you buy it?
The answer to this comes with a question: are you a gamer who plays for the experience or for the simple purpose of playing a game? The game is solid and fun, but I absolutely can't recommend it for the full $20 price tag, although on a sale of around $10-$5 i'd suggest buying it and playing with some friends.
The first issue is just in terms of content. There are only about 3 or 4 maps for the standard 'objective-based' gamemode, and 4 maps for the classic Zombie Panic mode. Dispite what the store page will tell you, there is absolutely no variation in these maps besides the occasional changed door. The maps always follow the same objectives and go the same ways by the end. You just might have to go to Hallway A instead of Hallway B to press a button.
The second  and as far as i'm concerned the worst issue is how objectives are communicated with the player in the actual objective co-op modes that are meant to be the game's main draw. You're given instructions using a smartphone your character is always carrying, which is a neat effect sure, but brings the issue of your only clues usually being a quick 10-word message saying the next objective in really vague terms. The maps are huge and easy to get lost in and the paths you're meant to follow can be really hard to spot and the game doesn't help you in any way.
You'll get a message saying 'Okay, we need to go to the hardware store!' Well♥♥♥♥♥♥ where the ♥♥♥♥ is that? Sure, there's the occasional maps scattered around the level, but they don't help because they don't mark the fences and random barracades blocking the streets, so instead you just have to look down every single alleyway until you finally find the tiny hole in the wall hidden in a back corner that lets you advance.
In particular, I had a game where we had successfully communicated with the military and gotten help sent in. The game was over and all we had to do was escape to a truck that our phone said was here to pick us up. We never found the truck. We looked everywhere and sure, there were military trucks, but we couldn't tell which one was apparently our salvation and which one was just a prop on the map. We tried pressing use against every truck or vehicle with no luck. Was the game bugged? Did we win? Was there even a way to win? We didn't know! The game wouldn't TELL US.
I can't recommend this. The classic ZP mode is fun, but there's just not enough maps, and the objective mode is more frustrating to play than it is fun. I didn't even get into how broken the infection mechanic is either.
If it's on sale, go fo it. If not, do not buy.

What is there to say about Hotline Miami 2? Well, first and foremost, it is a direct follow up story-wise to Hotline Miami 1. As a big fan of the first game, I simply love that idea. If you've played HM1, you are probably familiar with how the story for about two thirds of the game is a bit garbled, with small newspaper clippings or a clickable object here or there to fill in a little bit more, but past that, it's pretty much up to the player's interpretation of the events that unfold. Now, for those that haven't played the first one, I won't spoil anything, but I will disclose that the endings, and there are multiple, EVEN THEN don't 100% explain to players what the heck is going on. This, until HM2 (and the filling in of info with the awesome free digital comic), left folks wondering what all happened, and most importantly, why? Well, ladies and gents, the continuation, at least in terms of story, is fantastic. The continuing plot, which is played out over multiple chapters through the perspectives of different groups of psycho killers slowly begins to piece together a muuuuch larger picture, and this I simply adore. That, along with the booming  90's synth and vomit-inducing color scheme that has carried over well and true from the first game pretty much seal the deal for me....
Hm...I feel like something is missing...
Oh yeah! The gameplay!
Well, to first timers to the Hotline Miami series, this game will most likely come off as having a pretty steep, and I mean STEEP learning and difficulty curve. Alas, this is most likely an intentional part of the game put in by the developers to feel more comfortable and less patronizing to returning Miami fans. But, if you manage to hone your murdering skills, you can get the jist of the game in a relatively brief time. After having played the first Hotline Miami, however, I can say as a returning player that the feel of this game seems almost completely different from the first one. Now, that may have sounded like it had a negative connotation added to it, but I tend to like change. The layout of the levels are a wee bit tighter, the action is certainly faster, and I notice myself getting frustrated on a couple of occasions, but what does that amount to play-wise? Well, suffice to say, I really REALLY like how the game feels and plays. Again, I site the possible thoughts the developers had when making this game for returning Miami players. With each new group of characters you play, they add on a bit of extra challenge, as instead of having access to a veritable "arsenal" of rejected Halloween masks to choose from in the first game, now you must grapple with the unique dispositions of each of the multiple characters and their limitations. For example, and a fair warning for minor spoilers here, one of the primary groups you play as are a couple of vigilantes who are "fans" of the original mask wearin' murder maestro. Now, instead of playing as the leader of the group, or something like that, players have access to each character as their own individual mask. The "Tony's Revenge" mask limits players to the fists only, but those fists act like explosive punchers, insta-killing anything rather than simply knocking an enemy out like with other characters, while the "Mark" mask lets you play with a starter weapon of DUAL SMGS! Excuse me, but that's frickin' sweet. So, getting back on track, these characters limit the player with specific play styles depending on the character, and yet, it doesn't FEEL limiting. Now, i'm not gonna' nitpick this game, but I love this limitation...as stupid as that sounds. I like the challenge of having to play certain levels differently depending on the different limitations the masks give me, despite still being able to choose the mask at the beginning of most of the levels you play with this merry band of murdalizers. I just feel like i'm actually living these characters and their masks rather than simply putting on a mask, even though that was pretty awesome in the first game as well.  So, in short, with HM2, think "limiting, but refreshing".
SO! As a recap to folks interested in or planning to buy this game, know this:
-The game will challenge you if you are new, so take your time, get hyped up over the twitchy gameplay, and lose yourself in the psychedelic synth, and you'll get the hang of it in no time.
-Remember that you are playing the masks and the characters, not just the characters. The limitations on the levels are meant to embody the individuals you are playing. Whether you play as a Russian mobster who starts with a silenced pistol, or a crazy agile girl with a zebra mask that can roll-dodge, play the way you want to challenge yourself, and try to strategize your play style around the way the character acts and feels to you.
-Really get immersed in the crazy story! Since this IS truly a story continuation that has a lot more narrative than the first game, I would highly suggest playing the first one before running through this, but if you are simply looking for an awesome plot and a bunch of characters with complex and interesting backgrounds, this game will certainly fulfill that need as well.
Well, looks like my time is up...so, I hope I at least got you interested in the Hotline Miami series and story, 'cause lemme' tell ya', it's certainly a good series to get into! Try the first game out if you want the complete feel and plot of the game, but even if you are just looking for a solid arcade twitch top-down 90's-themed over-the-top murder simulator with a kickin' soundtrack, this game is certainly for you!

To start off, this is a decent game. I even enjoyed the first half of this game. Once you hit act 4 (there are 6) however things go south. Lets start with the good.
Pros:
-Amazing soundtrack. Even better then the first game
-The Fans' levels are extremely enjoyable
-Added executions for guns
Honestly I really wanted to like this game but once you hit the level "Stronghold" in act 4 you realize that they stopped caring about this game. Now for the bad.
Cons:
-General pacing of the game is MUCH slower. It is near impossible to rush many of the levels.
-Terrible level design, many later level become window shooting and baiting games. The game is unplayable using melee for the most part.
-AI gets stuck, doors are buggy, and camera is terrible. That being said these are all techincal bugs and can be fixed.
-Level are much more static. There are no random weapon spawns anymore in levels.
-Fewer melee weapons and more guns. Yes they actually added new guns and took away melee weapons. The only new melee weapons that I noticed are the chain, chainsaw and the skateboard.
Overall the game just isn't fun. It is a mixture of endless tedium and waiting. The flow and variety are gone. This game is basically a top down shooter. That being said the level editor may be enough to redeem this game although we won't know until they release it. At this point I would have to give this game a thumbs down. It's a major letdown with a strong start and a steep slide into mediocrity.
