2012 was a good year for gaming in my eyes. Games like Telltale's The Walking Dead, Max Payne 3, and Mass Effect 3 were released, all of them are, in my humble opinion, some of the best games ever made. Sure there were some flops in there, *cough* Steel Batallion *cough**cough*, but for the most part the year was great. There is one game, however, that stands out from the rest in my eyes. That game is Far Cry 3, developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft, this game was the first I playyed out of the whole lot and was the first game that I actually like that I had on my 360. After three years since my last play of the game, I remembered that I had this game on my Steam list and decided to try it again and see if it held up. So did it? Let's take a look.
STORY: You're Jason Brody, a California rich boy who goes on an Asian tour with his brothers, his girlfriend, and his friends, culminating to a skydiving trip to the Rook Islands. Unfortunately, the Rook Islands is the base of a slavery ring, and you and your friends are kidnapped by pirates. You and your brother Grant escape where you're held, however he is killed by the leader, Vaas, and you barely escape, waking up to see one of the residents of the island giving you a tatau, a tribal tatoo that signals a great warrior, and they tell you that since you managed to escape, this signals the beginning of a change of the war. You have never killed a single person in your life, but you are the only person who is able to save your friends, so you have to go out and save them. The story is pretty good, it sounds like a silly action movie plot, but it goes a lot deeper than at times than some people might realize, as you see Jason turn from a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frat boy to a depraved warrior who might not be killing just to save his friends anymore. The story kind of loses steam in the second half when you run into a new villain, but for the most part its momentum keeps up. It has one of the best FPS stories out there.
GAMEPLAY: First person shooter. You got a variety of weapons to go with and, as a result, a lot of ways to go at the game. Shotguns, LMG's, sniper rifles, if you want to go loud and proud or quiet or some mix of the way, you can do that, and with upgrades, you can carry up to four guns. There are two ways to upgrade yourself, one way is crafting, where you kill varying animals around the island to craft their skins into upgrades like weapons holsters and ammo pouches. This is fine, it's a bit annoying that you can't use any animal skins for them, but from a mechanical standpoint I do understand why they did that. The second way to upgrade yourself is a skill path that you get points for when you level up. You have three paths you can gain skills in, and you can go down any of these paths and get the bonuses in anyway you want, with a few restrictions so you don't get OP skills too early on in the game. This is also fine enough, there are some useless abilities in there, but that will always be the case with stuff like this. Overall, the gameplay is great. The gunplay is good and movement works fine.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: Ran at mostly Ultra settings, 1440p, above 60FPS constantly. Get a more recent graphics card like a GTX 900 or 1000 series and you'll be good pretty much. The game looks pretty good, and while it does show its age a bit in some regards, it looks really good overall.
CHARACTERS, VOICE ACTING, AND DESIGN: Jason is not your usual silent protagonist, he actually speaks a bit, which is nice. His friends are finely voice acted and look unique enough. The villain for the first half of the game, Vaas, is honest to got one of the best video game characters ever. Later on the island you run into more colorful figures, from a CIA agent to a German privateer, you'll run into at least one character you like.
SIDE ACTIVITIES: Outside of the story mission, there is a decent variety of things to do. The aformentioned hunting is fun, there's a lot of different animals to look for, from sharks to goats to bears. Across the island there are radio towers, which are platforming puzzles that, once you reach the top, you get a piece of the map revealed as well as some free weapons, which are nice to do. There are outposts across the islands on the island run by the pirates that, once you take over them, removes nearby pirates from the area and also gives you hunting missions and killing missions, all of which are fine. There are also little collectibles across the map; ancient relics, drug cards, and World War 2 soldier letters, which honestly feel kind of grindy to go after and collect. For the most part, though, the side activities are decent and don't get in the way of things.
MULTIPLAYER: Oh yeah, multiplayer... didn't really play it, even on Xbox. I did play a bit of the co-op mode, which was alright I guess, but not really something to write home about. Ah well, though.
FINAL THOUGHTS: One of my favorite games of all time, really. 10/10, there are some problems surely, but every game has them, and the game completely shadows them.. If the game interests you, pick it up when it goes on sale for sure.

This is more of a Strategy Game than an RPG. Everyone your character interacts with is generic and most battles will be decided on the number of generic people you've recruited from generic towns and kingdoms, rather than your skill. In strategy games, this is not a problem, nobody cares about the motives of a pawn, only their utility matters. However, RPGs rely mostly on gameplay and immersive lore, of which Mount and Blade, has none.
As far as the gameplay goes, many people enjoy this game's Horse Combat, and I understand that it's a unique mechanic that forces players to use new styles than they might have used in other games.

I haven't played this game as much as some, but I feel it is important to add to the people saying this game is amazing! If the main game wasn't enough then the mods available (e.g the GoT mod) will extend the time you can play M&B to the hundreds of hours.
The combat is weighty; using the mouse to direct exactly how your spear will thrust or how your sword will swing is great fun, and manages to be fairly intuitive - as is the blocking mechanism when using a shield. The number of troops on a battlefield is part of what makes the game feel so great: it feels awesome riding with your cavalry into a mass of enemy infantry; playing sniper with a bow and arrow during a siege and having a hundred enemies to pick from; or just joining a battle on foot against a bunch of low tier units and smashing some faces together.
It must be said that the 'main' game world map is nowhere near as good as the combat, although it is engaging enough, with plenty to do at each different stage of the game: from doing random quests for lords; joining a kings army; wooing a lady to marriage; boosting your prestige throughout the kingdom; hosting feasts or even starting your own kingdom and conquering the world!
Complaints about the game would be that the sieges are really stupid at times, with only 1 (max 2?) ladder(s) meaning that your 100 guys are only able to fight the enemy 2 at a time, and the crushing feeling when you reach the top only to be pushed down by the AI. The main other issue I have with the game is the timescale village/town improving has, when you have only a couple of villages near the start and you have to constantly babysit them while their messenger post builds it is really infuriating.
After this short insight into why I love the game I would say that you should absolutely buy this game, it is the most fun I have had in a very long time! 9/10!

Even though the game is still in beta, I have to say that I am genuinely impressed with the quality of the game, also I particularly like the fact that you can pick what branch of the armed forces you want your German or American soldier to join after they attain a high enough rank (rank 3 being the lowest rank where you can switch branch), personally I chose the Panzer korps for my German soldier and I have to say the Tanks are certainly fun to play even when compared to the likes of Warthunder and World of Tanks, of which I have played both. The other branches I have not yet played with the exception of Infantry since that is the starting army branch, are the air forces, paratroopers, recon corps (snipers basically) and the very last branch which is General which allows you to take control of the war in Europe in a sort of RTS style gameplay from what I've heard against opposing generals as you try to capture 12 critical cities around Europe and achieve victory for your faction. The infantry play is pretty solid and is realistic to a degree especially when it comes to taking damage since you can only take 1-3 shots before death from most weapons whilst headshots are one-shot kills regardless of the weapon used. The game is of course not without its fair share of flaws/bugs as with any game but to be honest the only real Issue I have with the game thus far is that "deployment queue" which is basically when you have to wait for a couple of "teammates to fall" before you can spawn back into the game which does add some frustration to the game for me personally especially when you are trying to help your team capture/defend one of the control points on the sometimes very large maps since by the time you get back to that location it can be too late to help any further. That being said I believe that this game has great potential and since its Free to play at the moment why not give it a go? Especially if you are interested in combined arms assaults or WW2 in general such as myself, then I highly recommend this game to you. I rate this game thus far a 8 out of 10 and since this review is before the introduction of the Soviets that may very well rise depending on how they are implemented into the game, still though I eagerly look forward to working my way towards the T-34's and IS's in the Soviet tank line when they do come into the game. Review done on the 03/02/15.

Far Cry 3 is an open world first person shooter developed and published by Ubisoft and runs on a heavily modified fork of CryEngine1 called Dunia. It requires Uplay, and a fix to run, and for me wouldn't start through Steam at all, which is why I only have 19 hours on display.
At the start of the game you, Jason Brody, and your friends are taken by pirates with the intention of selling you into slavery before making you make your escape into the jungle where you meet the Rakyat. The Rakyat are a tribe of warriors and natives that have lived on Rook island for generations before outsiders conquered it up. They offer to train you to kill the pirates that kidnapped you and their notorious leader Vaas, starting a long journey of violence.
Far Cry 3's gameplay is as repetitive as it is boring, with very few exceptions to this rule. You'll by and large find yourself doing the same things you'd do in any other Ubisoft open world game a-la Assassins Creed. You climb towers to reveal areas & access free weaponry, take outposts, do their one or two missions which boils down to knife a commander or kill animals with a specific type of weapon. There's really just no variety to this game whatsoever. Even the crafting and hunting mechanics are cheaply done. Before you even reach the 2nd island you'll have collected all the animal materials needed to craft everything you need, and crafting anything but Hunter's Instinct and Health is worthless since you can just hold a button to heal yourself instantly and will never use anything else that you can craft. Money is also worthless, you'll hardly do anything with it besides buy more ammo and armor and maybe the signature weapons. This is largely due to the fact that climbing towers will reward you with weapons for free, bipassing the process of buying them altogether.
Gunplay is shallow and uninteresting, you have a collection of different hitscan weapon sets that are very generic and a small collection of skins for them. One of the most interesting weapons, the bow, is hurt by the fact that a lot of games coming out at the time also used it and I was already burned out on it before hand.
Certain weapons are useless altogether like the majority of the early game weapons and the repair tool. Just equip the signature weapons as you recieve them as they are vastly superior to everything else in the game, especially the Vector and AMR (two shot chopper kills.)
By far my biggest complaint with this whole game is the wholly braindead AI that they throw at you. What a pathetic bunch of idiots these are. It's so easy to clear outposts with stealth that it's better just skipping the process altogether and running in to clear them loud, which brings more reinforcements to the situation. If you're not absolutely terrible at FPS games you can easily clear outposts loud or not without alerting the alarms and gaining the maximum XP for it. Go ahead try, it's a hitscan game with hardly any control over recoil needed to play, just point and click on their heads all day long.
The story, while I appreciate some of the things they tried to do like Jason's decent into madness, Vaas' backstory (really the best character and story in the game really), and the Rakyat traditions. It still came off as very boring, as these sections were by and large unskippable and took you out of the game into simple delusional linear segments. The worst of which being the QTE "boss fights" against Hoyt and Vaas, pathetic.
This game is only really worth purchasing cheap, if at all, for it's eye candy visuals (which are still incredibly cheap, you have scope glint from the sun behind you but no shadow for your playermodel) and screwing with the outposts for a little while. I whole-heartedly do not recommend this game, nor do I recommend any like it.
Despite it has that uplay crap, it's still worth buying, it's extremely fun. I highly recommend this game.

I haven't played this game as much as some, but I feel it is important to add to the people saying this game is amazing! If the main game wasn't enough then the mods available (e.g the GoT mod) will extend the time you can play M&B to the hundreds of hours.
The combat is weighty; using the mouse to direct exactly how your spear will thrust or how your sword will swing is great fun, and manages to be fairly intuitive - as is the blocking mechanism when using a shield. The number of troops on a battlefield is part of what makes the game feel so great: it feels awesome riding with your cavalry into a mass of enemy infantry; playing sniper with a bow and arrow during a siege and having a hundred enemies to pick from; or just joining a battle on foot against a bunch of low tier units and smashing some faces together.
It must be said that the 'main' game world map is nowhere near as good as the combat, although it is engaging enough, with plenty to do at each different stage of the game: from doing random quests for lords; joining a kings army; wooing a lady to marriage; boosting your prestige throughout the kingdom; hosting feasts or even starting your own kingdom and conquering the world!
Complaints about the game would be that the sieges are really stupid at times, with only 1 (max 2?) ladder(s) meaning that your 100 guys are only able to fight the enemy 2 at a time, and the crushing feeling when you reach the top only to be pushed down by the AI. The main other issue I have with the game is the timescale village/town improving has, when you have only a couple of villages near the start and you have to constantly babysit them while their messenger post builds it is really infuriating.
After this short insight into why I love the game I would say that you should absolutely buy this game, it is the most fun I have had in a very long time! 9/10!

Well, pretty much the game is another FPS with zombies. This one is diferent, however, as it does not focuses on the singleplayer perspective nor totally in buckets of blood and truckloads of gore or mutated zombies to get a shot at the "Best zombie game ever" title. The zombies arent fast (other than sprinting player zombies), and they are not very smart (they're slow and stupid, but if they spot you, they'll chase you for quite a bit).
The weapon selection as of this review is somewhat limited, with melee weapons being hard to come by on the game, unless you're playing the PVP mode (Hunted), where you will spawn with one. The maps are huge, and there are some very subtle changes each time you play, almost unnoticeable from one playthrough to another, but they keep the game rather "fresh".
The multiplayer modes consist of the panic mode (just like Zombie Panic Source, albeit with some changes), a PVP mode called "hunted" (Survivors vs. Zombies) where your cellphone helps you track both player zombies and survivors, helping you either finish them off or avoid them. And two co-op modes, "Escape" where you team must complete a series of randomly generated objectives to escape, and "Extraction" where your team must rescue trapped survivors.
Depending on which mode you're playing, the cellphone has different uses. On escape it'll tell you what objective you need to accomplish, on "hunted", it'll help you locate your prey. On extraction, it'll act as a GPS, helping you navigate to trapped survivors.
Ammo does not grow on trees, nor do weapons, so you'll have to scavenge, and that's dangerous when you consider the fact that a single zombie attack and, if you're unlucky, you'll be infected. However, hiding isnt very... useful on the PVP mode since people can just ping you phone to find out where you are.
All in all, the game is worth the money spent on it, performance wise, it'll run nicely on even machines with 4GB RAM and everything else above the minimal specs. You'll also of course have a good time with the people you play (Not many people play this, by the way). Just remember one thing, can you REALLY trust them?

As much as I'd like to like this game (and I do), I can't support it due to several glaring problems.
The first is how expensive everything is.  It certainly strikes me as pay to win, it takes hours grinding up even individual mods, and to top it off, they depreceate and must be repaired, or special ammo types must be replenished.  It's a game that has too many rewards for paid players, and as someone who really has no problem spending money on games, the fact that it was trying to force me to do it so much turned me off pretty quickly.
There also seems to be a lack of guns, and moreso because beyond 2 guns you can get initially (the semi-automatic rifle or the smg) the rest are trapped behind paywalls or level-ups that will take days if not weeks to obtain.  Not enough choice beyond having a hamburger or a cheeseburger.
Finally, the matchmaking is very poor, and that's why I can't recommend the game.  Several times tonight I was put on teams with people rank 1-3 against people ranked 7+.  They clearly outgunned the teams, had access to things like tanks (when no one on my team even had access to anti-tank weapons), and could just camp objectives with tanks and we ended up losing very quickly.  When I first came to the game, the Nazi's lost 9 games in a row, even when I played as Nazi's and had k/d ratios of 5:1 (and pushing objectives).  The game isn't well balanced.
As far as positives, the combat itself is great.  A minimal HUD lends well to the long distance combat.  Shooting is difficult and takes patience, skill, and a steady hand.  The maps are well done and many times I had a great time fighting big battles over objectives, with a constant back and forth attack/defend going on in the domination style skirmish mode.  Even though you only get two weapons by default, both of them perform really well at their role, and seem well balanced.
All in all, this looked like such a great addition to the WW2 FPS style genre, but it really falls flat with balancing issues in matchmaker and pay to win access to skills and weapons.  As much as I want to love it, it still needs work.

Cons:

Deadlight is the single most terrifying, yet equally thrilling platformer I have ever played. The developers crafted a story behind Randall Wayne that seems to illuminate him as nothing more than an ordinary man. As you play through the game, the player must find ever inventive ways of survivng and problem solving. The game also provides several collectibles, achievements, and unlockables. The difficulty of the game resides in the fact that it is not a normal dukes of hazard, guns-blazing, huge-explosions type of game. One must understand the importance of cleverity, stealth and invention. The artwork of the game is absolutely phenomenal and I am intriged by the art director. The voice acting is brilliant and shows the personality of the characters in a way that is both dark and realistic. The game functions as though it's a play waiting to unfold. The only part of the game that I am rather upset over is the implementation of a "Nightmare Mode" as they called it. This mode gives no reason to complete it other then the alternate ending which one can easily view via youtube, and the achievement through steam.
Bottom Line: I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys well built puzzle solvers and platformers. Although the Nightmare Mode is fairly useless, most people decide to leave it by the wayside. 85/100

Deadlight started out strong in the first couple of levels, impressing me with the whole style and concept.  The story even got a little interesting (reminding me of Max Payne in a small way, with his inner monologue narration and trippy dreams and nightmares), and I expected it to unfold brilliantly as I went along.
However, the game just failed to be enjoyable for me.  I hated that the game made it nearly impossible to react fast enough in a situation as it happened.  Instead, I was pretty much forced to die every ten steps, then act in anticipation of what I now knew what was coming in order to get past it.  And repeat and repeat and repeat... every... step... of the way.  The end result was that all the dying and repeating (and dying and repeating) broke my immersion in the game, and I completely stopped caring about the story, and just wanted the damn thing to end so I could stop playing it.
If you can get your hands on this game for free, or for only a couple bucks, then I say give it a go.  Otherwise, Deadlight is just not worth the money or time, in my opinion.

C: > Program Files 86 > Steam > Steamapps > Common > Far Cry 3 > bin

Far Cry 3 is an addictive game. I cannot remember last time I have been so hooked on a game, since The Witcher, Red Faction Guerilla & Fallout 3.
The reason why Far Cry suceedes is in the excellent gun play. It has responsive and satisfying gameplay. Since it an open world game you will find yourself doing other objectives as well. The game rewards you for killing looting to upgrade your weapons and stats. There is a lot of loot and sidequest if you like that sort of stuff. It is definitely built around a "completionist"
The story wasn not as deep as I imagined, the talented actor who plays Vaas was one the sickest characters in the game. There's no point of spoiling the game. It is a good story, but it felt a bit flat at the end. The bosses, first of all, sucks ar-se. Pretty much all quick-time-events expect for one, which is not really hard to beat anyway. I completed pretty much all the outpost and radio towers first before I actually continued the missions. They were fun, but a bit too easy in my opinion. The checkpoints are too close to each other, which is great for some people but a burden for us, who likes a challenge.
Speaking of a challenge. The radio towers jumping puzzles was very frustrating, since the jumping controls are very inconsistent. There are also a lot of bugs in the game. I restarted some missions a couple of times, because I completed the mission in a different way. You should not be punished for doing that in a freeroam game like Far Cry.
The game has beautiful graphics even today standards and finally a game, which nails the customization right. The only problem I really had was the motion blur, which you cannot turn off. The graphics reminded my of
with its beautiful landscape and sunny beaches.
The music composed by Brian Tylor does an amazing job to set the mood the of the game. There's two genres of soundtrack in the game. One of them is the traditionel film music and second one is electronic music. It mixes well together and describes the situations you encounter in the game perfectly.
Overall an amazing game I can recommend to everyone who loves to explore. Definitely one of my favorite open-world games ever.

Far Cry 3 is an addictive game. I cannot remember last time I have been so hooked on a game, since The Witcher, Red Faction Guerilla & Fallout 3.
The reason why Far Cry suceedes is in the excellent gun play. It has responsive and satisfying gameplay. Since it an open world game you will find yourself doing other objectives as well. The game rewards you for killing looting to upgrade your weapons and stats. There is a lot of loot and sidequest if you like that sort of stuff. It is definitely built around a "completionist"
The story wasn not as deep as I imagined, the talented actor who plays Vaas was one the sickest characters in the game. There's no point of spoiling the game. It is a good story, but it felt a bit flat at the end. The bosses, first of all, sucks ar-se. Pretty much all quick-time-events expect for one, which is not really hard to beat anyway. I completed pretty much all the outpost and radio towers first before I actually continued the missions. They were fun, but a bit too easy in my opinion. The checkpoints are too close to each other, which is great for some people but a burden for us, who likes a challenge.
Speaking of a challenge. The radio towers jumping puzzles was very frustrating, since the jumping controls are very inconsistent. There are also a lot of bugs in the game. I restarted some missions a couple of times, because I completed the mission in a different way. You should not be punished for doing that in a freeroam game like Far Cry.
The game has beautiful graphics even today standards and finally a game, which nails the customization right. The only problem I really had was the motion blur, which you cannot turn off. The graphics reminded my of
with its beautiful landscape and sunny beaches.
The music composed by Brian Tylor does an amazing job to set the mood the of the game. There's two genres of soundtrack in the game. One of them is the traditionel film music and second one is electronic music. It mixes well together and describes the situations you encounter in the game perfectly.
Overall an amazing game I can recommend to everyone who loves to explore. Definitely one of my favorite open-world games ever.

Contagion isn't just another 3D First Person Shooter. This particular game is more of a "What If..." type game where you are put in a "Zombie Infestation" situation and you have to figure out what you would do under (such-in-such) circumstances. Each game only gives you limited items to start with and you have to look for other weapons and accessories as you progress into the game.
The game itself offers single as well as multiplayer modes. Most of the multiplayer is about helping each other out, but if you are more of a "Naw, you're on your own", that's fine to. The game also offers many kinds of ways you can deal with the zombies as well as create strategies for yourself on how you can get by with only a monkey-wrech and a cell phone to start with.
If you ever wanted to see what it's like to be in a "Zombie Infestation" world, this game offers that situation to you. Not a whole lot of areas to play with, but the areas themelves offer different ways on how you can handle the situation given to you. I will say that everytime I play, it's not easy avoiding the zombies at first while trying to find cool weapons, but once you do manage to find say a shotgun, and enough ammo, you're pretty much set for a while.
One thing you will have to get used to is that there is no crosshair or targetting dot, you have to "guess" whether or not you are aiming perfectly. To me, that's ideal since even in real life, even if you get a gun, you don't automatically get a crosshair.
Overall a good game that makes you think as well as teaches you how to survive a zombie infested world.
(STRATEGY ALERT) Like they say in the movies, aim for the head, once shot to the head and that's it. Shots to the chest or limbs only slow it down as well as make it angry.

Beats the *ISH* outta the L4D series. Much less "arcade"y, yet not too much realism where it takes the fun out of it. You've got coop objective-based maps which are fun (only thing is they can be a bit confusing at first if you're new as far as what exactly you have to do, this game will not hold your hand through everything and give you hundreds of annoying popups and markers). Then you have a pvp + pve mode where you face against zombies in the environment as well as other players. You are not a human pincussion in this game like in others, one or two well placed shots WILL kill you. Death is permanant for the round in both modes, though you do spawn as a zombie that can blend in and behave just like all the others which is pretty fun stalking other players in the shadows and taking out that damned camper that just killed you! Unlike most mainstream zombie games, headshots are almost required to take down a zombie (but for the most part take them out in one hit)
Graphics in this game for a Source engine game are pretty damn good! The team seems to have spent a lot of work with the basic mechanics/feel of the game where you can barely tell that it's Source. Weapon moves slightly with mouse movement (like in BF3/4 and Arma series), there are no crosshairs, you have iron sights. When you look down you see feet, no floating in the air over nothing like a lot of games like to do. Heads and limbs blow off of zombies where you shoot them, dynamic lighting/shadows, etc etc.
I'm really surprised this game isn't more popular. The developers of this game are the same team that brought us Zombie Panic Source mod, so they're not a big dev company backed by big publishers (or even valve). Even though the game is released, the team is still working on bringing out more maps and content, and even a reworking of the current character models. Every friday they host a livestream on twitch where they talk to the community and answer questions which is pretty damn cool. You can tell they are an old school dev studio like Unknown Worlds and valve was back in the half-life 1 days where 99% of new content and features come out in free updates, so what you see here is not all you're going to get!

I would definately recommend this game to any fans of WWII shooters or f2p shooters in general.
The graphics, when set to low, are pretty substandard, but when if you set the quality to high and turn on all the options it look pretty good. The vehicle models in particlar are very well done. The graphics are certainly not on par with a AAA title, and even some other f2p shooters surpass them by leaps and bound, but they are perfectly servicable for their purpose.
The game is divided into two sections, the action gameplay and the generals gameplay, the first revolving around FPS combat including land and air combat, and the latter revolving around tactical deployment of different types of combat teams around a map of Europe that constantly changes based on player decision.
The Generals gameplay is more of an RTS than anything else, and the decisions of the generals effect the outcome of the war more than anything else. The side with generals who have a better grasp on general military doctrines and troop deployment mechanics, as well as higher level assault teams, will almost invariably win. After each war (played until one side captures 12 our of 15 capitols or 30 days, whichever comes first), players are allowed to swtich sides. This, however, unfortunately means that if you just lost a war, prepare to lose another as all your good generals have swtiched to the winning side for the next war. It usually takes a little while for this to balance itself out. That having been said, as of right now, I've seen no benefit or penalty for winning or losing the war other than the experience you gained by fighting in it, so your ego may be the only thing that gets just by this system.
The Action gameplay is very well done, with the shooting controls in particular being very tight. The movement of your character seems a little clunky at first, but makes a lot of sense once a little bit of time is put into it. The ability to switch between characters on death is a must based on changing battle conditions, but feels like a clunkier mechanic than simply allowing the character the change loadouts on the fly. It also means that you'll have a lot of characters to fill different roles (tanker, pilot, infantry, recon, etc). Each of these characters levels independantly, so gaining medals (and the perks that come with them) can be a slow process if you've spread out your characters too much. The tank gameplay is entertaining, though one definatly needs to be cognizent of one's weakness to AT teams and aircraft. The aircraft gameplay is pretty solid as well, but a bad pilot can eat up a lot of your resources pretty quickly.
Which brings us to some of the problems the game has. First and foremost, the paywall. As a f2p game, Heroes & Generals is designed to get you to spend money on the game. Now, they do a pretty good job of not throwing obnoxious mechanics like limited-duration weapons and other common f2p practices at you, but the problem still exists. Since each character is leveled independantly, you need to buy equipment for each character and resupply their vehicles, granades, rockets, etc, which can be done with premium currency or in game cash. Unfortunately, in game cash is very slow to come, and more often then not when you unlock a new weapon or vehicle you won'y have anywhere near enough currency to buy it. Resupplying can also be very expensive. I found that with as little as 2 active characters the upkeep of those characters can be enough to cause you to break even on currency, which prevents you from either progressing those characters further or playing new ones without purchasing premium currency.
The secong major problem the game has is that it makes it cumbersome to play with your friends if your friends have different combat interests than you. For instance, if you want to be a tank driver and your friend wants to play a recon, to only times you can play together is if some general happens to have deployed an armored assualt force with a recon assault force to the same zone. You cannot form a platoon together unless you are using the same class, although the game does have a brillant mechanic that allows you to join the game that a friend is in without too much hubub, although the game will still limt the classes available to play in that game based on what the generals have deployed, so you may end up sitting in a queue screen telling you that there are no available assauly units for you to join for the duration of the battle.
The third problem I have is that some of the physics are laughable. Jeeps will flip over at the slightest provication, and will often spin out of control for no visible reason. Vehicles can't climb over minor obsacles, and get stuck on some of the dumbest things. Which still does not prevent the combined arms approach to tank gameplay from being very solid and more engrossing than other tank-on-tank based f2p games. The flight controls seem pretty good, though don't expect flight simulator levels of accuracy in the flight model.
All of that having been said, what you have here is a game that is a lot of fun, mixed with sheer rage if your generals are deploying forces ineffectively or rashly, with a couple of very definate rough edges. However, none of these rough edges are game breaking, aside from moments of frustration. I'd give the game a 7.5/10, which is pretty impressive considering the game is still in beta, but your opinion may vary considerably depending on your view of WWII era military hardware. All in all, the play experience is more fun than most of the other f2p shooters out there, and it is definately worth the play.
If nothing else, you can easily play for a few days without ever running into the paywall, so it can be a good indicator of what you will think of the game as a whole.

Things feel more methodical this time around. While the first Hotline Miami was undeniably abstract, HM2 feels a little more grounded in its various characters and story threads.

I'm not a fan of the design choices in the sequel so far.
First, having to scope around for enemies this time around because the levels are larger and enemies can see you way off screen really ruins the flow and speed I liked about the original. The idea of a larger level sounds nice, but pausing to scope around ruins the intensity for me. It's like if in Sonic the Hedgehog you just had to look up and down all the time instead of running at a quick pace.
Also, the addition of different characters for what I guess story purposes and their little "quirks" come at no warning.  This again, ruins the flow of the game.  You're at a good pace through the level only to suddenly find out when your character executes a mafia member by beating their head in...again..and again..and again, until you click RMB to move.  Which you don't assume is the case, as before characters beat the enemies head once or twice and got off automatically.  Thus, you get killed by a gunman because you didn't know he wouldn't hop off automatically.
Also, the story segments in between levels are interesting...But I'd much prefer them to just be a cutscene, rather than hobbling along trying to find the random exit or object I need to grab just to get to the next level.  A minor thing, but something I feel ruins the fast paceness of the game.  I had this complaint about the original.
The difficulty levels through the game jump a lot too.  One level might be super easy then the next much harder, only for the next one to be easy.  I assume this was for story reasons.
Lastly, the AI seems to get confused alot during play.  Multiple times I've seen enemies get stuck on a door and spin around in circles like a maniac.  Also, the AI loves to get stuck on corners, mostly doors though.  The AI also doesn't seem to "click" when it hears gunshots.  Several times I was like "He should have heard that".
It's not "awful" by any means.  I just enjoyed how the original paced itself compared to this one. When I get into a good groove in a game I don't like it broken and Hotline Miami 2 has a little too many design changes that does that for me.  I feel like some of the changes were made for "story" reasons..even though the story is so obscure half the time, and not for good game design reasons.
The OST is decent though.

New gameplay mechanics are great, new chalenges are superb, story is drugs induced nightmare (as it should be), no more random AI enemies (until chapter 11 that is), graphics and style are nice and atmospheric. Animations... mmm... thouse juicy animations.
Music... music IS huge part of series and it is mediocre in HM2 at best. Really dissapointing. No more adrenaline inducing carefully selected music tracks for me. Only some generic electronic dubstep-ish somethings..
Therefore - 8\10.

you need to get lvl 3 with starting rifle..meaning you need to kill around 30-50ish people while using it-rough guess.
this unlocks the unscoped bolt action rifle(which costs 36k silver-a TON of in game cash when you are lvl 3). then you need to get lvl 11 with bolt action rifle to unlock the scoped version...this is like 1000 kills...I'm not kidding.if you get lucky average 5-10 a game....yes I see the "madskillz" with 20+ kills...good for you!

But hey, I do anyway, because this game (or rather, this port) is very clumsy. The physics is buggy, the response time is delayed, and the axe is apparently made of rubber.
Most actions will result in your death, which would be completely justified had it been due to the challenging nature of the game, but instead most of it will be the result of faulty game mechanisms and strange quirks of the level layout. These errors can be ignored (albeit with some difficulty) during the initial playthrough, as the checkpoints are frequent and forgiving, but once the postgame "Nightmare Mode" is introduced, this becomes a whole different story. When there are only 3 checkpoints in the entire playthrough of the game, frustrating doesn't even begin to describe the task of completing this mode (That alternate hat Randall wears was pretty neato though).
As a port of the original XBOX game, this game also suffers from strange mapping of the controls. Well, maybe it's part of the challenge to press Shift and Ctrl while moving. It just feels like the controls were mapped by someone not accustomed to keyboard and mouse.
The art style was slick, the sidescrolling gameplay was a great idea, and the entire concept was generally pretty awesome. What this game suffers from are ridiculous response times and funky physics in a port that wasn't really thought out properly.

It's another zombie survival game this time done in a side-scrolling platform style. It does this very well. Not survival horror but more action adventure with a gloomy feel to it.
The graphics are really great. It really seems like it's not a side-scrolling platform because of this and kind of made me wish it was a 3D game I could explore. This is the most memorable and enjoyable part of the game for me.
I really didn't like the story so much - very generic "find your family after zombie apocalypse" one and the ending annoyed me. There is an alternate ending which I read about but the one in this game.
There's hidden secrets and such you need to find in the game so if you miss some the idea is you go through again thus adding replay value but these secrets didn't really add any new experiences to the game besides adding backstory. So I've played it once and that's enough.
I don't regret buying and playing through but I don't think I'll replay for a long while.

Deadlight is a fun, beautiful, Zombie-filled side scroller that will keep you busy for a couple hours. to get it out of the way, yes, this was a console game and there where a few hiccups frome time to time. I would sometimes get sound missing in a few cutscenes and the controls did seem a bit fauilty at times, but that wasn't enough to ruin the game for me. By far the best thing about this game is just how well done and amzing the levels look. They did an excellent job of making you feel like you where in an open environment when you where outside despite the fact that you could only go left or right. the lighting was very well done and the color pallette used in this game really capture a certain atmosphere. Most of the game is comprised of parkour style running, trial and error puzzles, and zombie encounters(that for the most part you're better off trying to outsmart and avoid). If you want a zombie-slaying game, this won't be it. You spend a lot of time without a weapon and during these times, the game teaches you that you don't a;ways have to fight the dead to beat them. The story is alright but a sort of cliche with a nice twist. If what you're looking for is a fun, beautiful side scroller to burn some time with, then I suggest you give it a try
7/10

The color use amongst the shadows of the world gives a good visual appeal, and the effects of the world around the player seems real for the decay and fragility of what would be left standing so far after Z-day.  Sound was good, except for the comic cutscenes, but that was probably an issue on my end of the game.  In short, I would like to see a sequel, as it could improve upon this game in some aspects.
